name: herd init
description: Stand up herdkit in a project: scout (detects lang node/python/go/rust/java), INTENT-FIRST project-archetype interview (HERD-409: pick code/research-lab/docs from templates/archetypes.tsv — code defers to scout's detected lang, research-lab/docs always seed the markdown/link/template-conformance healthcheck.docs.sh and skip the app-preview question), INTENT-FIRST posture interview (HERD-141: pick a named working style from templates/postures.tsv — solo-auto/team-approve/gated-push/observe-only/custom-steps/full-auto/docs-lab — and render its KEY=VALUE bundle into .herd/config; advanced path keeps per-key override), write .herd/config (including PROJECT_ARCHETYPE), seed .herd/healthcheck.project.sh from the template matching the detected stack (or the chosen archetype), render coordinator skill. Non-interactive init stays byte-identical seeded-default (archetype=code). `--archetype <name>` / `--posture <name>` (HERD-410) name a templates/archetypes.tsv / templates/postures.tsv row directly, validated up front and applied non-interactively — skips the corresponding interview even under a tty; the scripted caller this exists for is `herd fleet new`
when_to_surface: Onboarding a new project to the herd workflow for the first time; pass --archetype/--posture when scripting init (e.g. from 'herd fleet new') so a non-interactive run still picks a real archetype/posture instead of the code-shaped default

name: herd adopt [path]
description: Localize a CLONED herd project on THIS machine (HERD-520) — the one command a collaborator runs after `git clone`. A herd project COMMITS .herd/config, so a clone inherits the AUTHOR's absolute PROJECT_ROOT/WORKTREES_DIR and every lane, watcher lock and worktree path resolves into someone else's home dir. `herd adopt [path]` (default: cwd) is NON-INTERACTIVE and idempotent: it derives PROJECT_ROOT from the target's physical path (pwd -P) and WORKTREES_DIR as the sibling pool <PROJECT_ROOT>-trees, writes BOTH through the VALIDATED machine-scope setter (`herd config set --local`, under HERD_INIT_DEFER_APPLY=1 so a watcher-affecting key never drives a reload against a control room that does not exist yet) into the gitignored .herd/config.local overlay — the committed baseline is NEVER touched — creates the worktree pool, guarantees the overlay is git-ignored via .git/info/exclude (checkout-local, so the clone is never dirtied), runs the dependency doctor, and prints the next steps (herd render, herd reload). Re-running on an already-localized project prints a no-op report and changes nothing; a linked git worktree is REFUSED before any write
when_to_surface: Right after `git clone`ing a herd project you did not create (or after moving/renaming a project's directory) — run `herd adopt` in the clone root, then `herd render` + `herd reload`. Not for a fresh project: use `herd init` for that

name: herd doctor
description: One-pass dependency doctor: verify git, gh (+auth), claude, python3, herdr (+JSON contract) are present and working and that python3 can emit UTF-8 (Windows cp1252 guard, issue #31); reports every problem at once with per-platform install hints; soft deps (glow, shellcheck, bats) warn only; exits non-zero on any missing/broken hard dep. `herd doctor --posture` (HERD-154) adds a deterministic, no-LLM, report-only config-posture lint: it flags incoherent knob combos (a lever superseded/ignored by another key, each with a fix hint — e.g. legacy WATCHER_AUTOMERGE set alongside MERGE_POLICY) and reports whether the operator's effective posture is exercised by the posture-matrix sim (templates/postures.tsv); advisory, always exits 0
when_to_surface: When a herd command misbehaves, a fresh or Windows environment needs verifying, or the control room came up partially broken — run herd doctor to self-diagnose missing/broken dependencies in one pass; run herd doctor --posture to lint a custom .herd/config for incoherent or never-exercised knob combinations

name: herd upgrade
description: Bump HERD_VERSION and re-render the coordinator skill preserving all .herd/config answers
when_to_surface: After a herdkit engine update or when the coordinator template changes

name: herd render
description: Re-render only the coordinator skill from the current .herd/config without bumping version
when_to_surface: When only the template changed and no version bump is needed

name: herd map
description: Render docs/control-room-map.md — the operator-facing ONE-PAGE decision graph of how a change ships end-to-end: coordinator → lanes (feature/quick) → builder worktree → watcher gates (healthcheck + review) → verdict branches (PASS/BLOCK/refix) → merge policy → post-merge reconcile, plus bug routing (APP vs HERD-ENGINE), the async lanes (scribe/research), and the safety rails. The FLOW complement to `herd codemap` (the FILE map) and docs/driver-abstraction.md (the one runtime seam). Read-only + fail-soft: renders the committed doc with glow (themed) when available, else cat; distinct from codemap, which regenerates a scanned artifact rather than rendering a hand-authored one
when_to_surface: When an operator or new builder wants to orient on the whole ship-a-change pipeline in one page — the coordinator/lane/gate/verdict/merge/reconcile flow and where a bug or async task routes — instead of piecing it together from the code or the file map

name: herd codemap
description: Regenerate docs/codemap.md — a bash-native, DETERMINISTIC map of the herdkit engine tree scanned by scripts/herd/codemap.sh: module roles (bin/herd, each scripts/herd/*.sh, templates/ render surface, one line each from the file top comment), who-sources-whom (the static .-source edges between shell files), and config-key → consumer wiring (which script reads each kind=config key in this manifest). No timestamps/absolute paths, stable sort order, rewrites the file only when content changes (idempotent); prints what changed or 'up to date'
when_to_surface: When a coordinator/builder wants a compact, refreshable map of the codebase to load as context instead of re-exploring the repo each session, or after adding/renaming an engine script/config key so the committed map reflects the new tree

name: herd symbol-index
description: Regenerate docs/symbol-index.md — a bash-native, DETERMINISTIC function-level def→caller index of the herdkit engine tree scanned by scripts/herd/symbol-index.sh: for every shell function defined under bin/herd and scripts/herd/** (incl. backends/), its definition site(s) (file:line) and every CROSS-FILE call site. The function-level companion to `herd codemap` (which maps the same tree at FILE level): builders answer "who calls _backend_update_state" in one lookup instead of a grep-and-read session, and the coordinator sharpens its pre-spawn overlap read from file-level to symbol-level. No timestamps/absolute paths, stable sort order, rewrites the file only when content changes (idempotent); prints what changed or 'up to date'. HONEST SCOPE: a heuristic token scan, not a parser — it cannot bind a call to a specific same-named def, and command-position call detection can miss/over-count around dynamic dispatch, heredocs, strings, and inline comments (limits spelled out in the artifact header)
when_to_surface: When a coordinator/builder wants a def→caller map to jump straight to a function's definition or find its cross-file callers without a grep session, or after adding/renaming/moving an engine function so the committed index reflects the new symbol graph

name: herd agents <list|new|show|install|verify>
description: The SPECIALIST AGENT ROSTER (HERD-667, epic HERD-666): committed per-project agent definitions (.herd/agents/<name>.md — frontmatter name/description/sentinel, body = the system prompt) plus the driver-aware machinery that gets one in front of a builder. `list` prints the roster with the ACTIVE driver's definition mode, lookup path and per-entry CACHED resolution verdict (a read — it never spawns); `new <name>` scaffolds a definition from templates/agent-definition.md.tmpl with a unique verification sentinel already in it; `show <name>` prints one; `install` publishes the committed source to the active driver's REAL lookup path (load-bearing on a runtime that only reads USER scope — verified: grok honors ~/.grok/agents/ and ignores a repo-local copy — and a clean no-op where nothing needs publishing); `verify [<name>]` is the EMPIRICAL proof: it spawns a one-shot through DRIVER_AGENT_ONESHOT_EXEC with the definition selected (by the driver's DRIVER_AGENT_SELECT_FLAG, or by injecting the body where the runtime has no by-name selector — whichever mechanism the LANE would use), asserts a sentinel that exists ONLY in that definition comes back, AND runs a NEGATIVE CONTROL with a name that cannot exist, because a runtime that silently ignores an unknown name (grok does) makes a one-sided probe worthless. Verdicts — ok / unresolved / indeterminate / no-sentinel / unverified — cache by (driver, definition sha) in the worktree pool, so editing a definition invalidates its own verdict and `herd doctor` can report roster state without spawning (`herd doctor --probe` re-runs it live). Select an agent for a build with HERD_AGENT=<name> on the lanes. SHIP-DORMANT and never blocking: no roster = byte-inert, HERD_AGENT unset = byte-identical spawn argv and task spec, and an unresolved name warns LOUDLY but still spawns
when_to_surface: After authoring or editing an agent definition (verify, then install where the runtime needs it), when picking which specialist to spawn an item with (list), or when a builder behaved like a plain agent despite HERD_AGENT being set — `verify` is the one check that can tell a resolved definition from a silently ignored one

name: herd ledger <set|get|list|rm|compact|path>
description: The COORDINATOR PROGRESS LEDGER (HERD-103): durable, cross-session coordinator-side state keyed by tracker id so a coordinator or a SECOND operator resumes with an accurate picture instead of re-deriving it from herdr/gh/backlog every session. Records per work item the coordinator facts nothing else holds: what was spawned (slug/worktree/PR/lane), sequencing decisions (seq/blocked-on notes), a planned marker for not-yet-spawned work, and a free-form status/note. APPEND-OR-UPDATE: `set <id> [k v]...` appends an update (later fields override earlier, so an update is just another line); `get <id> [--json]` folds to the item's current state; `list [--json] [--planned]` lists live items; `rm <id>` tombstones one out; `compact` folds history to one line per live item; `path` prints the file. Coordinator-side ONLY — NOT a watcher gate, nothing merges on it; it complements the engine journal (gate forensics) with the coordinator's editable plan+progress memory. Local + NEVER committed (WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/ledger.jsonl, gitignored); ZERO-SECRET by contract. Default-dormant: unused, no file exists and behavior is byte-identical
when_to_surface: At session start to reload prior coordinator state (list/get) and after each spawn or sequencing/planning decision to record it (set), so the picture survives a context reset or hand-off to another operator; never for watcher/gate decisions — it carries no gate authority

name: herd advise "<question>" [context…]
description: MID-FLIGHT strong-model ADVISOR (HERD-101): a builder pulls a ONE-SHOT second opinion on a hard decision from a strong advisor model (MODEL_ADVISE, default the MODEL_FEATURE/Opus tier) WITHOUT escalating its whole lane's tier, and reads the advice on stdout. Extra positional args after the question — and, when stdin is not a tty, piped stdin — are appended verbatim as context. No agent, no herdr tab, no repo mutation, no journal write: a pure one-shot query. ADDITIVE + FAIL-SOFT: an absent advisor model or a failed/empty model call degrades to a clear one-line 'unavailable' message on stdout and exit 0, never a hard error; a builder that never calls it sees byte-identical behavior
when_to_surface: When a builder on a cheaper tier hits ONE genuinely hard judgment call (an API shape, a tricky invariant, a which-design-is-safer fork) and wants a strong model's read without re-spawning the whole lane on Opus — it is a pull the builder chooses, not a push

name: herd note "<finding>"
description: Builder findings JOURNAL (HERD-202): a builder mid-build files a load-bearing finding (`herd note "<finding>"`) so the coordinator sees it in the watch stream WITHOUT a human clipboard paste. Journals a builder_note event (component=builder, slug from HERD_SLUG or the worktree basename, free text truncated ~300 chars) via journal_append into .herd/journal.jsonl. HERD-298: when the finding EXCEEDS the ~300-char cap, the full flattened text is spilled to a sidecar (WORKTREES_DIR/.builder-notes-full/<epoch>-<slug>.txt) in the shared worktree pool and its path is recorded on the event as note_full, so no tail is lost — fail-soft (a sidecar-write failure degrades to today's capped-only behavior and never blocks the note; a sub-cap note spills nothing and its journal line stays byte-identical). The watcher drains NEW builder_note rows each tick (byte cursor; first scan pins to EOF so restarts never re-flood), fires one herd_driver_notify per note, and renders a needs-you-adjacent 'builder notes' console section. The lane task-spec preamble (herd-quick.sh + herd-feature.sh) instructs builders to file notable findings this way. Ship-dormant: no behavior change unless a builder calls it; an empty ledger leaves the console byte-identical
when_to_surface: When a builder discovers a mid-build finding the coordinator should know about (stale cache, unwired test, env-not-code hold) — call `herd note` instead of relying on a human to paste the pane transcript

name: herd notes [list|ack <n|all>]
description: Bounded builder-notes console (HERD-243): `herd notes` lists the builder notes currently taking console space (newest first, numbered, aged-out and already-acked rows omitted — the SAME visibility decision the watcher renders, via the shared scripts/herd/console-section.sh); `herd notes show <n>` prints one note's FULL finding (HERD-298: resolves the note's builder_note event by ts+slug+capped-text and prints the note_full sidecar an over-cap note spilled, so the dropped tail is recoverable — a sub-cap note prints its capped row text unchanged); `herd notes ack <n>` / `herd notes ack all` records the exact ledger line in an ack sidecar (.agent-watch-builder-notes-acked) so the note leaves the DISPLAY on the watcher's next tick. HERD-640 (M4, Phase 3 of HERD-625) adds `herd notes route <n> <artifact>` — artifact `item:<ref>` | `pr:<num>`, an explicit prefix beating the bare-number inference — which acks NOTHING now: it records "<epoch>\tkind\tartifact\t<the note's verbatim ledger line>" in .agent-watch-builder-notes-routes, and the watcher (_scan_note_routes) enqueues a `note-ack` intent into the shared intent queue the moment that artifact demonstrably EXISTS (the item resolves through the active backend; the PR shows merged via the same reap-ledger-then-gh predicate a HERD-94 dependency hold uses), which the drain then executes into this same ack sidecar. The split is the doc's §1.4: ROUTING stays coordinator judgment, only the ACK leaves the seat — a note routed as 'dismiss' has no artifact, gets no row, and is never auto-acked. Gated by INTENT_QUEUE like every other intent tenant. Display-only and fail-soft: the journal keeps every note (`herd log` still shows it), no tracker state is touched. Unacked calm notes age out of the display on their own after CONSOLE_ROW_RETENTION (2h); both the notes ledger and the ack sidecar are trimmed on write to the last 20 rows
when_to_surface: After handling a builder note surfaced on the watcher console — ack it so the 'builder notes' section shows only what still needs the operator, instead of an append-only wall that trains everyone to ignore it

name: herd tracker-heals [list|ack <n|all>]
description: The herd-notes-style operator clear path for the "tracker healed" console section (HERD-613 LEG 3): `herd tracker-heals` lists the heal-ledger rows (.agent-watch-tracker-heals, written by tracker-state-sweep.sh) currently taking console space — newest first, numbered, aged-out/superseded/already-acked rows omitted, via the SAME visibility rule the watcher renders through (herd_console_visible_lines_tracker, console-section.sh); `herd tracker-heals ack <n>` / `ack all` records the exact ledger line in an ack sidecar (.agent-watch-tracker-heals-acked) so the row leaves the DISPLAY immediately. A `failed`/`escalated` row is LOUD (never ages out on its own) — before this command the only way off the console was a fresh `healed` row for the same ref superseding it, which a ref that can never resolve (a shape-invalid `Refs:` value — pr-ref.sh's HERD-613 shape guard) can never produce. tracker-state-sweep.sh's own auto-retire leg does the SAME ack automatically for an escalated row whose ref fails the shape guard; this command is the manual path for everything else. Display-only and fail-soft: the ledger and journal are untouched
when_to_surface: After investigating an ESCALATED or stuck-FAILED row on the "tracker healed" console section that will never self-clear (a ref the auto-retire leg did not already catch) — ack it so the section shows only what still needs attention

name: herd intents [list|ack <n|all>]
description: The herd-notes-style operator clear path for the "spawn intents" console section (HERD-630, Phase 1 of HERD-625): under INTENT_QUEUE=on the watcher's spawn-queue drain REFUSES to launch an intent that aged past INTENT_TTL — it retires the intent to a terminal `escalated` state and writes one row to .agent-watch-intent-escalations, rendered as a LOUD needs-you row that never ages out on its own (only a coordinator can decide whether to re-ground and re-publish the plan). `herd intents` lists the rows currently taking console space — newest first, numbered, already-acked/retired rows omitted, via the SAME visibility rule the watcher renders through (herd_console_visible_lines + herd_console_classify_intent_escalation, console-section.sh); `herd intents ack <n>` / `ack all` records the exact ledger line in an ack sidecar (.agent-watch-intent-escalations-acked) so the row leaves the DISPLAY immediately. agent-watch.sh's own age-to-retired sweep (_intent_escalations_retire) does the SAME ack automatically once a row is past CONSOLE_ROW_RETENTION, journaling spawn_intent_retired with the intent's ref so the evidence outlives the console; this command is the immediate path for a row an operator has already handled. Shipped in the SAME slice as the escalation itself, per the HERD-613 LEG 3 lesson that an escalation surface without a clearing surface is a permanent-red generator. Display-only and fail-soft: the ledger and journal are untouched
when_to_surface: After re-grounding an ESCALATED spawn intent on the "spawn intents" console section (re-queued what still matters via HERD_SPAWN_PRIO=<n> scripts/herd/spawn.sh, or decided the plan is dead) — ack it so the section shows only what still needs a coordinator

name: herd queue [list|plan]
description: THE PUBLISHED PLAN surface (HERD-642, Phase 5 of HERD-625; design doc docs/spikes/coordinator-work-queue.md §4.4 supersede-over-delete + §6 Phase 5). Phases 1-4 externalized spawn SELECTION one intent at a time, so a coordinator's ranked candidate list still lived only in a conversation and countermanding it meant cancelling N intents by id. This command makes the LIST the unit. `herd queue plan [--file <path>|-]` reads one TAB-separated candidate per line (<slug> <lane quick|feature> <tracker ref or -> <after dep or -> <task text>), TOP CANDIDATE FIRST — line order IS the priority, stamped into bands 10/20/30… so work can be slotted between them later — validates EVERY line before publishing any of it, enqueues each candidate through the shipped scripts/herd/spawn.sh (so the TRACKED_SPAWNS gate, ref threading, the .prio band and the M3 marker-publish intent all behave exactly as a hand-run enqueue — no parallel implementation), stamps them all with one opaque GENERATION id, and then makes that generation live in ONE atomic rename of the queue's .gen pointer: the new plan and the old one are never both claimable, and never neither. A mid-publish failure retires what it staged and leaves the PREVIOUS plan live, loudly. `herd queue list` prints the live generation's still-pending candidates in DRAIN order with priority band, ref and blocker — the same rows the watch pane's 'planned work' section renders, through the same reader (iq_plan_rows, intent-queue.sh), so the CLI and the pane can never disagree. NO NEW CONFIG KEY: publishing always works, but a generation (like a priority band) is only CONSULTED under INTENT_QUEUE, and both surfaces say so when the lever is off. `queue plan` is a control-room ACTUATOR (context-guard.sh refuses it from a builder worktree); `queue list` is a read and stays allowed everywhere.
when_to_surface: Publishing the ranked candidate list so mechanical spawn SELECTION survives a coordinator pause (herd queue plan), re-publishing it after changing your mind (one write supersedes the whole previous generation — never N per-intent cancels), or reading what another seat's pool intends to build next instead of re-deriving it from the backlog (herd queue list)

name: herd reload
description: Rebuild the control room minus the coordinator: stop + relaunch the watcher with pane visibility verified, ensure the pinned backlog pane, re-render the coordinator skill; prints a per-component summary and effective MERGE_POLICY; never closes the coordinator tab/agent
when_to_surface: When .herd/config changes need to take effect, the watcher or backlog pane died or went invisible, or duplicate watchers must be cleared — safe to run from inside the coordinator

name: herd pane <watch|backlog|coordinator|agents>
description: Restart ONE control-room pane in place without a full reload: watch stops + reruns the watcher in its registered pane (recreated below the coordinator if gone); backlog reruns the backlog viewer in its pane, interrupting a live viewer safely first; coordinator relaunches the coordinator agent pane (KILLS the live claude session, so it requires a typed 'yes' or --yes); agents (HERD-668) reruns the read-only AGENTS_PANE pane beside the watch pane (recreated if gone) — a clean no-op, never destructive, when AGENTS_PANE=off. Each rewrites .herd-panes from observed state and prints a per-component outcome; refuses when no project .herd/config resolves
when_to_surface: When just one pane died or went stale (watcher stopped, backlog viewer stuck, coordinator session needs a fresh start, agents pane went stale) and a full 'herd reload' is more than needed — surgically restart that single pane; use 'herd reload' instead when the whole control room needs rebuilding

name: herd watcher-resurrect
description: External-cadence WATCHER RESURRECTION probe (HERD-489): meant to be driven by an operator cron/launchd job, never by the watcher's own tick loop — code the watcher executes cannot run once the watcher itself is fully dead (the gap a 5-hour outage on 2026-08-02 exposed; WATCHER_SELF_RESTART/WATCHER_SINGLETON_RECONCILE/COORDINATOR_WATCHDOG are all watcher-tick code and are therefore inert against that exact failure). Gated by WATCHER_RESURRECT (default off, ship-dormant): off is a byte-inert no-op even when invoked. On, each run classifies this project's watcher through the shared watcher-exempt.sh seam (watcher_singleton_verdict — the same argv0 + lockfile/flock reconciled check `herd status` and WATCHER_SINGLETON_RECONCILE use) and acts ONLY on a CONFIRMED zero-mains verdict (state NONE); every other state (a live main, a drifted lock, a duplicate, a self-restart handoff) is left STRICTLY alone, so a live watcher is never doubled. On NONE it journals watcher_resurrect_detected, relaunches via the VERIFIED stop/start seam `herd reload` (issue #579, never a home-grown kill/spawn), then journals watcher_resurrected on a confirmed live pid or watcher_resurrect_failed (exit 1) otherwise
when_to_surface: Wire a cron/launchd job to run this on a schedule (e.g. every 5-15 min) as the one revival path that survives the watcher process itself being gone — the exact failure every in-process watchdog lever cannot reach; turn WATCHER_RESURRECT on first (default off)

name: herd update [--force]
description: Pull the herdkit engine (git pull --ff-only in HERDKIT_HOME), show the incoming delta, re-render the coordinator skill preserving .herd/config answers, and reload the workspace in one step; refuses if the engine checkout is dirty or builders are mid-flight (--force overrides both guards)
when_to_surface: When a fix has landed upstream in herdkit and you need to bring it in, or when the user asks 'how do I get the latest engine fix' — answer: run herd update

name: herd agent-update [--dry-run]
description: SAFELY update the AGENT RUNTIME the active driver points at (claude — or, via the driver seam, codex/grok), INSIDE the engine instead of a hand-run OS job. Opt-in via AGENT_UPDATE: off (default) is a HARD no-op (no probe, no exec, no xattr), byte-identical to before. When on it resolves the runtime binary + installer package names from the active driver's DRIVER_AGENT_BINARY/_NPM_PKG/_BREW_PKG/_NATIVE_UPDATE bindings, DETECTS the installer (brew formula|cask / npm global / native), runs the update, then STRIPS com.apple.quarantine from the RESOLVED binary on macOS — the issue #137 footgun where a `brew upgrade --cask` leaves the new binary quarantined so every new exec hangs in _dyld_start and spawned agents sit idle with blank panes. Distinct from `herd update` (which pulls the herdkit ENGINE, not the runtime). DRIVER-AWARE + FAIL-SOFT (a missing runtime or a failed installer command warns, never aborts); --dry-run prints every command it would run (installer + xattr) without executing
when_to_surface: When you want the engine to keep the agent runtime current instead of a hand-run brew/npm/native upgrade — especially on macOS, where a cask upgrade's quarantine flag silently wedges every spawned agent; enable with AGENT_UPDATE=on and preview with `herd agent-update --dry-run`

name: herd log [--pr N] [--tail]
description: Page the append-only engine journal (.herd/journal.jsonl): one readable line per gate event (review dispatch, verdict + provenance, healthcheck attempt/outcome, refix bounce, merge, reap, reload, infra death). --pr N filters to a single PR; --tail follows live
when_to_surface: When you want the raw chronological event stream, to watch gate activity live, or to see every recorded event for one PR before drilling in with herd why

name: herd why <pr#>
description: Summarize ONE PR's full gate history from the journal, chronologically: every dispatch, verdict (with reviewer/gate_default/infra provenance), healthcheck attempt + outcome, auto-refix bounce + wake result, and the merge/reap — the first post-mortem tool for 'what happened to this PR'
when_to_surface: FIRST tool to run when the user asks what happened to a PR, why a PR is stuck, or why a gate/review/merge failed — grounds the answer in recorded events instead of process archaeology

name: herd approve [<pr#|slug>] [--sha <sha>]
description: The APPROVAL front door under MERGE_POLICY=approve (HERD-200) — a first-class alias for scripts/herd/herd-approve.sh, which stays the single source of truth for the approval / override / push-hold / step-hold ledgers (bin/herd delegates verbatim, duplicating no logic). `herd approve <pr#>` approves the sha currently held for a gate-passed PR (--sha <sha> pins the approval to the commit the operator reviewed and REFUSES if a newer push superseded it); `herd approve <slug>` releases a pre-push (PUSH_GATE=human) or pipeline-step hold and resumes it; `herd approve list` (the default with no args) shows everything awaiting approval with its review verdict and any HUMAN-VERIFY steps; `herd approve why <pr#>` prints the verdict + block reason; `herd approve override <pr#>` records a human override of a cached BLOCK. A first arg that is not one of list/approve/why/override is treated as the argument of `approve`
when_to_surface: When a PR or builder is HELD awaiting a human — approve it, inspect why it is blocked, or override a cached BLOCK — without remembering the engine-script path; run `herd approve list` first to see what is waiting, then `herd approve <pr#>` to release it

name: herd status
description: One-shot READ-ONLY control-room health snapshot for THIS project (deterministic, no LLM, no mutation): (a) is the watcher alive? via the herd-watch-<workspace> argv0 marker / pid lock; (b) in-flight builders from herdr agent list joined to this project's worktrees, classified building/done/idle and flagged DEAD when a worktree has no live agent + no open PR + no commits (a small read-only replica of the watcher's dead signature); (c) open PRs + gate state (mergeable/mergeStateStatus + last review/health verdict from the watcher's ledgers + GitHub reviewDecision); (d) backlog open/in-progress counts; (e) HERD-492: 'NOTES <n> unacked (newest: <slug> <age>)' — the builder notes (`herd note`) still awaiting an ack, read through the SAME ack-aware console-section.sh reader `herd notes` and the watcher console use, so a note nobody has drained surfaces on the one-shot pulse every coordinator runs instead of only on a live console; INFORMATIONAL (never flips the exit code) and SILENT at zero, so a drained control room is byte-identical. Exits NON-ZERO when something needs attention (DEAD builder, CONFLICTING PR, review-blocked PR), 0 when healthy
when_to_surface: When you (or a cron/dashboard) want a fast, greppable 'is this control room healthy right now?' answer for one project without opening the live TUI — surfaces dead builders, conflicting or review-blocked PRs, and whether the watcher is even running; the single-project analogue of 'herd fleet status'

name: herd sweep
description: ONE-COMMAND CONTROL-ROOM CLEANUP (HERD-191): runs every reaper the engine owns, on demand, composing the shipped helpers rather than reimplementing them (sweep.sh loads agent-watch.sh via AGENT_WATCH_LIB=1). Seven legs: (1) WORKTREES — sha-anchored reap of merged/closed-PR worktrees (a PR whose headRefOid equals the tree's HEAD; regenerable dirt like .DS_Store/__pycache__ is tolerated), but a merged/closed tree whose builder is still WORKING (HERD-356) is DEFERRED not reaped (⏸️, its own count — clears itself when the agent goes idle), plus unowned tmp/detached scratch trees that carry ZERO unique commits (a detached HEAD's commits are reachable from no branch ref, so removing the worktree destroys them irrecoverably — such a tree is FLAGGED, never reaped); (2) TABS — stale engine tabs, registry-allowlisted + workspace-scoped, never another project's; (3) MARKERS — dead-pid inflight markers (and past-deadline live workers, both narrated in the plan) via HERD-185's restart-safe corpse sweep, now serialized under an atomic claim so a CLI sweep and the live watcher tick cannot double-charge a PR's review-retry budget or the global infra breaker; (4) PROCESSES — orphaned (ppid=1) bats/healthcheck trees attributed to THIS project by path-boundary match, killed by process group (pgid and start-time both captured at LISTING and re-verified against the live process immediately before the signal; a mismatch degrades to a single-pid kill or refuses outright), listed before they die; a live inflight marker's worker is exempt (a backgrounded gate worker is ppid=1 but still collectable), and duplicate argv0-tagged watchers are reported; (5) WATCHER — restart the watcher pane via cmd_pane_watch (the single watcher-killing code path, which also reaps the duplicates) then verify it survives one tick; (6) TRACKER LINKAGE (HERD-267) — for a merged PR whose `Refs:` line names no tracker item, enqueue ONE search-first retroactive-linkage request into the backlog queue (advisory only, never writes the tracker); (7) ONCE-GUARD MARKERS — the .live-noted-<kind>-<pr>-<sha> / .live-posted-<kind>-<pr>-<sha> once-per-(pr,sha,kind) guard files pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's LiveState.once/.posted write (a permanent record with no pid and no age, so leg 3's liveness-based marker sweep never touches it), reaped once a PR is PROVABLY MERGED or CLOSED via the SAME gh pr view proof leg 1 uses — an OPEN PR or an unreachable gh leaves every marker untouched. SAFETY: anything not PROVABLY disposable — a worktree with real dirt, ANY tree (closed-PR branch or detached scratch HEAD) carrying commits that exist nowhere else, or a once-guard marker for a PR whose state cannot be confirmed — is FLAGGED WITH EVIDENCE (legs 1) or simply left untouched (leg 7), and NEVER deleted, in any mode. --dry-run prints the full plan and touches nothing; --no-restart skips leg 5. Every action is journaled
when_to_surface: After a watcher crash, an overnight merge burst, or any session that left debris — stale tabs, worktrees whose PR merged hours ago, inflight-marker corpses holding a gate slot, orphaned bats/healthcheck trees. Run 'herd sweep --dry-run' first to read the plan, then 'herd sweep' to execute. The watcher also detects the same debris on its own cadence and renders a '🧹 sweep recommended' row (see SWEEP_AUTO)

name: herd cost [--pr N]
description: Aggregate the engine journal's token/cost events (measured per builder and per in-worktree review at merge time, deduped by message id and priced against the perishable model→$ table): per-PR cost, cost-per-merged-PR, and running totals by component and model; --pr N drills into one PR's cost lines. READ-ONLY measurement precursor to the efficiency program — never changes any gate
when_to_surface: When the user asks how many tokens or how much $ a builder/review/PR cost, wants cost-per-merged-PR, or is scoping the flow-audit / efficiency levers and needs the measured spend instead of a guess

name: herd stats [--today|--since <date>|--pr N]
description: A shepherd's digest CARD: a compact, DETERMINISTIC (zero-LLM) rollup of a window of the engine journal (.herd/journal.jsonl), same reader pattern as herd cost. Aggregates PRs merged (a 🐑 each), review verdicts grouped by value AND provenance (reviewer/gate_default/infra), refix bounces, limit park (limit_detected) / resume (limit_resume_result), reaps, and recorded cost. No filter = all time; --today and --since <date> bound by the ISO ts (string compare, lexical); --pr N scopes to one PR; filters compose (AND). Fail-soft: an empty or missing journal prints an all-zeros card, never an error; no LLM, no mutation
when_to_surface: When you want a fast throughput+friction snapshot of the herd over a window — how many PRs shipped today, how the review verdicts split and where they came from, how much refix/limit/reap churn happened, and the cost — without reading the raw stream (herd log) or drilling one PR (herd why)

name: herd changelog [generate|tag <ver>]
description: Journal-driven CHANGELOG + release-tag helper (HERD-256 / HERD-168 part 2/3): `herd changelog generate` reads merge events from .herd/journal.jsonl (+ rotated archives) and conventional-commit subjects (git log on the merge sha / PR-citing subjects; optional HERD_CHANGELOG_SUBJECTS test seam), then emits/updates the ## [Unreleased] section of CHANGELOG.md grouped Keep-a-Changelog-style by conventional-commit type — DETERMINISTIC, no LLM. `herd changelog tag <ver>` promotes [Unreleased] → [ver] - date and creates a local annotated git tag (does NOT commit, push, or publish). Ship-dormant / read-mostly: never auto-run by the watcher; operator or release runbook invokes it. See docs/releasing.md
when_to_surface: When cutting an OSS release notes section from the engine journal, refreshing CHANGELOG.md after a stretch of merges, or preparing a local version tag before the HUMAN-VERIFY publish steps (GitHub release / Homebrew / npm)

name: herd triage [run|report]
description: OSS auto-triage (HERD-255 / HERD-168 part 1/3): `herd triage run` lists open issues on HERD_REPO (gh issue list), enqueues one research-lane request per NEW issue to CLASSIFY (bug/feature/question/duplicate) and DRAFT a suggested reply/labels, then writes a ranked shortlist (+ operator-inbox pointer) under $WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/oss-triage/ for the coordinator. `herd triage report` prints the current shortlist. Opt-in via OSS_TRIAGE=on (default off → byte-inert: no gh, no research, no files). NEVER auto-posts — no issue comment/close/label; drafts for human approval only. FAIL-SOFT (missing HERD_REPO / gh error → empty shortlist). Reuses research.sh + research-get.sh; test seams HERD_OSS_RESEARCH_SH / HERD_OSS_TRIAGE_DIR
when_to_surface: When an OSS project wants auto-classification + draft replies for incoming GitHub issues without occupying the coordinator context window — enable OSS_TRIAGE=on and run `herd triage`; review the shortlist before any human posts

name: herd backlog
description: List open work items via the active SCRIBE_BACKEND (file/github/linear) in a uniform line shape; subcommands: --rich (state+desc TSV), --closed (HERD-490: closed/completed/canceled items via _backend_list_closed — the mirror of the default open-only list, so a "does this already exist?" search can also see a manually-closed duplicate), show <#id>, browse (fzf), and the HERD-52 planned-work markers — queued (list plan-time markers, >24h flagged ADVISORY), queue <#id> [--after <blocker>] (publish 'I'm building this next' so a second operator doesn't grab it), unqueue <#id> (clear it). --closed/queue/unqueue/queued are backend-optional + fail-soft
when_to_surface: Any time the coordinator needs the current open work set regardless of backend, or (queued/queue/unqueue) to check/publish plan-time intent before picking or spawning an item

name: herd backend switch
description: Guided work-tracker backend switch (file|github|linear|jira|changelog): preflights credentials BEFORE any change (linear prompts for the API key on a tty → .herd/secrets chmod 600 + gitignore, then proves it with a live viewer{} round-trip; jira prompts for JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/JIRA_API_TOKEN → .herd/secrets, then proves it with a live /myself round-trip; github checks gh auth), flips SCRIBE_BACKEND via the validated config-set path (inherits the #139 stale-drainer warning + skill re-render), optionally --migrate replays the old backend's open items into the new one (idempotent — already-present titles skipped, '(migrated from …)' provenance suffix), stamps BACKLOG.md with a frozen-archive banner when leaving the file backend, restarts the backlog viewer pane, and journals backend_switched
when_to_surface: When the operator asks to move work tracking between a markdown file, GitHub Issues, Linear, or Jira — run this ONE command instead of hand-editing config/secrets; everything downstream (scribe drainer, herd backlog, watcher mark-shipped, coordinator skill) follows SCRIBE_BACKEND automatically

name: herd report [--to <link>] [--dep] "<symptom>"
description: File a cross-repo issue on HERD_REPO or a peer from .herd/links via --to; deduplicates first. Default is fire-and-forget dispatch; add --dep (requires --to) to ALSO record the filed item as a blocked-on dependency in .herd/deps so dep-watcher tracks it
when_to_surface: When a HERD-ENGINE bug needs to escalate to the herdkit repo or a registered peer; use --dep when this lane cannot proceed until the filed item is resolved

name: herd link <list|--scan>
description: List peer repos registered in .herd/links with their backend and routing target (list); --scan (HERD-384) proposes candidate peer links from the fleet registry (~/.herd/fleet): for every OTHER registered project (self-comparison is symlink-safe — both sides physically resolved via pwd -P) it re-resolves the repo identity from that project's OWN origin remote (same freshness discipline as herd fleet register) and reads its own SCRIBE_BACKEND including a .herd/config.local overlay (falling back to github), then proposes name|repo|backend| unless a link with that name or repo already exists in .herd/links OR collides with another proposal from this same scan; flags any linear/jira proposal with a blank tracker_target (it would otherwise silently route to YOUR OWN team/project). Dry-run by default (prints proposals, writes nothing); --write appends them — terminating the file with a newline first if a hand-edited last line lacks one — creating .herd/links with a header if absent. Idempotent — a second --write recomputes against the now-updated file and finds nothing new. Fail-soft: no fleet registry → a soft note, exit 0
when_to_surface: When reviewing cross-repo filing targets or confirming link names for herd report --to; run --scan after registering peers with herd fleet register to auto-populate .herd/links instead of hand-editing it, --write once the dry-run proposals look right

name: herd depend <link>#<id>
description: Record a WATCHED blocked-on dependency on a peer-repo item (link resolved via .herd/links) as a blocked-on row in .herd/deps; dep-watcher.sh polls it until the upstream item closes, then notifies and un-blocks. Backward-compatible with the row format the watcher already parses
when_to_surface: When a feature cannot ship until a specific upstream item (a peer-repo issue/PR) closes — records the blocker as tracked, watched state rather than fire-and-forget

name: herd deps <list|rm|demote>
description: Inspect and edit recorded dependencies — a dep is editable data, never stuck: list prints each dep with its current upstream state; rm drops one (warns if a blocker is still open); demote reclassifies a blocked-on into a non-blocking watch row (instantly un-blocks the lane while keeping the item on the radar)
when_to_surface: When reviewing what this project is blocked on, dropping a resolved/obsolete dep, or downgrading a hard blocker to a non-blocking watch so the lane can proceed

name: herd config <list|get|set>
description: View/validate/set .herd/config keys with the known-key set + per-key metadata sourced from templates/capabilities.tsv (this manifest); `set` validates BOTH halves — an unknown KEY is refused, and a VALUE outside the key's recorded value_shape domain (a pipe-separated enum, `numeric`, or `glob`) is refused WITH THE VALID SET PRINTED and nothing written (GH #570: SCRIBE_BACKEND=__probe__ was accepted while its domain sat unrecorded). Keys with no domain recorded stay free-form exactly as before, and a MALFORMED domain cell warns and skips validation rather than blocking the write; set edits in place preserving comments then restarts the watcher (watcher-affecting keys) or re-renders the coordinator skill (coordinator-facing keys). HERD-519: that restart is CONDITIONAL and BOUNDED — with no live watcher (the shared watcher-exempt.sh identity) the restart is SKIPPED with a printed note and only the skill is re-rendered (the key still lands; it takes effect when the watcher next starts), and with one alive the reload runs under a wall-clock bound (HERD_CONFIG_RELOAD_TIMEOUT, default 180s; 0 disables) whose expiry WARNS loudly instead of hanging the terminal on a wedged pane socket. `set --local` (HERD-47) routes the write to the gitignored per-user overlay .herd/config.local; `set --shared` (HERD-62) applies a PROJECT-scoped change to the committed baseline AND opens a tiny single-file PR (branch config/<key>, body stating old->new and an optional --reason) so operators who cannot push to the default branch still propagate policy the gated way — others receive it via `git pull` + `herd update`. --shared is refused for machine-scoped keys and is mutually exclusive with --local. Never touches DENY_PATHS or .herd/secrets; masks secret-shaped values
when_to_surface: Anytime to inspect or change a workflow preference post-init (nothing is init-only); use --shared when a PROJECT-scoped policy change (CONTEXT_PROVISION, MERGE_POLICY, CLAIM_REQUIRED, TRACKED_SPAWNS, ...) must reach every operator; the coordinator's Workflow settings menu drives it

name: herd theme <list|preview|set>
description: The active-THEME picker (HERD-145): a thin operator surface over the pluggable-theming seam (scripts/herd/theme.sh) that never re-implements resolution. `list` prints the catalog — every engine BUILT-IN under templates/themes/ (tokyonight, gruvbox, catppuccin, nord) plus every USER theme under .herd/themes/<name>/ — marking the ACTIVE one (current HERD_THEME) and noting any built-in shadowed by a user theme of the same name. `preview [<name>]` renders that theme's palette as color swatches (default: the active theme). `set <name>` validates the name resolves to a COMPLETE theme dir (palette.sh + glow.json, user or built-in) then writes HERD_THEME through the validated `herd config set` path (manifest validation + the watcher restart that repaints every live surface), refusing an unknown/incomplete theme rather than persisting a value that would silently fall back to tokyonight. Fail-soft + NO_COLOR / non-TTY aware: swatches degrade to plain rows
when_to_surface: When switching the herd color theme or browsing available themes: run `herd theme list` to see built-ins + user themes, `herd theme preview <name>` to compare palettes, and `herd theme set <name>` to apply one (a project's own theme drops palette.sh + glow.json into .herd/themes/<name>/ first)

name: herd governance <export|apply>
description: Export/apply a project's GOVERNANCE as a portable, versioned profile (HERD-126). `herd governance export [--file <path>]` writes the governance-scoped .herd/config key subset (every key marked governance in this manifest — merge/gate/PR/attribution/commit policy; secrets and machine-scoped keys NEVER travel) as a commented, versioned profile to <path> or stdout. `herd governance apply <file>` PROPOSES each key interactively (evidence = the profile line, current->proposed) via the VALIDATED `herd config set` — never a blind overwrite; --yes applies all non-interactively (journaled) for automation; declining every key leaves .herd/config untouched. A malformed profile (missing/unknown version marker, an unknown/non-governance/secret/machine key, or a shell-active value) is refused LOUDLY with ZERO partial writes. Profiles are ONE optional governance source among several — apply composes with the interview, `herd init --governance <file>` seeding, and manual `herd config set`; `herd fleet set --profile <file>` propagates a profile across the whole registry
when_to_surface: When you want to capture a project's governance stance (merge policy, push gate, PR flow, commit/attribution conventions) as a portable artifact to review, version-control, seed a fresh install with (herd init --governance <file>), or roll out across several repos (herd fleet set --profile <file>); export it, then apply it elsewhere

name: herd posture <list|show|apply>
description: Move an ALREADY-INITIALISED project onto a CANONICAL OPERATING POSTURE (HERD-466) — the same templates/postures.tsv bundles `herd init --posture` offers at stand-up, now appliable to a live control room. `list` prints every posture + intent; `show <name>` prints its full KEY=VALUE bundle; `apply [--local|--shared] [--yes] [--no-reload] <name>` validates the WHOLE bundle against this manifest FIRST (key known + value_shape admits the value + no secret/DENY_PATHS key + no shell-active char) so a single defect refuses with ZERO writes, prints the full current→new delta against the EFFECTIVE value (.herd/config.local overlay included), applies every key through the validated `herd config set` on the shared governance-apply path, seeds a STEPS_PROFILE steps.tsv when the bundle names one, and then rebuilds a FRESH watcher via `herd reload`. LAYER ROUTING (HERD-469): `--local` forces the whole bundle into the gitignored `.herd/config.local` overlay (the committed baseline stays byte-identical); `--shared` keeps the pre-HERD-469 committed-baseline write and prints explicit commit-or-already-committed messaging so the shared tree is never left silently dirty; with neither flag the layer DEFAULTS to `--local` whenever the write would leave `.herd/config` uncommitted or more than one identity has committed to the repo, and the chosen layer + why is always printed — a running watcher keeps the environment it was STARTED with, so without the rebuild a flipped lever can stay shadowed by the stale exported value and silently never take. All-or-nothing: ONE confirmation for the whole bundle (--yes for automation; refuses non-interactively without it), never a per-key prompt. The `yolo` posture flips every auto lever at once and pairs with the coordinator DRAIN MODE loop
when_to_surface: When you want a live project to hold a named, sim-proven posture instead of a hand-assembled custom combo (`herd doctor --posture` reporting a never-exercised effective posture is the signal); when starting an unattended drain and you want every auto lever on in one atomic step (`herd posture apply --yes yolo`); when you want to read what a posture WOULD change before changing anything (`show`, or the delta `apply` prints before its confirmation)

name: herd fleet new <path> [--archetype X --posture Y --no-remote]
description: One-command project spin-up (HERD-410): replaces the hand-rolled mkdir + git init + gh repo create + herd init + control-room launch + herd fleet register chain a fleet-room operator used to type by hand. Orchestrates, never re-implements: git init (idempotent), delegates to 'herd init' (--archetype/--posture pass straight through when given), ensures .herd/secrets and .herd/config.local are gitignored (never committed, regardless of which init path ran), commits the rendered .herd/ project files (config, healthcheck.project.sh, steps.tsv/links if created, .gitignore, a seeded BACKLOG.md) via a named 'git add' (never -A), 'gh repo create' + push (unless --no-remote; a missing/unauthenticated gh degrades to the same no-remote outcome with a loud warning, never a crash), 'herd fleet register', and journals a fleet_project_created event into the new project's own journal. PRESERVES OPTIONALITY (the bug this item fixes): --archetype/--posture given → passed to 'herd init'; neither flag + a real tty → 'herd init' runs its own interactive interview; neither flag + no tty → defaults (archetype=code, posture=solo-auto) are computed AND PRINTED LOUDLY before delegating, never silently. --repo-name / --public / --alias are secondary flags (herd fleet new --help)
when_to_surface: When spinning up a brand-new non-code (or code) project from the fleet room / coordinator and you want the FULL chain in one command with the archetype/posture choice preserved and visible — instead of hand-rolling mkdir+git init+gh repo create+herd init+register and risking a silent HERD_NONINTERACTIVE default to a code-shaped project

name: herd fleet <register|list|discover|status|digest|inbox|upgrade|reload>
description: DETERMINISTIC (no-LLM) multi-project fan-out over a flat project registry (default ~/.herd/fleet, one line per project: name|path|repo|aliases, the trailing aliases field OPTIONAL and comma-separated): register <path> [--alias <name>]... adds a herd project (read from its .herd/config); repeatable --alias records extra free-text names (e.g. --alias alpha-svc --alias "Alpha Service") that `herd fleet resolve` also matches — a register call with no --alias preserves whatever aliases the row already had, so a plain re-register (e.g. from discover --register) never silently wipes curated aliases; list prints the registry including each project's aliases; discover [--register] <root>... scans roots for .herd/config projects; status prints a read-only per-project rollup (branch, open PR count, watcher alive? via the herd-watch-<workspace> argv0 marker, last .herd/journal.jsonl activity); digest [--since <dur>] aggregates every project's .herd/journal.jsonl over a window (default 24h) into a cross-project standup (per project: shipped/merged, needs-you holds+escalations, blocked BLOCK verdicts, in-flight reviews, gate-failure count) plus a fleet summary line; inbox is the cross-project ATTENTION INBOX — one view of what needs the human RIGHT NOW, joining each project's journal-derived CURRENT state (human-verify/approval holds, review BLOCK verdicts, escalations, CODEERROR health gates; a released hold or merged PR clears itself) with gh's live CONFLICTING PRs, printing each item as PR# · reason · suggested action (herd why <pr> / herd-approve.sh approve <pr> / herd-resolve.sh <slug>) plus a fleet-wide count, a clean project shown as clean; upgrade and reload DELEGATE to each project's own 'herd update'/'herd reload' and collect a per-project outcome table. Read-mostly — never mutates a project's tree beyond what the delegated per-project command already does; a missing/dirty/gh-unavailable project is reported, not fatal
when_to_surface: When managing several herd projects at once — bulk-upgrade or reload every repo, or get one cross-project status board (which watchers are alive, what each is doing, open PRs), a daily digest/standup of what shipped/blocked/is-in-flight, or one attention inbox of what needs you right now (blocked PRs, holds, conflicts, failed gates) across all repos, instead of visiting each control room; P0+P1+P2 of the Master/fleet-coordinator EPIC

name: herd fleet resolve <free text>
description: DETERMINISTIC (no-LLM) NL pre-resolver (HERD-387): matches free text against the fleet registry's project names and --alias values, case-insensitive, with a FIXED precedence — 1) exact name match, 2) alias match, 3) unambiguous PREFIX match (name or alias). The first tier with any hit decides the outcome: exactly one hit resolves (prints the canonical project name on stdout, exit 0); more than one hit at that tier is ambiguous (candidates listed on stderr, exit 2 — it never silently falls through to a looser tier); no hit at any tier exits 1 listing the registered projects. Read-only. templates/fleet-coordinator.md.tmpl's NL dispatch instructions call this FIRST and fall back to the room agent's own judgment only on a non-zero exit, so the skill stays thin and every deterministically-resolvable dispatch skips the LLM entirely
when_to_surface: When the fleet room (or any script) needs to turn a human's free-text project reference ("the alpha one", "svc-alpha") into an exact registered project name before dispatching work — deterministically for the common case, refusing loudly instead of guessing on a genuine tie

name: herd fleet graph [--json]
description: DETERMINISTIC (no-LLM) relationship-graph rollup (HERD-386): registry projects (~/.herd/fleet) are nodes; each project's OWN `.herd/links` and `.herd/deps` are labeled edges — "link" rows from .herd/links, "blocked-on"/"watch" rows from .herd/deps (the exact ref format `herd depend`/dep-watcher.sh already own: <link-name>#<id>; parsed via the same row shapes, never re-invented). Every edge's peer is resolved against the fleet registry — matched by repo identity first (same identity fleet_register/_fleet_repo_slug derive), falling back to a name match — and flagged inline: `registered` (peer is a reachable registered project), `unreachable` (registered but its path/.herd/config is gone), or `unregistered` (no matching registry row at all). Plain-text tree/edge-list output by default (glow-friendly, no new dependencies); `--json` emits {registry, nodes:[{name,path,repo,reachable}], edges:[{from,kind,ref,repo,status,to_project}]} for machine use. Fail-soft: a missing registry/links/deps file yields an empty graph, never an error
when_to_surface: When you want to see how your registered fleet projects relate to each other — which peers are cross-repo LINKED vs a live BLOCKED-ON dependency, and whether a referenced peer is actually registered and reachable in your fleet — instead of opening each project's `.herd/links`/`.herd/deps` by hand; the relationship-graph half of docs/fleet-landscape.md's Q2 gap ("relationship/dependency graph … not visualized/rolled up")

name: herd governance hooks render [--shared]
description: Render SESSION-TIME Claude Code hooks from the governance map's surface==hook rows (HERD-131). Dual-surface enforcement: the same governance rules the merge-time watcher gate enforces ALSO bind at the keyboard as PreToolUse hooks (e.g. block a `git commit` carrying an AI attribution trailer — the session sibling of the ATTRIBUTION_POLICY merge-time lint; warn on a direct `git push` under PUSH_GATE=human). PROPOSE-then-write: each hook is shown and the operator accepts per-hook; accepted entries MERGE into .claude/settings.local.json (default) or .claude/settings.json (--shared), preserving every existing entry. Each generated matcher-group carries a herd-governance marker key so re-render strips ONLY its own prior entries and re-adds the current selection (idempotent). Fail-soft: no map / no hook rows / non-interactive → clean no-op, no file written
when_to_surface: After importing governance from a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (herd init adoption, HERD-119) or setting gates manually — bind the hook-surface rules session-time so a violation is blocked at the keyboard, not only at merge; safe to re-run to refresh

name: fleet.sh
description: Helper library behind 'herd fleet' (sourced by bin/herd): the project-registry reader/writer, per-project config resolver, status rollup (branch/open-PRs/watcher-liveness/last-journal-activity), and the update/reload fan-out that delegates to each project's own herd command
when_to_surface: Internal to 'herd fleet'; not launched directly

name: herd-feature.sh
description: Full feature lane: creates worktree, opens live app preview pane, spawns Claude agent, runs healthcheck before PR
when_to_surface: App-facing changes where a running preview aids development; APP_PREVIEW_CMD must be set

name: herd-quick.sh
description: Lightweight lane: creates worktree, single agent pane, no preview, runs healthcheck before PR
when_to_surface: Trivial or non-app changes: scripts, docs, config, engine fixes; no APP_PREVIEW_CMD required

name: herd-resolve.sh
description: Isolated conflict resolver: merges default branch into worktree, fixes conflicts, verifies, pushes or escalates
when_to_surface: When the watcher surfaces a CONFLICTING PR that cannot auto-resolve

name: herd-approve.sh
description: Approval entry-point for MERGE_POLICY=approve AND per-PR human-verify holds: list gate-passed PRs (printing any declared HUMAN-VERIFY steps) and write sha-keyed approval records
when_to_surface: When MERGE_POLICY=approve, or a PR declared a HUMAN-VERIFY block, and it has passed all gates but needs coordinator sign-off before the watcher merges

name: push-gate.sh
description: PUSH_GATE=human hold helper (HERD-123): a finished builder records a sha-keyed pre-push hold instead of pushing; herd-approve.sh approve <slug> resumes push + PR creation. Sourced by herd-approve.sh (list/approve/resume) and agent-watch.sh (the 'ready · awaiting push approval' console row); run directly by the builder lane (hold)
when_to_surface: Only reached when PUSH_GATE=human; a builder holds here before its first push and a human approves the LOCAL diff to resume

name: governance-hook.sh
description: Session-time governance enforcer (HERD-131): the command rendered into a project's .claude/settings by `herd governance hooks render`. Invoked by Claude Code as a PreToolUse hook — reads the tool payload on stdin, extracts the Bash command, and enforces ONE governance rule at the keyboard (exit 2 = block, exit 0 = allow/warn). Complements the merge-time gate (dual-surface). Targets: pre-commit:no-ai-coauthor (block an AI attribution trailer), pre-push:human-gate (warn under PUSH_GATE=human), pre-action:run-checks, pre-action:format. Unknown target → fail-open
when_to_surface: Not run directly — Claude Code invokes it per the settings.json hook entry the render command writes; run standalone only to pipe-test a rule

name: steps.sh
description: Pipeline steps runner (HERD-132): runs operator-defined stages from .herd/steps.tsv at the post-build | post-healthcheck | pre-merge | post-merge seams — a shell command or a skill:<name> invoked in the builder session. on_fail=block|warn; hold=none|notify|approve (approve reuses the sha-keyed herd-approve ledger). Sourced by herd-feature.sh / herd-quick.sh (builder-seam rule), agent-watch.sh (pre/post-merge seams in do_merge), and herd-approve.sh (list/approve/release a step hold); run directly as a CLI (steps.sh run <seam> | validate | holds). name: triggers.sh
description: Scheduled/triggered runs (HERD-169): a cron-style trigger in .herd/triggers.tsv either ENQUEUEs a workflow (a named backlog-item template or a steps.tsv pipeline named in its task text) onto the EXISTING durable spawn queue via spawn.sh (lane=quick|feature — optionally with a 6th 'agent' column selecting a .herd/agents/<name>.md roster definition via HERD_AGENT, HERD-673), or, lane=mechanical (HERD-673), runs the rendered task text DIRECTLY as a shell command — no worktree, no agent, no PR — for cheap deterministic maintenance (a cache refresh, a report). It never touches the spawn queue internals. DIFF-AGAINST-LAST-RUN: each fire diffs the trigger's input set against a per-trigger snapshot under .herd/trigger-state/ and spawns/execs ONLY the delta; first run (no snapshot) = a loudly-labelled full run; an input-command error is fail-soft (spawns/execs nothing, keeps the snapshot), and a mechanical command's own non-zero exit is fail-soft too (reported + journaled, tick never wedges). Run as a CLI (triggers.sh tick [--now EPOCH] [--force] | fire <name> | validate | list). An absent/empty triggers.tsv is a byte-identical no-op (ships dormant)
when_to_surface: Only reached when .herd/triggers.tsv defines triggers; the tick cadence is an operator cron/scheduler and the schedule column decides which triggers are due — every quick/feature spawn still runs the normal build/healthcheck/review/merge pipeline; mechanical rows are for work that never needs one
