name: scripts/herd/gardener.sh
description: The MAINTENANCE GARDENER (HERD-673, tuned HERD-730): a periodic, ADVISORY doc-drift sweep. `gardener.sh run` reads merge events journaled since its own stored cursor (a byte offset under the worktree pool; an absent, corrupt, or rotated/oversized cursor always re-baselines at the CURRENT journal EOF, never replaying history as archaeology), diffs each merge's changed files against a small SURFACE set (bin/herd, scripts/herd/*.sh, templates/capabilities.tsv, templates/conformance.tsv) and a DOC set (README.md, docs/** except the GENERATED docs/codemap.md and docs/symbol-index.md, templates/*.tmpl, templates/capabilities.tsv itself) — SURFACE touched with no DOC touched in the same merge is real drift, unless the surface file's own diff only touches its leading `#`-comment header block (self-documenting). Every drifted file found in a run is grouped by subsystem (its own directory) into ONE rollup tracker item per run — never one item per file (HERD-730: a per-file design once filed fifty items from a single run) — filed via scribe.sh, gated by a per-signature filing cooldown (HERD_GARDENER_COOLDOWN_SECS, default 7d) so a standing drift is not re-included every run, and bounded by a per-run filing cap (HERD_GARDENER_MAX_FINDINGS, default 20) that truncates LOUDLY in the rollup body and holds the cursor back so the same window is honestly rescanned next run. `--dry-run` previews without filing/cooldown/cursor side effects. FILES, NEVER EDITS: never writes README.md/docs/**/templates/*.tmpl itself. Gated by MAINTENANCE_GARDENER (default off, byte-inert). Scheduled weekly via the docs-gardener agent row in .herd/triggers.tsv (HERD-169)
when_to_surface: Any time MAINTENANCE_GARDENER=on and either the weekly trigger fires or an operator/the docs-gardener specialist wants to preview (--dry-run) or run the doc-drift sweep by hand

name: spawn.sh
description: Enqueue a builder spawn intent (slug + lane=quick|feature + task text) to the durable spawn queue ($WORKTREES_DIR/spawn-queue/) and return instantly with an INTENT_ID. The watcher drains the queue each tick via spawn-step.sh, launching herd-quick.sh or herd-feature.sh bounded by REVIEW_CONCURRENCY + SPAWN_AHEAD — so a coordinator pause never loses a spawn and the pipeline cap is always respected. HERD_SPAWN_AFTER=<slug|pr#> holds the intent until that dependency merges (HERD-94); HERD_SPAWN_PRIO=<n> (HERD-630) publishes a priority BAND in an optional .prio sidecar — lowest drains first, FIFO by INTENT_ID within a band, CONSULTED only under INTENT_QUEUE=on, and byte-inert when unset. Both ride SIDECARS, never the .req body, whose slug/lane/task parse is positional and frozen so an intent enqueued by an older engine still drains. HERD-639: the id minting, the queue-scoped sequence lock and the atomic publish come from the shared scripts/herd/intent-queue.sh (iq_mint_id / iq_publish), and a TRACKED enqueue under INTENT_QUEUE=on ALSO publishes an M3 `marker-publish` intent into the sibling intent-queue/ so the item's 📌 planned marker appears without a coordinator turn; byte-inert with the lever off
when_to_surface: When the coordinator wants to launch a new builder without blocking its own context window; preferred over calling herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh directly when throughput matters

name: spawn-step.sh
description: Atomic queue mechanics for the durable spawn queue, called from agent-watch.sh's _drain_spawn_queue (NOT a Claude drainer). Subcommands: next reclaims ABANDONED claims (>5 min old AND no live owner — HERD-237: a backgrounded lane legitimately holds its claim for the whole lane, so liveness, not age, decides) and atomically claims the oldest pending intent (prints CLAIMED + slug/lane/ref/after/task or EMPTY, returns immediately); own binds a claim to the pid of the lane worker running it, so the reclaim can tell a live lane from a dead watcher; done removes a claimed file after a successful launch; release returns a claimed intent to the queue unconsumed (a deferred spawn, a dependency hold); skip logs a warning and drops a malformed intent without crashing the watcher. done/release/skip exit 3 rather than silently no-op when the claim they were handed has vanished, so a lost claim is never mistaken for a consumed one. HERD-630 adds the INTENT_QUEUE-gated ops (all inert while the lever is off): `next` orders candidates through _intent_queue_order (lowest .prio band first, FIFO by INTENT_ID within a band; lever off = the untouched `ls -1 <q>/*.req | sort` FIFO); `cancel <intent-id>` COUNTERMANDS a still-unclaimed intent by renaming <id>.req -> <id>.cancelled and journaling spawn_intent_cancelled — atomic, so it races the drain's own claim safely and the loser exits 3 (a CLAIMED intent cannot be un-launched: countermand the builder instead); `expired <path> <ttl>` is a pure predicate (exit 0 = aged past <ttl> seconds since ENQUEUE, measured from the INTENT_ID's own epoch field, never an mtime the claim handoff deliberately touches); `escalate <path> <reason>` retires a claim to the terminal <id>.escalated so no later `next` can serve it. HERD-639 (Phase 2) COMPLETED that lift: the mechanics now live in scripts/herd/intent-queue.sh and this script is the spawn queue's TENANT CLI over them — it supplies only the queue dir, the frozen positional payload format, the operator-facing messages and the spawn journal event names, and its behavior is byte-identical (tests/test-spawn-queue-drain.sh passes UNMODIFIED). The one exception is `release`, whose three statements stay INLINE because that test asserts their order by inspecting this file's own case body; tests/test-intent-queue-lib.sh asserts the same order inside iq_release AND that the two bodies still agree, so the mirror cannot drift
when_to_surface: Internal mechanics of the spawn queue drain; not called directly by the coordinator

name: intent-queue.sh
description: THE shared intent-queue library (HERD-639, Phase 2 of HERD-625; design doc docs/spikes/coordinator-work-queue.md §3.2 Option B + §6). ONE implementation of the pool-queue mechanics every intent tenant needs — iq_claim (abandoned-claim reclaim by OWNER LIVENESS not age, orphan-sidecar GC, then an atomic-rename claim in drain order), iq_own / iq_done / iq_release / iq_skip / iq_cancel / iq_escalate, plus the priority band (iq_prio / iq_order), the enqueue-epoch TTL predicate (iq_expired), the transient-attempt counter (iq_attempts / iq_attempt_bump), the atomic enqueue (iq_mint_id / iq_publish / iq_enqueue, HERD-443 same-second FIFO) and the lazy journal hook (iq_journal). SOURCED, never executed: every entry point is PURE over a queue DIRECTORY or claim PATH passed as an argument, so a second tenant needs no rewrite — which is exactly what Phase 1 wrote its policy block shaped for, and what turns §8's 'extraction-shaped by discipline' risk into structure. Grounding: the pool already ran three near-identical `next` implementations (spawn / scribe / research) whose reclaim, linger and ordering behavior had DRIFTED — a per-surface copy of one rule is what docs/multi-seat-doctrine.md Rule 2 calls a correctness defect. Tenants today: the SPAWN queue via spawn-step.sh + spawn.sh (tenant #1, byte-identical — tests/test-spawn-queue-drain.sh passes UNMODIFIED against it), the M3 QUEUE-MARKER queue via agent-watch.sh's _drain_intent_queue (tenant #2), and HERD-640's Phase-3 pair on that same sibling queue — M2 `close-on-evidence` (a PR carrying `Refs:` CLOSED UNMERGED drives its item to the right terminal; produced by tracker-state-sweep.sh's closed-unmerged evidence scan, executed by _intent_evidence_apply) and M4 `note-ack` (clear a routed builder note once its artifact exists; produced by _scan_note_routes from `herd notes route`, executed by _intent_note_ack_apply). NO new config key: Phase 1's INTENT_QUEUE lever governs every non-FIFO behavior, and with it off the library serves the untouched `ls -1 <q>/*.req | sort` FIFO. Tenant knobs are plain variables set before sourcing (IQ_LOG_PREFIX / IQ_ENGINE_DIR / IQ_SIDECARS / IQ_PRIO_DEFAULT / IQ_RECLAIM_MMIN), never config. NOT multi-seat safe: at-most-one CLAIM is cross-seat safe (one atomic rename), at-most-one ADMISSION is Phase 4's job (§5.5) HERD-642 (Phase 5) added GENERATIONS and the plan reader to the same library: iq_gen_mint/iq_gen_publish/iq_gen_retire stamp, atomically swap and retire a whole priority-ordered generation of intents through one rename of a <qdir>/.gen pointer (iq_order drops any intent whose stamp is not the live generation, so a superseded plan leaves the drain set instantly, while an UNSTAMPED intent — every ad-hoc spawn.sh enqueue — is unaffected), and iq_plan_rows is the ONE reader both `herd queue list` and agent-watch.sh's 'planned work' console section render.
when_to_surface: Internal mechanics shared by every intent queue in the worktree pool; not called directly by the coordinator. Read it before adding a THIRD tenant — a new intent kind passes §2.1's four-part test in its own item, never by inheritance

name: scripts/herd/agents.sh
description: THE shared specialist-agent-roster implementation behind `herd agents` (HERD-667) — SOURCED by the builder lanes (herd-feature.sh / herd-quick.sh) for HERD_AGENT selection and by bin/herd for the CLI and the doctor leg, and RUNNABLE as that CLI. Owns: roster location + definition parsing (frontmatter name/description/sentinel, body = system prompt); the three driver bindings DRIVER_AGENT_DEFINITION_DIR / DRIVER_AGENT_SELECT_FLAG / DRIVER_AGENT_DEFINITION_MODE read through driver.sh's PURE herd_driver_agent_value, with the drivers' @degrade:<reason> sentinel read as CAPABILITY ABSENT so an unbound runtime degrades to the portable INJECT fallback instead of a red row; the publish step (install); the two-sided empirical verify and its (driver, definition sha)-keyed verdict cache in the worktree pool; and the two lane seams — herd_roster_lane_select_flags (appended to the spawn <flags>, which herd_driver_agent_spawn_argv already word-splits into the argv, so selection needs NO new seam in the spawn composer) and herd_roster_lane_spec_block (the definition body prepended to the task spec). Exactly one of the two is ever non-empty and BOTH are empty when HERD_AGENT is unset. Fail-soft throughout: a missing roster, an unreadable definition, an absent runtime binary and an unwritable cache all degrade to a clear note and exit 0
when_to_surface: Internal implementation of the agent roster; drive it through `herd agents` rather than calling it directly. Read it before adding a driver for a new runtime — the three roster bindings are DATA in templates/drivers/<name>.driver, not code here

name: backlog-reconcile.sh
description: Reconcile BACKLOG.md against a merged PR's rename/move surface: diff the PR (surface = renamed/moved/deleted files via git rename detection + functions/section-headers defined before the PR and gone after), find backlog entries that still reference the old path/name, and enqueue ONE scribe request to update or ⚠️-flag each dangling entry (subcommands: surface | scan | run <pr#|git-range>); never edits the backlog itself
when_to_surface: After landing a cutover/extraction/rename PR that moves files, renames functions, or retitles sections the backlog points at — run `backlog-reconcile.sh run <pr#>` so stale references get fixed or flagged instead of dangling silently

name: backlog-reconcile-sweep.sh
description: Periodic ADVISORY drift sweep: cross-reference open 🔜 backlog items against recently-merged PRs (gh pr list --state merged) and recent commit subjects (git log) by conservative key-term overlap, and PRINT a ranked list of probably-shipped-but-still-🔜 candidates (title + matching PR#/commit + confidence). Catches work that shipped via an automated path (auto-refix / direct hand-off) without being reaped. Default is report-only and never edits the backlog; --enqueue files ONE scribe reconcile request per HIGH-confidence candidate (the scribe verifies before touching BACKLOG.md)
when_to_surface: Run periodically (or when the backlog looks stale after a merge burst) to catch 🔜 items that already shipped — review the printed candidates, then re-run with --enqueue to have the scribe reap the confirmed ones

name: journal-audit.sh
description: Journal-driven self-audit / gap-finder (HERD-238 / N12): a periodic ADVISORY auditor that replays a BOUNDED window of the engine journal looking for invariant violations that were VISIBLE in the journal but nothing was reading — (a) a merge without a later reap for the same pr/slug; (b) a *_dispatched event with no terminal outcome past a family TTL; (c) a refix_bounce with no matching refix_wake_result; (d) a main_health red older than a TTL with no later green; (e) pushed=no never followed by pushed=yes (codemap/symbol_index refresh); (i) a DETACHED shared checkout (HERD-336) — a main_detached result=detected with no later result=reattached; (f) known-fixture slugs (retiree/conv/stuck/hd — the HERD-223 pollution set); (g) a MERGED PR whose body declares a HUMAN-VERIFY block but carries NO sha-keyed approval record under HUMAN_VERIFY_POLICY=hold|coordinator (HERD-272; POLICY-AWARE since HERD-644 — under policy=auto every hv-holding merge is DESIGNED to go through unsigned as informational, so that case is never a finding) — the class the _pr_body fail-open (fixed in 65fe660) could have auto-merged on any gh 5xx blip. Check (g) reads DURABLE evidence from the journal itself — `approval_recorded` (herd-approve.sh) and `human_verify_policy policy=auto` (agent-watch.sh) — because do_merge's purge_pr_approvals deletes every approval-ledger row for a PR the instant it merges; the live ledger is consulted through approvals.sh only as a union fallback, and the PR body through gh; it runs ONGOING each tick and RETROACTIVELY when a one-shot run widens JOURNAL_AUDIT_WINDOW_SECS. With no gh (and no HERD_JOURNAL_AUDIT_PR_BODY_CMD seam) it skips silently; an unreadable body is reported as an `unknown` finding, never as a missing approval. Findings → journal_audit events (component=audit) + operator-inbox ledger rows (source=audit). ADVISORY ONLY — never gates a merge, never mutates git/PRs/tracker/BACKLOG. SHIP-DORMANT behind JOURNAL_AUDIT=off (default); FAIL-SOFT on empty/short/unreadable journal; idempotent via a seen-ledger so re-runs do not re-flood. Wired into the watcher housekeeping cadence (same tick interval as tracker-state-sweep) via agent-watch.sh _sweep_journal_audit
when_to_surface: Enable JOURNAL_AUDIT=on for an unattended coordinator so journal-visible gaps (stranded reviews, missing reaps, fixture pollution, stale MAIN RED) surface in the operator inbox instead of waiting for a human to read herd log; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior. Never a merge gate

name: journal-audit-replay.sh
description: THE REPLAY half of journal-audit.sh (HERD-608): _ja_replay_findings and _ja_replay_merges, the two python-heredoc scanners that turn a bounded journal window into the FINDINGS and MERGES TSVs journal-audit.sh's checks consume, moved out of journal-audit.sh verbatim (same env-var contract, same stdout shape, same exit status — byte-identical behavior) so BOTH files sit well clear of bash 3.2's heredoc-parser line-count cliff (macOS system /bin/bash 3.2.57 — the interpreter the watcher pane resolves, no /opt/homebrew/bin on its PATH — throws a FALSE "syntax error near unexpected token `('" at an unrelated heredoc once a script crosses roughly 1271 total lines, while GNU bash 5.x and shellcheck parse the identical file cleanly; see scripts/herd/bash-syntax-lint.sh, the standing guard against a script drifting back toward that cliff). Sourced (never executed) by journal-audit.sh only, immediately after herd-config.sh/journal.sh/human-verify.sh/approvals.sh/aging-pr.sh. Defines two functions only; no source-time side effects.
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced only by journal-audit.sh; the seam to change when the replay scanner's env-var contract or output shape changes, or when journal-audit.sh itself needs to shed more lines to stay clear of the bash-3.2 cliff

name: journal-act.sh
description: THE RAIL-DISPATCH half of "journal-audit findings become ACTIONS" (HERD-544): given ONE journal-audit finding class, drive the ONE existing engine rail that unsticks it, so the auditor becomes the safety net UNDER all rails instead of a report that waits for a human. Detection alone left the engine stuck in the seam between rails — every stall class that DOES auto-resolve has an owner (refix, stale-base, wedge, dead-builder, limit-park, resurrect), but a journal-audit finding had none. COMPOSITION, never reimplementation (the discipline retirement.sh/sweep.sh follow): agent-watch.sh is sourced in LIB mode (AGENT_WATCH_LIB=1) and each arm calls a shipped primitive — dispatch_no_outcome → _sweep_gate_corpses (the HERD-185 restart-safe gate hygiene) frees the concurrency slot the dead/timed-out worker still holds and the NEXT tick's gate step owns the re-dispatch with its own retry budget + infra breaker; refix_bounce_no_wake → re-deliver the review bounce ONCE to the builder's agent pane (_find_builder_pane_id_any + herd_driver_send_text + _wait_agent_working) and, ONLY on a proven wake, journal the real refix_wake_result the lost bounce never wrote, so the finding closes itself — no refix ROUND is charged, since the round was already recorded by the bounce that lost its wake; red_state_stale → drop the main-health run-once marker for the CURRENT $MAIN HEAD so reconcile_main_health re-dispatches the suite next tick (the MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS re-verify, forced once), declining with rail_off when MAIN_HEALTH_TICK is off rather than reporting a heal that never happened; merge_without_reap → retirement_tick (HERD-164) NOW, after fetching the open-PR roster honestly and DECLINING on a failed lookup so the invariant never runs on a roster known to be blind. An unrecognized class prints `unmapped` BEFORE any library load, which is what makes journal-audit.sh file a dedup-keyed tracker item for the gap. Stdout is a SINGLE lowercase result token journaled verbatim as audit_acted result= — retired/slot_freed/rebounced/reverify_armed mean the rail ran; rail_off/no_pane/no_wake/no_slug/no_head/pr_lookup_failed/reverify_pending/unavailable/unmapped mean it did not, and say why. ONE bounded action per invocation: no loop, no retry — "once per finding key" is the CALLER's guarantee (a shared-pool once-guard), so this file keeps no ledger. ALWAYS exits 0; never self-arming (nothing schedules it — journal-audit.sh's action pass is its only caller, and that pass is dormant unless JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT=on). HERD_JOURNAL_ACT_SELFTEST=1 skips the LIB source so argument parsing + the unmapped path are provable with no control room
when_to_surface: Internal rail dispatcher, executed (never sourced) by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh's action pass; the seam to change when a journal-audit finding class gains, loses, or changes its auto-action — keep its case arms in step with _ja_act_mapped in journal-audit.sh

name: lifecycle.sh
description: The SUPERVISED-PROCESS CONTRACT shared library (HERD-193): owner / deadline / liveness / retire bookkeeping for EVERY agent population herdkit spawns (builders, reviewers, resolvers, the scribe + research drainer singletons, the health/review gate workers, and the two backgrounded lane workers HERD-237 forks off the tick — the builder lane and the resolver lane, whose corpse sweep is agent-watch's _spawn_inflight_sweep (HERD-268)). Sourced by agent-watch.sh, scribe.sh and research.sh. lifecycle_spawn records one per-process file under $WORKTREES_DIR/.lifecycle/ (population, id, OWNER=the component that spawned it, PROBE=pid:<n> | heartbeat:<file>, DEADLINE, spawn epoch, ROUTE=the existing owner that tears this population down) and journals lifecycle_spawn; lifecycle_retire drops it and journals lifecycle_retire with lived_secs; lifecycle_sweep (a per-tick watcher leg) retires any process that has EXITED (after a short grace, so the population's own teardown records the TRUE reason first) and journals lifecycle_expired ONCE — plus an operator-inbox row — for anything past its deadline while STILL RUNNING. A stale heartbeat is never a hang on its own: it is corroborated against the agent's real liveness (HERD-122), so a drainer that finished cleanly is retired, not reported hung; the drainers additionally retire their own record on their normal completion path (*-step.sh finish). DEADLINES REUSE each population's existing timeout (REVIEW_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT / HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT / DRAINER_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT), so no new tunables. OBSERVABILITY-ONLY: it NEVER kills, gates or merges — an expiry routes to the population's existing owner (gate corpse sweep, drainer reclaim, stall detector, resolver escalation). Per-process record files (never one shared ledger) so two concurrent writers cannot drop each other's rows. SHIP-DORMANT behind LIFECYCLE_CONTRACTS=off (default): every public function is an immediate no-op. FAIL-SOFT: an unreadable probe is treated as ALIVE, never a fabricated death
when_to_surface: Turn LIFECYCLE_CONTRACTS on when an unattended coordinator must account for every process it spawned — a hung drainer, a reviewer past its corpse-sweep deadline, a health worker that died verdictless — surfaced in the journal and operator inbox instead of found by process archaeology. Leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: governance-drift-sweep.sh
description: Periodic ADVISORY governance-DRIFT sweep (HERD-125): re-extract an OPTIONAL CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md with the SAME deterministic extraction the HERD-119 init adoption pass uses (scripts/herd/governance.sh + templates/governance-map.tsv) and DIFF the config-key rules the prose maps to against the effective .herd/config. A mapped rule whose value differs from the enforced config is DRIFT — surfaced LOUDLY (a stdout advisory naming the key + proposed value + the exact `herd config set` to adopt, one governance_drift journal event per drifted key, and with --pr N one PR comment) but NEVER auto-applied. Fail-soft and BYTE-IDENTICALLY SILENT when there is no such file or every mapped rule already matches the config. Reuses HERD-119 extraction (same file surface, which is why HERD-125 is sequenced after it)
when_to_surface: Run periodically (or after a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md edit lands on the default branch) to catch governance PROSE that drifted from the enforced .herd/config — the advisory names each key and the `herd config set` to adopt it; add --pr N to also comment on a PR. Advisory only: it never edits config, so review and adopt (or update the prose) by hand

name: agent-watch.sh
description: Live status console and auto-merge state machine: polls PRs, runs healthcheck and review gate, merges ready PRs; a PR whose body declares a HUMAN-VERIFY block is held for sha-keyed approval instead of auto-merging
when_to_surface: Runs continuously in the watcher pane; coordinator checks its verdicts for blocked, held, or failed PRs

name: approvals.sh
description: THE shared seam for the sha-keyed APPROVAL LEDGER ($WORKTREES_DIR/.agent-watch-approvals, rows `<epoch> <state> <pr#> <sha>` with state ∈ awaiting|approved|hv-informed). _approvals_file resolves the path once (HERD_APPROVALS_FILE overrides it for tests) and approval_state/approval_recorded interpret a row once, so herd-approve.sh (which writes the ledger) and agent-watch.sh (which reads it before merging) can never name two different files. NOTE the ledger is EPHEMERAL: do_merge purges every row for a PR on merge (HERD-90), so a post-merge auditor must read the journal's `approval_recorded` event instead — journal-audit.sh check (g) does, and consults this ledger only as a union fallback. An `hv-informed` row (HUMAN_VERIFY_POLICY=auto) is deliberately NOT an approval — nobody ran the declared steps. Sourcing only defines functions: no writes, no journal, no side effects. Missing or unreadable ledger folds to `none`, so callers never distinguish no-ledger from no-row
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the approval-ledger path or row grammar changes

name: merge-policy.sh
description: THE shared resolver for the effective merge policy (HERD-159, unified in HERD-210): _effective_merge_policy resolves auto|approve|observe once, and agent-watch.sh, bin/herd cmd_reload and posture-lint.sh all source it, so the watcher, the reload summary and herd doctor --posture can never disagree about whether PRs will be merged. MERGE_POLICY wins when recognized; empty/unset derives from the legacy WATCHER_AUTOMERGE boolean; a non-empty unrecognized value is a typo that fails STRICT to observe (never merge)
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the merge-gate contract changes

name: engine-seat.sh
description: CROSS-SEAT DUAL-ENGINE SAFETY (HERD-308): THE one shared helper that stamps every mutable-state write under the worktree pool with the writer's engine level and reconciles it every watcher tick, so two engines at different behavior levels can never silently clobber one pool. herd_engine_seat_stamp appends (seat, level, epoch, state) to an append-only pool registry; herd_engine_seat_reconcile classifies the active seats COHERENT|LEAD|STALE and herd_engine_seat_hold refuses the stale seat's writes (do_merge / post_gate_status hold). Also carries the P4 migration-quiesce gate: herd_engine_migration_guard refuses a store migration unless every other registered seat is quiesced (herd_engine_seat_quiesce) or a dual-write window is declared (HERD_ENGINE_DUALWRITE / marker). The pysrc store accessors adopt the same stamp format in P4. Sourced (never launched) by agent-watch.sh; wholly inert while ENGINE_SEAT_RECONCILE=off and always inert for a single seat
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the dual-engine stamp format, the cross-seat reconcile, or the P4 migration-quiesce contract changes

name: work-unit.sh
description: WORK-UNIT DELIVERY FACADE, Phase 1 (HERD-395/HERD-396; design: docs/spikes/work-unit-abstraction.md): names the work-unit interface (open/gate/apply/reconcile/teardown/list_open/inspect) as wunit_* functions, implementing ONLY the git-pr kind — each wrapper is a one-line delegation to today's existing git-pr path (gh pr create/list/view for open/list_open/inspect; _cand_gates_ready for gate; do_merge for apply; reconcile_backlog for reconcile; _reap_slug for teardown). Auto-sources agent-watch.sh's function bank via the AGENT_WATCH_LIB=1 seam (sweep.sh/retirement.sh precedent) when not already in scope. HARD INVARIANT: no existing caller is switched to the facade in this PR — zero behavior change, byte-identical git-pr path
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; REFERENCE-MODEL-ONLY for open/list_open/inspect/gate/apply (zero production call sites — superseded live by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py, spike §9.1), still LIVE for reconcile/teardown (called every merge by agent-watch.sh regardless of which engine merged); the seam a hermetic test or the sim scenario suite exercises to keep the git-pr semantics proven

name: resolver-pane.sh
description: THE shared resolver for the RESOLVER_PANE lever (HERD-286): _effective_resolver_pane resolves on|off once, and agent-watch.sh + herd-resolve.sh both source it, so the pane-placement decision and the pane-closing reconcile can never disagree about which values arm the path. RESOLVER_PANE recognized on-values (on|true|yes|1) → "on"; empty/unset → "off" (ship-dormant default); any unrecognized non-empty value → "off" (fail-soft: a typo can never arm a pane-closing path). _resolver_pane_is_typo lets callers surface a bad value advisory. Pure helpers, no side effects
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the resolver-pane lever contract changes

name: review-panel.sh
description: THE shared resolver for the mixed-vendor review panel (HERD-276): parses REVIEW_PANEL_MODELS into per-panelist model refs, resolves REVIEW_PANEL_POLICY, and folds the per-panelist verdict files into ONE verdict line (herd_review_merge_verdicts). herd-review.sh sources it for BOTH enforcement surfaces (the local pre-PR review and the watcher's pre-merge gate) and bin/herd sources it to validate refs eagerly at 'herd config set', so no surface can drift into a different fold. Guarantees a non-reporting panelist never moves a verdict toward BLOCK, only toward INFRA
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the panel's dispatch or verdict-fold contract changes

name: review-pregate.sh
description: THE shared REVIEW FAST PATH chokepoint (HERD-559): one implementation of the MECHANICAL-RED PRE-GATE and the SMALL-MECHANICAL-DIFF FLOOR, shelled as a subprocess by all three call sites (agent-watch.sh's review dispatch leg, pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's live review rail, and herd-review.sh's own preamble) so they can never disagree. `herd_review_pregate <tree> [<base-ref>]` runs the EXISTING shared lint set (caps-sync, the config-manifest ghost/dead-key scan, journal-emission, pipe-safety, git-scope, doc-drift — no new rule, the SAME implementations both healthcheck profiles run) with the tree as cwd and prints every red lint's findings; it is BASELINE-SUBTRACTED (the identical set is re-run against a `git archive` snapshot of the merge base and matching finding lines are dropped) so a red already standing on the default branch — which the diff-scoped merge suite provably lets through — never bounces a builder onto somebody else's problem. `herd_review_mech_floor <tree> [<base-ref>]` recognizes a diff whose every changed file is a TSV row edit, a pure 100%-similarity rename, or a version bump, within REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR_MAXFILES/MAXLINES and matching no REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB path. Exit 0 clean/mechanical - 1 red/not-mechanical - 2 skipped; a skip is NEVER a red. Sourceable for tests, executed everywhere else: builder-authored lint bodies must not be sourced into the watcher
when_to_surface: Internal library plus a `lint|floor <tree> [<base-ref>]` CLI; the seam to change when the pre-gate's lint set or the mechanical-diff shape rules change

name: config-viability.sh
description: THE shared EXTERNAL-CONSISTENCY PROBES (HERD-355): validate .herd/config against LIVE external reality — the GitHub repo's allow_*_merge flags, its branch-protection required checks, and the runtime a driver-qualified MODEL_* resolves to — catching config-vs-ENVIRONMENT mismatches (MERGE_METHOD the repo disallows / HERD-354; a required herd/gates check GATE_STATUS=off never posts / HERD-352; an undriveable MODEL_REVIEW driver / HERD-311) at set time instead of hours later as a silent gate failure. herd_config_viability_probe <key> <value> dispatches the probe DECLARED for that key in capabilities.tsv's env_coupling column (a key with empty env_coupling is skipped, so a new coupled key auto-covers itself) and prints one STATUS(OK|WARN|MISMATCH|SKIP) line; bin/herd sources it so BOTH `herd config set` (a targeted probe that REFUSES a PROVEN mismatch naming both sides, WARNS when offline) and `herd doctor` (the advisory "Config viability" section) drive the SAME check. Probes read live external state each run (no seat-local cache), fail-soft offline (a probe that cannot reach gh WARNS, never a red, never blocks), and land results as a config_viability journal event + a machine-readable report ($WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/config-viability.json) the coordinator reads at session start
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced (never launched) by bin/herd; the seam to change when a NEW externally-coupled config key needs a live-consistency probe — add its probe token to the env_coupling column and implement it here

name: retirement.sh
description: THE RETIREMENT INVARIANT (HERD-164): teardown reconciled on EVERY watcher tick instead of fired as a merge-time event. A slug whose PR is MERGED or CLOSED (or whose worktree is gone) owns no worktree, tab, agent, branch, or ledger row; retirement_tick observes the world, computes the leftovers, drives the idempotent teardown one step further, and repeats until converged — so a watcher killed at ANY teardown step is harmless (the next tick of the next watcher finishes the job) and the only disk state is an escalation counter. Composes the shipped primitives rather than reimplementing them: _reap_slug (HERD-91), sweep.sh's regenerable-dirt + unique-commit proofs (HERD-191), herd_teardown_slug, _herd_tabs_drop_row. SAFETY: the anchor is the COMMIT, never the slug — nothing is torn down unless its HEAD is the head of a PR GitHub reports terminal, so a reused slug, an in-flight builder with no PR, and a gh outage all fail the anchor and are left untouched. Regenerable dirt (.DS_Store, __pycache__) is tolerated; a modified TRACKED file or commits that exist nowhere else are REAL WORK — never deleted, never silently skipped, always a LOUD needs-you row carrying the evidence, curable only by a human. DELETE_BRANCH_ON_MERGE=false means a landed branch is retained on purpose, so it is neither deleted nor counted as a leftover. VOCABULARY (HERD-172's closed set): 'retiring… · <leftovers> · <age>' while converging (the herd's move, calm); 'reap deferred · <why> · <age>' when a MERGED/CLOSED tree still has a WORKING builder (HERD-356 — the herd's move, calm ⏸️; only a POSITIVE agent_status=working defers, an idle/absent builder reaps, and the deferred tree reaps itself the moment the agent goes idle); 'needs-you · retirement stuck: <blocker>' once a teardown has failed 3 ticks running (yours, red, naming what would not die); 'needs-you · <evidence>' when held — which is what finally reserves 'awaiting task' for a genuinely unassigned pre-PR builder
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced by agent-watch.sh (never launched); the seam to change when teardown must reap a NEW kind of per-slug residue, or when the retiring/deferred/stuck/held console vocabulary changes. `herd sweep` remains the on-demand, whole-control-room cleanup

name: suite-shard.sh
description: THE shared curated-test-selection + stable shard-assignment library for the hermetic suite (HERD-463: CI 24m/13m + local heavy gate ~20m, ~350 tests run serially). herd_suite_curated_tests <tests_dir> [<exempt_file>] prints the CURATED tests/test-*.sh set (every test-*.sh MINUS tests/gate-coverage-exempt.tsv — the same selection scripts/ci/run-suite.sh has always used). herd_suite_shard_hash <name> derives a stable non-negative integer from `cksum` (POSIX 1003.2, present on every platform this suite runs on). herd_suite_shard_of <name> <shard_count> gives the 1-based shard a name belongs to: (hash % shard_count)+1 — deterministic across processes/machines, and STABLE under insertion (adding one test never reshuffles an existing test's shard, unlike an index/chunk partition). herd_suite_tests_for_shard <tests_dir> <shard_index> <shard_count> [<exempt_file>] composes the two: shard_count<=1 is the full curated set, byte-identical to an unsharded selection. Sourced (never executed) by scripts/ci/run-suite.sh (HERD_CI_SHARD_INDEX/HERD_CI_SHARD_COUNT, the CI matrix fan-out) and tests/test-suite-shard.sh (the mutation-prove membership check: the union of every shard reconstructs the curated set exactly, so a dropped or double-counted test can never read as green)
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the curated-selection rule changes (a new exempt convention) or when the shard-hash algorithm changes — every consumer (the CI matrix, the membership proof) reads the SAME function so they can never disagree about what a shard drops

name: scope-escape.sh
description: HERD-575 SCOPING-ESCAPE TELEMETRY: the shared detector both sides of a diff-scoped gate (HERD-532) source. herd_scope_gate_record <sha> <selected-list> <curated-list>, called by .herd/healthcheck.project.sh right where it computes a narrowed HEALTH_SUITE_SCOPE=diff selection, journals ONE `gate_scoped` event (sha, selected/total counts, the selected test basenames) — durable proof this shas gate ran scoped. herd_scope_gate_was_scoped <sha> looks that record up. herd_scope_escape_check <sha> <failing-identity> <tests_dir> <changed-path>... — sourced by scripts/herd/agent-watch.sh's main-health/CI red chokepoint (_main_health_set_red via _scope_escape_detect) — no-ops unless the sha was recorded scoped, otherwise RECOMPUTES the selection fresh via suite-shard.sh's herd_suite_tests_for_diff (never a replay) and, only when a failing test-*.sh token is absent from that recompute, journals `scope_escape` (sha, missed test(s), recomputed selection) and prints one candidate row for herd_scope_escape_append_candidate to append (idempotent, never materializes a new file) to the committed tests/suite-deps-candidates.tsv ledger — an advisory worklist a human/builder promotes into a real `# suite-deps:` header. `herd stats` surfaces the running scope_escape count. Observability only: every function fails soft, and is byte-inert whenever HEALTH_SUITE_SCOPE never narrowed a shas gate in the first place (HERD-532's own default-off lever), so a red's journal line stays byte-identical to before this file existed.
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change if a scope-escape false-positive or false-negative is found — every consumer (the gate recorder, the main-health detector) reads the SAME recompute so they can never disagree about what counts as a proven miss

name: health-trust.sh
description: THE shared SHA-MATCHED BUILDER-LOCAL HEALTH TRUST library (HERD-531, hardened HERD-560): the health gate is the pipeline's dominant cost (~350 hermetic tests, 20-60 min per suite), and when a builder runs the heavy profile before opening its PR the watcher re-runs the IDENTICAL suite on the IDENTICAL commit and pays for it twice. herd_health_trust_write <trees> <sha> <worktree> <profile> <outcome> <duration> [provenance] [log] appends an ENGINE-AUTHORED FORMAT VERSION 2 provenance record ($WORKTREES_DIR/.health-provenance-<sha>: version, sha, worktree, profile, outcome, duration, provenance, tree_state, epoch, log_digest) when a heavy healthcheck completes, and — only for a CLEAN outcome — a companion suite-log file ($WORKTREES_DIR/.health-provenance-log-<sha>) whose sha256 becomes log_digest; herd_health_trust_check <trees> <sha> <worktree> returns 0 (printing the provenance token) only when that record attests a CLEAN heavy run of the EXACT head sha from a CLEAN working tree at that same worktree, its log_digest matches the companion log's actual bytes, it is within HEALTH_TRUST_MAX_AGE_SECS (default 21600s/6h) of now, and it was written no earlier than the commit itself and stamped builder-local. Sourced (never executed) by scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh (the writer, always) and scripts/herd/agent-watch.sh (HERD-531's original reader). HERD-555: the LIVE read is pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's LiveGates.health — agent-watch.sh's own _healthcheck_gate has had zero production callers since the Python engine port, and stays sourced only for the bash-parity test/sim surface still exercising it directly. Both readers consult the SAME herd_health_trust_check contract, so they can never disagree about what earns a skip. FAIL-CLOSED: no record, a pre-HERD-560 or unrecognized-version record (reads ABSENT, never an error), stale sha, non-heavy profile, non-CLEAN outcome, dirty tree, mismatched worktree, a record older than the age bound, a record predating the commit, an unresolvable commit time, a digest mismatch/missing companion log, or a record the watcher itself authored — every one is a FULL re-run, exactly as before. NO SIGNING: the single-tenant threat model is staleness, not forgery. Gated by HEALTH_TRUST_BUILDER (default off): off writes nothing and reads nothing
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the rule for what a builder-local heavy run PROVES changes (a new record field, a new disqualifier) — every consumer reads the SAME function so the writer and the trusting reader can never drift apart

name: core-surface.sh
description: THE shared CORE-SURFACE implementation (HERD-577): which diffs touch the engine's load-bearing core, which sandbox-sim scenario proves each touched seam, and whether the scorecard that sim emitted says result=pass. ONE implementation behind CORE_SURFACE_GLOB, reused at every enforcement surface (docs/multi-seat-doctrine.md Rule 2) — pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's gate leg and serialize prepass EXECUTE it (`paths` / `scenarios-for` / `run`), agent-watch.sh SOURCES it for the console rows, tests/test-core-surface.sh sources the pure functions. `herd_core_surface_glob` is the ONE resolver of the effective glob (empty = feature off); `herd_core_surface_paths <tree> [<base-ref>]` prints the merge-base-scoped changed paths that match it (exit 0 matched / 1 none / 2 unreadable); `herd_core_surface_scenarios <path>...` maps them through the committed seam table (concurrency: capacity-ledger/capacity-agent-lease-wait/burst/suite-shard/herd-spawn-gate; limit: agent-update/driver; panes: herd-feature/herd-quick/resolver-pane/tab-discipline/coordinator/herd-watch; gate: everything else, the fail-toward-more-proof default); `herd_core_surface_scorecard_ok <file>` is the jq-free result=pass read; `herd_core_surface_run <art> <out> <log> <nonce> <scenario>...` IS the async worker body the watcher dispatches, writing one `<nonce>\t<PASS|FAIL|SKIP>\t<detail>` line. Env seams (not config keys): HERD_CORE_SURFACE_SIM_DIR (scenario dir, default <here>/sim — the hermetic suite's stub seam) and HERD_CORE_SURFACE_TIMEOUT (per-scenario hard timeout, default 1800s, so a hung sim fails the scorecard instead of wedging the rail). FAIL-SOFT NEVER SILENT: an absent scenario is skipped with the absence carried into the verdict detail, and a run where NOTHING ran reports SKIP, never PASS
when_to_surface: Internal library plus a `glob|paths|scenarios|scenarios-for|verify|run` CLI; the seam to change when the definition of the core surface, the seam->scenario map, or the scorecard contract changes — every enforcement surface reads the SAME functions, so the console and the gate can never disagree about what "core" means

name: bats-fd3-guard.sh
description: THE shared HEALTHCHECK-LAYER chokepoint guard for the bats-FD3 wedge (HERD-462): bats-core dup's a live pipe onto an internal fd before each test so it can stream results back to its own aggregator; a test that backgrounds a child without closing that fd keeps the WRITE end open long after the test itself already reported "ok", wedging the WHOLE `bats` run behind that one leaked child (see tests/test-cli-reload.sh's own `_bg_close_fds` for the test-authoring half of this fix). herd_bats_early_reap <outfile> <wrapper_pid> [<grace_secs>] polls a bats run's growing output file for its TAP plan line (`1..N`) plus N result lines; once every planned test has reported, gives the run GRACE_SECS (default 15) to exit on its own before concluding it is wedged and killing it — signalling the `timeout` WRAPPER's pid specifically, since `timeout` relays a received signal on to its whole child process group, reaping a leaked descendant too. Sourced (never executed) by .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate's own bats invocation) so a future leaky test can never wedge the local gate behind the full ${HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_TIMEOUT:-1800}s backstop alone. Mutation-proven by tests/test-bats-fd3-guard.sh (a synthetic leaking fixture wedges unguarded, completes in seconds guarded)
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when bats' own internal fd/pipe mechanics change (a new bats major version) or when the healthcheck's early-reap grace window needs tuning

name: caps-sync-lint.sh
description: THE shared caps-sync guard (HERD-220): herd_caps_sync_lint <base-ref> reds a change that adds a cmd_* subcommand to bin/herd, a config key to scripts/herd/herd-config.sh, or ANY new scripts/herd/*.sh script without also touching templates/capabilities.tsv. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate) and scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate), so a manifest miss is caught before 'gh pr create' instead of bouncing at the merge gate (incident: PR #328) and the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: no resolvable diff, or no capabilities manifest in the tree (every consuming project), is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_CAPS_SYNC_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 violation / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the capability-manifest sync rule changes

name: aging-pr.sh
description: THE shared AGING-PR TTL helper (HERD-334): ONE implementation of the threshold both the watcher render pass (agent-watch.sh, the OBSERVED-state 'aging · engine-approved but blocked on <check>' advisory row) and the journal auditor (journal-audit.sh, the gates_passed_no_merge finding) read AGING_PR_TTL through — _aging_pr_ttl_secs (effective seconds, default 3600, non-numeric→default, 0=disabled), _aging_pr_armed (true iff TTL>0), _aging_pr_over_ttl <since> <now> (echoes the age, returns 0 iff ≥ TTL). Sourced (never executed) by BOTH surfaces so the render row and the audit finding can never disagree on when a PR is 'aging'. Read live on every call so a mid-process override (a test) is honored. Defining functions only, it has no side effects
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the aging-PR TTL threshold definition or the over-TTL predicate changes

name: gate-coverage-lint.sh
description: THE shared gate-coverage drift guard (HERD-292): herd_gate_coverage_lint [<root>] reds when a tests/test-*.sh exists but is not referenced in tests/herd.bats AND not listed in tests/gate-coverage-exempt.tsv. Prevents a new test file from sitting ungated at the merge gate indefinitely (proven live: HERD-257 had to do a one-time manual wiring of hundreds of files that had accumulated without this guard). Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Pure-function form herd_gate_coverage_check <bats> <tests-dir> [<exempt-file>] used by hermetic tests. Fail-soft: no tests/herd.bats in the tree (every consuming project) is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_GATE_COVERAGE_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 ungated / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the gate-coverage rule changes (e.g. exempt list path, matching pattern)

name: bash-syntax-lint.sh
description: THE shared SYSTEM-BASH SYNTAX guard (HERD-608): herd_bash_syntax_lint [<root>] bash -n's every scripts/herd/*.sh under the SYSTEM /bin/bash — a hardcoded path, never $(command -v bash) / a PATH-resolved bash. Catches the class that broke journal-audit.sh: once a scripts/herd/*.sh crosses roughly 1271 total lines, macOS's SYSTEM /bin/bash 3.2.57 — the interpreter the watcher pane resolves (no /opt/homebrew/bin on its PATH) — can throw a FALSE "syntax error near unexpected token `('" at an unrelated heredoc, while a PATH-resolved bash 5.x and shellcheck both parse the identical file cleanly. A builder who only ever runs `bash -n`/shellcheck against PATH bash never sees the failure their change is about to trip — the first place it surfaces is the live watcher pane, mid-tick. Pure-function form herd_bash_syntax_check <file>... used by hermetic tests. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. FAIL-SOFT ON THE TOOL, NEVER ON THE FINDING: no /bin/bash on the machine (e.g. a Windows collaborator on Git Bash), or no scripts/herd/*.sh surface, is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_BASH_SYNTAX_SKIP_REASON, never a red; a machine whose /bin/bash is not 3.2 still runs the probe under that /bin/bash rather than skipping, since a real syntax error is real on every bash. Exit 0 clean / 1 syntax error / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the scan surface (currently scripts/herd/*.sh, non-recursive) or the target interpreter path changes. Surface it when a BASH-SYNTAX red needs explaining, or when asked what stops a script from silently drifting past bash 3.2's heredoc-parser cliff

name: source-guard-lint.sh
description: THE shared dot-source-guard drift guard (HERD-632): herd_source_guard_lint [<root>] reds a NEW fail-soft '. "$VAR/lib.sh"' (a best-effort, optional-dependency source whose own error handling resolves to success/continue — '|| true', '|| return', or a '{ …; exit 0; }' fallback) that lacks a preceding '[ -f ]' test or real subshell wrapping. bash treats '.' as a SPECIAL BUILTIN: sourcing a path that does not exist can KILL THE SHELL OUTRIGHT under a caller's set -e, bypassing the '||' entirely — proven live at scripts/herd/herd-claim.sh lines 56/61, where 'command -v journal_append >/dev/null 2>&1 || . "$DIR/journal.sh" 2>/dev/null || true' read as fail-soft but silently killed the whole process on a missing journal.sh. A source whose failure is meant to be FATAL ('|| exit 1' etc.) is out of scope — the special-builtin bypass and the intended '||' land on the same outcome there, so nothing needs guarding. A real subshell ('( … )', '$( … )', '< <( … )') also protects without a '[ -f ]' test, since the fatal exit only kills the subshell. scripts/herd/sim/, scripts/herd/experiment/ and tests/ are classified FIXTURE — scanned, counted in the advisory, never flagged. A deliberate exception (a subshell this lint's line-based heuristic cannot prove safe) carries an inline '# source-guard-ok: <why>'. Scan surface: bin/herd, herd.sh, install.sh, scripts/herd/*.sh + backends/ + work-units/, scripts/ci/*.sh, migrations/*.sh. Pure-function form herd_source_guard_check <file>... used by hermetic tests. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: the scan runs ONLY in a herdkit ENGINE tree (scripts/herd/ or bin/herd present) — every consuming project is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_SOURCE_GUARD_SKIP_REASON before a file is read. Exit 0 clean / 1 unguarded / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the fail-soft/guard detection rule changes (the failsoft signature, the subshell heuristic, the opt-out annotation, or the scan surface). Surface it when a SOURCE-GUARD red needs explaining, or when asked what stops a new fail-soft dot-source from silently becoming a whole-process crash

name: pipe-safety-lint.sh
description: THE shared pipe-safety guard (HERD-299): herd_pipe_safety_lint [<root>] reds a NEW '<producer> | grep -q/-m' (or '| head') across scripts/herd/*.sh + scripts/ci/*.sh + bin/herd. Under set -o pipefail the early-exit consumer (grep -q/-m exits on first/Nth match, head after N lines/bytes) closes the pipe, the producer takes EPIPE, and the pipeline goes nonzero once its output crosses a pipe buffer (macOS 16KB / Linux 64KB) — exactly the bug that turned macOS CI chronically red (HERD-297, swept for existing instances in #412; this is the GUARD against new ones). Safe forms 'grep -q PAT FILE' and 'grep -q PAT <<< "$v"' (no producer pipe) are not flagged; a verified-small producer opts out with an inline '# pipe-ok: <why>' (block-aware across a '\'-continued command). Pure-function form herd_pipe_safety_check <file>... used by hermetic tests; the detector greps files directly so it is itself pipefail-safe. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: no engine scan surface in the tree (every consuming project) is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_PIPE_SAFETY_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 unsafe / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the pipe-safety rule changes (e.g. the anti-pattern regex, the opt-out annotation, the scan surface)

name: test-cap-ledger.sh
description: THE shared PER-TEST TIMEOUT LEDGER library (HERD-478): scripts/ci/run-suite.sh wrapped every hermetic test in ONE static `timeout <HERD_CI_TEST_TIMEOUT>` (default 120s) no matter how heavy it genuinely is — a heavy outlier (e.g. test-cli-reload.sh's ~24 real `bin/herd reload` subprocess spawns, ~82-93s measured, little headroom against 120s) either gets silently added to tests/known-env-sensitive.tsv as a periodic-TIMEOUT XFAIL, or the shared cap gets raised for every test to cover the one outlier. herd_test_cap_for <test-name> <tsv-file> [<default-secs>] prints tests/test-caps.tsv's cap-secs for a listed test, else the default (fail-soft: a missing/malformed row falls through to the default, never leaves a test with NO cap). herd_test_cap_ledger_lint [<root>] [<default-secs>] reds a MALFORMED row (not exactly test/cap-secs/reason/measured-baseline, a non-numeric cap-secs or measured-baseline, or an empty reason/measured-baseline — no bare rows, the tests/gate-coverage-exempt.tsv / HERD-437 lesson) or a STALE row (measured-baseline sits at or under half the default: the test no longer needs an elevated cap). Sourced (never executed) by scripts/ci/run-suite.sh (the per-test timeout invocation) and BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the stale/malformed-row guard), so all three surfaces read the SAME ledger the SAME way. Fail-soft: no tests/ directory in the tree (every consuming project) is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_TEST_CAP_LEDGER_SKIP_REASON; a missing tests/test-caps.tsv is a valid empty ledger (every test uses the default), not a skip. Exit 0 clean / 1 malformed-or-stale / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the per-test timeout override rule changes (the ledger format, the stale-row margin) or when a newly-measured heavy test needs a cap-secs row

name: git-scope-lint.sh
description: THE shared engine/project ISOLATION guard (HERD-435, GitHub issue #547): herd_git_scope_lint [<root>] reds a PRODUCTION engine path that stages REPO-WIDE (git add -A/--all/-u/./:/ or git commit -a|-am|--all) or COMMITS WITH NO '-- <pathspec>'. Both shapes reach beyond the paths the engine owns: repo-wide staging can swallow an unrelated git repo nested in or beside the tree (proven: 'git add -A' stages it as a gitlink) and an index-wide commit can carry an operator's mid-edit in the shared checkout onto the default branch under a message that never names it. Isolation used to be EMERGENT (every call site was written carefully); this lint makes it ENFORCED. scripts/herd/sim/, scripts/herd/experiment/ and tests/ build throwaway repos in temp dirs and are classified FIXTURE — scanned, counted in the advisory, never flagged — so the sim-vs-production distinction is asserted, not accidental. A deliberate exception carries an inline '# herd-scope-ok: <why>' (honored on the line, anywhere in a continued command, or on the comment run directly above it). Scan surface: bin/herd, herd.sh, install.sh, scripts/herd/*.sh + backends/ + work-units/, scripts/ci/*.sh, migrations/*.sh and pysrc/herd/*.py — lines are normalized (quotes/commas to spaces) so ONE grammar covers the shell form and the python argv form alike. Pure-function form herd_git_scope_check <file>... used by hermetic tests. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: the scan runs ONLY in a herdkit ENGINE tree (scripts/herd/, pysrc/herd/ or bin/herd present) — every consuming project is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_GIT_SCOPE_SKIP_REASON before a file is read, so a consumer's own install.sh/scripts/ci can never be reded. Exit 0 clean / 1 unscoped / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the isolation rule changes (the repo-wide/unscoped grammar, the fixture classification, the opt-out annotation, or the scan surface). Surface it when asked what stops herdkit from touching an unrelated project repo, or when a GIT-SCOPE red needs explaining

name: journal-emission-lint.sh
description: THE shared CONSUMER-ONLY EVENT guard (HERD-442): herd_journal_emission_lint [<root>] reds any journal event NAME that a consumer PARSES but no producer EMITS. The defect it stops has landed three times — human_verify_policy (producer deleted with the bash action pass at ede7d45, 19 days unnoticed), hold_released (same deletion; herd why and the fleet inbox/digest all still read it) and merged_external (HERD-291 shipped the consumer with no producer at all, so the cross-seat leg never once fired). It is invisible to every other rail: the journal is best-effort, so a missing event is indistinguishable from 'it did not happen this run'. PRODUCERS are counted from PRODUCTION code only (bin/herd, scripts/herd/**.sh, pysrc/herd/*.py) — scripts/herd/sim/, scripts/herd/experiment/ and tests/ are EXCLUDED, because a sim that journals an event itself and then asserts it is a self-fulfilling guard, not a producer. Dynamic producers are RESOLVED, not ignored: journal_append "$1" through the wrapper's call sites and journal_append "$var" through same-file literal assignments, so control_pane_mutation_refused and healthcheck_retried are correctly seen as produced, and a "prefix_$kind" form registers a prefix producer. CONSUMERS are every surface that parses a name: journal-audit.sh, fleet.sh, bin/herd (herd why / herd log), pysrc/herd/*.py, the sims and experiments, and the §3.4 event catalog in docs/engine-contract.md. A deliberately-unproduced event opts out in the in-file allowlist WITH ITS REASON (kept in step with docs/engine-contract.md §3.5). Pure-function form herd_journal_emission_check <root> for hermetic tests; HERD_JE_VERBOSE=1 dumps every name the scan saw on both sides, so the scan surface itself is inspectable. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh, so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: a tree with no scripts/herd/journal.sh + pysrc/herd (every consuming project) is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_JOURNAL_EMISSION_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 orphan(s) / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the producer/consumer scan surface changes or an event is deliberately dropped. Surface it when a consumer is added for an event, when an emission is being deleted, or when an EMISSION-ORPHAN red needs explaining

name: env-export-lint.sh
description: THE shared shell→python EXPORT guard (HERD-449): herd_env_export_lint [<root>] reds a config knob the Python engine core reads from os.environ (pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's _CORE_ENV_KEYS, imported directly — never a text scrape) that is SET after herd-config.sh sources but not `export`ed — the shape that starved HEALTH_CONCURRENCY/REVIEW_CONCURRENCY: `python3 -m herd.live_runtime --tick` runs as a CHILD process (engine-version.sh:herd_engine_live_tick) and inherits only the EXPORTED shell env, so an unexported knob silently reverts to the engine core's built-in default no matter what .herd/config says. A key that stays completely UNSET (no default line, no project override) is NOT flagged — os.environ.get() reads the identical None whether or not an unset var carries the export attribute. Sources herd-config.sh in an ISOLATED child bash so a project's real .herd/config can never mutate the caller's environment. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: no scripts/herd/herd-config.sh + pysrc in the tree, or no python3, is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_ENV_EXPORT_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 violation / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when a new config knob is added to _CORE_ENV_KEYS or when the shell↔python export contract changes. Surface it when asked what stops a config key from silently defaulting for the python engine core, or when an ENV-EXPORT red needs explaining

name: lever-reachability-lint.sh
description: THE shared INERT-LEVER guard (HERD-556): herd_lever_reachability_lint [<root>] reds a templates/capabilities.tsv config-key row whose ONLY consumers sit inside bash functions the production ENTRYPOINTS cannot reach. Grounded: HEALTH_PANE (HERD-313) and HEALTH_TRUST_BUILDER (HERD-531) were both silent no-ops -- key set, default right, capabilities row written, unit tests green -- because their only consumers hung off `_healthcheck_gate`, defined-but-never-called since the P5b port (HERD-306) moved gate dispatch into pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py. Reachability is TRANSITIVE (roots = every function named at top level in production; edges = every whole-word mention inside a function body), because the grounded chain was reader -> caller -> corpse and a one-hop rule reports clean on it. The scan surface is asymmetric ON PURPOSE: callers count from production only (bin/herd, scripts/herd/**.sh, .herd/*.sh, templates/*.sh) and NEVER from scripts/herd/sim, scripts/herd/experiment or tests -- the sandbox sims call `_healthcheck_gate` directly and stayed green through the whole window production stopped calling it. Deliberately NOT red, and counted in the ADVISORY line instead so the blind edge stays visible: a key with zero consumers anywhere (the caps-sync/doc-drift class) and a PARTIAL key whose live consumer only renders its value into a doc while the behavioral consumer is dead (REVIEW_AUTOFIX today). Opt-out in tests/lever-reachability-exempt.tsv as `<KEY><TAB><reason>`; the reason is mandatory (EXEMPT-MALFORMED) and a row that stops matching a finding reds as STALE-EXEMPT, so the ratchet cannot rot. That file also carries the eight-lever BASELINE found inert the day the guard landed. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH gate surfaces -- scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh -- so they can never disagree. Exit 0 clean / 1 finding / 2 skipped (fail-soft: every CONSUMING project has no capability manifest and skips, never a false red)
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when a new config key needs its consumer chain proven reachable, when a deliberately-unreachable lever needs recording, or when a finding must be traced -- HERD_LR_VERBOSE=1 dumps every dead function, every lever's live/dead consumer counts and every PARTIAL, so the scan surface is inspectable instead of taken on trust

name: hermetic-env-scrub.sh
description: THE shared hermetic-test env scrub (HERD-458): herd_hermetic_env_scrub [<herd-config.sh path>] unsets, in the CURRENT shell, every key herd-config.sh itself `export`s — so a CONFIGURED project's live values (MERGE_POLICY, HEALTH_CONCURRENCY, MAIN_HEALTH_TICK, …), already exported by scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh sourcing herd-config.sh in its own process, never leak past the harness into a hermetic test's `: "${KEY:=default}"` default assertion — the shape that reproduced six false reds (test-cli-reload, test-env-export-lint, test-health-autofix, test-healthcheck-gate, test-main-health-invariant, test-main-health-slot-priority) on this repo's own configured .herd/config. herd_hermetic_scrub_keys [<path>] is the pure-function form: a TEXT scan (never sources — a project's real .herd/config runs arbitrary shell) of every `export …` statement in the file — plain, multi-name, backslash-continued, or a guarded `cond && export NAME` — comment prose using the English word "export" excluded, so the derived key set can never drift from herd-config.sh's own export surface (no hand-maintained list to edit when a future PR adds a new export). Sourced (never executed) by tests/herd.bats (`setup()`, per test), .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate, once before the suite) and scripts/ci/run-suite.sh (the direct-invocation/CI chokepoint) — three independent entry points into the same hermetic suite, so none of them can leak the ambient export surface past the others. Fail-soft: a missing herd-config.sh path is a silent no-op (empty set), never a crash
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when a hermetic test needs to assert a NEW config key's default, or when a false red traces back to a CONFIGURED project's live value leaking into a test

name: doc-drift-lint.sh
description: THE shared doc-drift guard (HERD-168 / extends HERD-96; HERD-254 templates/*.tmpl extension): herd_doc_drift_lint [<root>] reds when README.md, docs/*.md, or templates/*.tmpl references a `herd <subcommand>` (or README references a CONFIG_KEY-shaped token) absent from templates/capabilities.tsv — the docs-drift analog of the conformance / caps-sync ratchet. Phantom commands in templates are MORE damaging than in a doc: coordinator.md.tmpl renders into every seat's operating instructions. Command-position scoped extraction (inline code + fenced command lines, `#` comments stripped; `{{...}}` placeholders stripped so template tokens never false-red) so English prose never false-reds. Sourced (never executed) by scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile and by tests/test-doc-drift.sh (the hermetic unit proof the heavy suite wraps via herd.bats), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: no capabilities.tsv / no python3 / no README-docs-or-tmpl surface → SKIP with $HERD_DOC_DRIFT_SKIP_REASON, never a red. Exit 0 clean / 1 drift / 2 skipped. SHIP-DORMANT: a clean tree exits 0
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the doc↔manifest drift rule changes

name: console-section.sh
description: THE shared bounded-console-section helper (HERD-243): one implementation of how an append-only ledger becomes a console section that AGES OUT. herd_console_visible_lines/herd_console_section render the newest N still-relevant rows (a classifier marks each row calm|loud: calm rows leave the display after CONSOLE_ROW_RETENTION=2h, LOUD rows — a FAILED tracker heal — never age out while unresolved); herd_console_acked hides a row whose verbatim ledger line sits in an ack sidecar (`herd notes ack`); herd_console_trim tail-keeps every ledger FILE at CONSOLE_LEDGER_MAX=20 rows on write. Sourced (never launched) by agent-watch.sh (build_tracker_drift + build_builder_notes), tracker-state-sweep.sh (heal-ledger trim) and bin/herd (`herd notes`), so no surface can disagree. Display-only + fail-soft: an unparseable epoch or clock skew SHOWS the row, and the journal is never touched
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the console's age-out / ack / ledger-bound rules change, or when a NEW append-only ledger needs a bounded console section

name: red-ledger.sh
description: THE shared RED-ROW LEDGER + RECHECK-CADENCE helper (HERD-539): one keyed TSV ledger (<key>\t<class>\t<first-seen>\t<last-verified>\t<why>) that any red-row class can note()/get()/clear() against, plus herd_red_ledger_recheck_due, which lifts reconcile_main_health's inline cadence test (age >= N minutes) into a reusable predicate. herd_red_ledger_note caches the SAME text a caller journals at diagnosis time, so a row's rendered 'why' is provably the diagnosing excerpt, not a second guess; herd_red_ledger_row_suffix renders it back as ' · verified Xm ago'. herd_red_ledger_clear removes the row and journals ONE red_cleared key=<k> reason=<reason> event. Wired today into MAIN RED (main_health:<sha>) and the 'unlinked merges' alarm (ref_unparsed:<pr>, which had NO clear mechanism before this). herd_red_ledger_engine_shaped (HERD-547, HERD-539 leg 4) is the routing-rule classifier a caller offers a noted why-text to — true iff it names herdkit's own engine surface (bin/herd, scripts/herd/**, pysrc/herd/**, …) — that agent-watch.sh's RED_AUTOESCALATE lever uses to decide whether a red auto-escalates via `herd report`; pure string match, no gate of its own. Sourced (never launched) by agent-watch.sh and work-units/git-pr.sh; reuses console-section.sh's _console_now_epoch/CONSOLE_LEDGER_MAX (self-sources it if not already loaded, so the library is standalone-testable). Every function self-gates on RED_LEDGER=off (default) → pure no-op: no file, no journal line, empty reads
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when a NEW red-row class needs a why+last-verified cache and a recheck cadence, or when the ledger's storage shape changes

name: pr-ref.sh
description: THE shared `Refs:` PARSER (HERD-522, GH #637): one implementation of "given a PR body, print its explicit tracker ref", plus the silent-miss probe the reconcile alarms on. Replaces four independent copies of the regex — merge-time reconcile (work-units/git-pr.sh via agent-watch.sh), sweep.sh's retroactive-linkage leg, stale-dup-gate.sh and tracker-state-sweep.sh — three of which claimed in a comment to MIRROR the first and had already drifted (the stale-dup copy never stripped trailing punctuation). herd_pr_ref_from_body reads a body on stdin and prints the ref; HERD_PR_REF_PY is the python half the `gh pr list --json` callers prepend to their own driver; herd_pr_ref_unparsed_line is the SILENT-MISS probe. Matching is decoration-TOLERANT: a heading (`## Refs: X`), list item, blockquote or bold-wrapped (`**Refs:** X`) ref parses, which the column-0 anchor missed — emberglen-godot PR #125 shipped `## Refs: EMG-111`, reconciled to nothing and left its tracker item open with zero warning while 29 sibling PRs passed. Pure widening: every body that matched before matches identically. HTML comment blocks are stripped FIRST (a PR-template example ref would otherwise poison every untracked PR), trailing punctuation is stripped, and `<...>`/none/n/a are placeholders, not refs. NO SHAPE TEST by default — what counts as an identifier belongs to the backend (the default `file` backend's ref IS a title slug) — NARROWED by HERD-613 for the backends that DO have one fixed shape: pr_ref_shape_ok/herd_pr_ref_shape_ok reject a token that fails linear/jira's TEAM-NUMBER shape or github's optional-hash-digits shape under the ACTIVE $SCRIBE_BACKEND, routing it to the silent-miss alarm instead of ever letting it flow into the tracker-heal loop as a literal ref (PRs 712/719: a comma-joined list of failing TEST FILENAMES parsed clean pre-HERD-613 and sat forever as an unresolvable ESCALATED console row). pr_ref_find_in_text/herd_pr_ref_find_in_text is the inverse helper — pulls a real id out of free-form text (a backend create call's own URL/identifier output), used by agent-watch.sh's MAIN_HEALTH_AUTOFIX=spawn leg to thread a synchronously-created item's REAL ref instead of ever fabricating one from a failing-test identity. Sourced (never launched); fail-soft, and without python3 it degrades to the grep/sed pass (shape guard included) rather than dropping every explicit ref onto the fuzzy path
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the `Refs:` convention widens again (a new decoration, a second keyword), when a backend's tracker-id shape changes, or when a NEW surface needs to read a PR's tracker ref — add the caller here rather than a fifth regex. Surface it when a merged PR's tracker item stays open despite a visible Refs: line, when explaining an 'unlinked merges' console row, or when a garbage `Refs:` value is somehow still resolving instead of alarming

name: watcher-exempt.sh
description: THE shared WATCHER-IDENTITY check (HERD-266): the ONE place the engine decides whether an argv0-tagged pid is a watcher MAIN or just one of the canonical watcher's own forks. watcher_list_mains enumerates the mains (lockfile pid when alive, union every process whose argv0 is EXACTLY $HERD_WATCH_ARGV0) minus three exemption clauses: (1) MARKER-OWNED — a live .review-inflight-* / .health-inflight-* / .spawn-inflight-* worker (HERD-185/217/237/245); (2) CHILD-OF-CANONICAL — ppid equals the lockfile watcher; (3) PARENT-OF-GATE-WORKER — a reparented fork still parenting a live healthcheck.sh / herd-review.sh / herd-feature.sh / herd-quick.sh / herd-resolve.sh. Before this, bin/herd's _list_project_watchers exempted only clause (1) while sweep.sh's sweep_stray_watchers exempted (1)(2)(3) — so a sub-second tick fork (every fork inherits the argv0) made `herd status` alarm '2 watcher mains alive' on a healthy control room. Both seats plus status.sh's alarm now read the same answer from this file. Also owns the SELF-RESTART GENERATION HANDOFF marker (watcher_handoff_begin/_clear/_active, TTL-bounded): during a WATCHER_SELF_RESTART exec the alarm is suppressed but the pids stay LISTED, so `herd reload` can still stop the watcher. A GENUINE orphan duplicate — parent dead, no gate child, no marker, no handoff — is still listed and still alarmed. Every probe reads the process table through watcher_ps_table (the $HERD_SWEEP_PS_CMD seam), once per listing, so argv0 match and parent/child exemptions resolve against ONE snapshot
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced (never launched) by bin/herd, sweep.sh, status.sh and agent-watch.sh; the seam to change when a NEW kind of watcher fork must be exempted from the duplicate-watcher count, or when the handoff window's semantics change

name: context-guard.sh
description: THE ONE shared INVOCATION-CONTEXT check (HERD-269): the single place the engine decides whether a `herd` subcommand is allowed to ACTUATE the control room from where it was invoked. A builder worktree carries the SAME committed .herd/config as the main checkout — same PROJECT_ROOT, same HERD_WATCHER_LOCK, same panes — so `herd config set` + `herd reload` run from a builder's tree rebuilt the operator's control room and killed the live watcher mid-run (the grounding incident). herd_context_guard is called ONCE from bin/herd's dispatch, before any command body: when the cwd is NOT the main checkout — clause (A) a git LINKED worktree (`git rev-parse --git-dir` != `--git-common-dir`), or clause (B) a tree inside $WORKTREES_DIR (catches a plain copy) — the enumerated ACTUATOR set REFUSES loudly with exit 3 and a message naming the cwd, the blast radius, and what to do instead. The actuator set: config set, theme set (delegates to config set), governance apply (same), backend switch, reload, pane, sweep, update, upgrade, agent-update. Every READ-ONLY subcommand (status, log, why, backlog, notes, config get|list|lint|sync, doctor, codemap, conformance, cost, stats, render, help, …) is untouched — builders legitimately read control-room state. Per-SUBCOMMAND, never per-flag: `config get` passes where `config set` refuses. Escape hatch HERD_ALLOW_CONTROL_MUTATION=1 permits the actuator, WARNS, and journals a control_mutation_bypass event; a refusal journals control_mutation_refused, so the coordinator sees either within a watcher tick. BYTE-INERT from the control room: neither clause can fire at PROJECT_ROOT, so output, argv and journal are identical to before the guard
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced (never launched) by bin/herd; the seam to change when a NEW herd subcommand mutates control-room state (add it to _herd_context_is_actuator — never a per-command guard copy), or when a builder tree gains a shape neither clause (A) nor (B) recognizes

name: LINEAR_TEAM_ID
description: Optional Linear team id (HERD-474, GH #582) that scopes the linear backend (backends/linear.sh): new issues file under it, and herd backlog's open-issue list is filtered to it, so a Linear workspace shared with other teams' trackers never leaks their issues into this project's backlog. Deliberately does NOT scope issue-ref resolution (mark_shipped, claim, release, update_state, item_state) — those resolve by the identifier's own team prefix (e.g. HERD-5 resolves against team HERD), so a cross-team dependency reference still resolves correctly regardless of this setting. Unset (default) is byte-identical to pre-HERD-474 behavior: new issues file to the first team the API key can see, and the open list spans every team the key can see. Settable via herd config set LINEAR_TEAM_ID <id> (committed .herd/config) or alongside LINEAR_API_KEY in .herd/secrets — .herd/secrets is sourced after .herd/config, so a value there wins if both are set
when_to_surface: When a Linear workspace hosts more than one team's or project's issues under the same API key, so herd backlog and new-issue creation should be scoped to just this project's team instead of every team the key can see

name: SCRIBE_LINGER_SECS
description: Backlog-drainer linger window in seconds (HERD-88): after the scribe empties the queue, `scribe-step.sh next` keeps polling this many extra seconds before returning EMPTY so the drainer session stays alive across idle gaps between requests, letting a burst share ONE MODEL_SCRIBE session instead of paying a fresh cold-start per gap. Default 0 → today's behavior byte-identical (next's total wait stays == SCRIBE_POLL); suggest 90. A request enqueued during the linger is claimed by the same session; single-drainer mkdir-mutex semantics are unchanged
when_to_surface: Set to cut scribe cold-start cost when backlog updates arrive in bursts with short gaps (e.g. a merge burst enqueuing several reconciles); leave 0 for byte-identical legacy behavior

name: SCRIBE_POLL
description: Backlog-drainer base poll window in seconds (scribe-step.sh): how long `scribe-step.sh next` waits for a queued request before returning empty; SCRIBE_LINGER_SECS extends this across idle gaps in a burst. Default 25.
when_to_surface: Raise to reduce scribe cold-starts on a bursty queue; lower for snappier drain latency.

name: RESEARCH_POLL
description: Research-drainer base poll window in seconds (research-step.sh): how long `research-step.sh next` waits for a queued research request before returning empty. Default 25.
when_to_surface: Raise to reduce researcher cold-starts on a bursty queue; lower for snappier latency.

name: DRAINER_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT
description: Drainer singleton liveness window in seconds (HERD-109). The scribe and researcher drainers are per-project singletons: an enqueue that finds a same-named drainer in `herdr agent list` normally short-circuits and spawns nothing — a liveness blind spot, since a LISTED but HUNG drainer (wedged claude session / stuck step) then blocks the queue forever. When set, scribe-step.sh / research-step.sh heartbeat on every drain step (and each poll iteration); if the enqueue path finds a running drainer whose heartbeat is staler than this, it treats it as HUNG, RECLAIMS the singleton and spawns a FRESH drainer. The queue's atomic per-request claim (`.req`→`.req.mine`) prevents double-draining. Default 900 (15 min) — far above any legitimate single drain step, so a healthy drainer is never falsely reclaimed and behavior is byte-identical; 0 DISABLES liveness reclaim (pure legacy behavior); non-numeric → off. An ABSENT heartbeat is treated as alive (fail-soft)
