when_to_surface: Leave at the 900 default in almost all cases; lower it only if a hung drainer must be reclaimed faster (at more risk of reclaiming a legitimately slow drainer), or set 0 to disable liveness reclaim entirely

name: BACKLOG_VIEW_EXTRAS
description: View-only backlog-pane extra section: "" (default, off → pane byte-identical to today) | github-issues. When github-issues, the backlog viewer renders a SECOND, clearly-labeled '📥 incoming (github issues)' section BENEATH the primary work queue listing this repo's open GitHub issues (the herd-report incoming inbox) via `gh issue list`. Strictly ADDITIVE display: never merged into the primary list, never feeds `herd backlog` or coordinator work-selection (SCRIBE_BACKEND stays the single source of truth); fails SOFT on any gh error with a quiet 'incoming unavailable' note, never a red row. Applied on the backlog pane's next launch (herd pane backlog / herd reload)
when_to_surface: Set to surface this repo's open GitHub issues as an incoming inbox beneath the live work queue, without letting them enter planned-work selection

name: SHARE_LINKS
description: Space-separated dirs to symlink into each new worktree (e.g. node_modules target)
when_to_surface: When worktrees need large shared dirs that should not be duplicated on disk

name: MODEL_COORDINATOR
description: Claude model for the coordinator agent (default: claude-opus-4-8)
when_to_surface: Override to trade cost for quality on coordination tasks

name: MODEL_FEATURE
description: Claude model for full feature lane agents (eco-leaning starter default: claude-sonnet-4-6; Opus is now an ESCALATION tier reached via MODEL_ESCALATE_GLOB, not a default)
when_to_surface: Override when a different model tier is preferred for feature implementation; an explicit key always beats the starter default

name: MODEL_QUICK
description: Claude model for quick lane agents (eco-leaning starter default: claude-haiku-4-5, the cheapest tier)
when_to_surface: Override for lightweight task agents; an explicit key always beats the starter default

name: MODEL_SCRIBE
description: Claude model for the async backlog scribe drainer (default: claude-sonnet-4-6)
when_to_surface: Override for backlog editing tasks

name: MODEL_RESEARCH
description: Claude model for the async researcher drainer (default: claude-sonnet-4-6)
when_to_surface: Override for repo research tasks

name: MODEL_REVIEW
description: Claude model for the adversarial pre-merge review gate (eco-leaning starter default: claude-sonnet-4-6; Opus is now an ESCALATION tier reached via REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB, not a default)
when_to_surface: Override when a different model tier is preferred for correctness review; an explicit key always beats the starter default

name: MODEL_RESOLVER
description: Claude model for the isolated conflict-resolver agent (default: claude-sonnet-4-6)
when_to_surface: Override for conflict resolution; resolvers do mechanical merge work, so a cheaper tier is usually fine

name: MODEL_ADVISE
description: Claude model for the `herd advise` one-shot mid-flight advisor (HERD-101): the strong tier a builder pulls a second opinion from without escalating its whole lane (default: the resolved MODEL_FEATURE tier — Opus under standard TOKEN_MODE, sonnet under eco). Set explicitly to pin the advisor to a specific strong model regardless of the feature tier; an explicit key always beats the default
when_to_surface: Override to point the mid-flight advisor at a different (usually strong) model than the feature lane uses, or to keep it on Opus while the feature lane runs a cheaper tier

name: TOKEN_MODE
description: Token-budget mode: standard (default) | eco. eco flips the BUILT-IN model defaults to cheaper tiers (coordinator/feature→claude-sonnet-4-6; quick/scribe/research/resolver→claude-haiku-4-5; review→claude-sonnet-4-6). An explicit MODEL_* key in .herd/config ALWAYS beats eco — eco replaces built-in defaults only, never a user override
when_to_surface: Opt in to cut engine token cost. Tradeoffs: the review gate on sonnet may miss subtle logic bugs; the feature builder on sonnet is weaker on complex multi-file work; haiku is fine for mechanical scribe/resolver work. Composes with the model step-up item, which escalates FROM whatever tier eco sets

name: APP_PREVIEW_CMD
description: Shell command to launch the live app preview pane (blank = no preview pane)
when_to_surface: For projects with a runnable app; blank restricts lanes to herd-quick.sh only

name: APP_PREVIEW_SERVER_ARGS
description: Extra launch args appended to $APP_PREVIEW_CMD for the preview server, with a literal {port} token substituted by the chosen port (default: --server.port {port} --server.headless true, reproducing today's dev-server flags exactly); set "" for a command that needs no injected flags (it reads $PORT itself or takes the port another way)
when_to_surface: Set for a non-web-framework preview command (a CLI, a Go/Node/Rust server, java -jar) that the default dev-server flags would crash; leave unset to keep an existing web app byte-for-byte unchanged

name: APP_PREVIEW_HEALTH_CMD
description: Preview health-probe command, run with PORT exported; exit 0 = 🟢 serving. Highest-precedence probe: overrides APP_PREVIEW_HEALTH_PATH when set; empty (default) falls through to the HTTP path probe
when_to_surface: Set for a CLI / gRPC / non-HTTP or non-root-path preview that a curl GET / can never verify

name: APP_PREVIEW_HEALTH_PATH
description: HTTP path curled at http://localhost:$PORT<path> for the preview health probe; HTTP 200 = 🟢 serving (default: /, reproducing today's probe). Set "" to DISABLE the HTTP probe — with no APP_PREVIEW_HEALTH_CMD either, health renders ⚪ unknown, never a false-red 🔴
when_to_surface: Set a non-root path for a web app whose / is not a 200, or "" to silence a false-red on a non-HTTP preview

name: APP_PREVIEW_PORT_BASE
description: Base of the free-port search range the feature/resolver lanes scan for the app-preview server (they try base..base+98; default: 8501, reproducing today's 8501-8599 block); non-numeric falls back to 8501
when_to_surface: Set to an app's own port convention (e.g. 8080, 3000) so the preview binds where its stack expects; consumed by herd-feature.sh + herd-resolve.sh

name: HEALTHCHECK_CMD
description: Project health command: exit 0 clean, exit 1 code error, exit 2 data/env tolerated. herd init seeds .herd/healthcheck.project.sh from the template matching scout's detected stack (Go/Rust/Java/Node/Python), UNLESS PROJECT_ARCHETYPE is research-lab/docs, which always seeds healthcheck.docs.sh regardless of detected language
when_to_surface: Required for the heavy healthcheck profile; blank falls back to bash -n syntax check only

name: PROJECT_ARCHETYPE
description: The PROJECT ARCHETYPE axis (HERD-409): what KIND of project this is, orthogonal to the operating postures (who merges). code (default) — a codebase with a test/lint suite; the seeded healthcheck is chosen from scout's detected language, byte-identical to pre-HERD-409 init. research-lab | docs — no runnable app or test suite; herd init always seeds healthcheck.docs.sh (markdown fenced-block + relative-link + template-conformance lint) and the interview skips the APP_PREVIEW_CMD question. Named archetypes + intents come from templates/archetypes.tsv (via scripts/herd/sim/archetype-lib.sh), the archetype axis's single source of truth, offered at herd init time
when_to_surface: Set at herd init time via the archetype interview (defaults code, byte-identical); herd config set changes the recorded value but does NOT retroactively re-seed the healthcheck template — reseed by hand for an existing project

name: HEALTHCHECK_HEAVY_GLOB
description: Egrep pattern of diff paths that force the heavy profile; blank (default) means every change is heavy
when_to_surface: When only certain changed files need the full test suite — match your own layout (e.g. ^app/, ^cmd/|^internal/, ^src/); leave blank if unsure

name: HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS
description: Bounds the bats intra-suite worker fan-out (HERD-463) in herdkit's OWN .herd/healthcheck.project.sh: `_hk_suite_workers()` reads this, floors it at 1, clamps it to the box's own core count (nproc/hw.ncpu/getconf, never oversubscribed), then passes it as `bats --jobs N` when GNU parallel is on PATH; <=1 stays strict serial (no --jobs flag at all, byte-identical to pre-HERD-463). Non-numeric or unset → default 4. A DOGFOOD-ONLY env knob (HERD-497 sweep), not a .herd/config key: each project's .herd/healthcheck.project.sh is seeded per-stack by `herd init` (Go/Rust/Java/Node/docs/python each get their own template), so this lever is specific to HERDKIT'S OWN copy, not the shared engine surface capabilities.tsv otherwise documents
when_to_surface: Set with a plain `export HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS=N` before running .herd/healthcheck.project.sh or scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh — a bare subprocess call, so the export is inherited unmodified and the HERD-458 hermetic-env-scrub never eats it (it only unsets herd-config.sh's OWN exported keys, and this is not one) — to raise or clamp the local heavy-suite's bats fan-out on a bigger/smaller box. Not yet wired as a `herd config set` key; the operator's current .herd/config.local workaround (a raw `export HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS=10`) could convert to a front-door herd-config.sh default in a follow-up

name: HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_TIMEOUT
description: Outer `timeout -k 15 N` wall-clock bound (seconds) around the whole `bats tests/*.bats` invocation in .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (HERD-185); a hit is reported as an infra hang ("suite timed out"), never a code error. Default 1800s (30 min) when unset; passed straight to `timeout`, unsanitized, so a non-numeric override fails at the shell/timeout level rather than silently falling back. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep)
when_to_surface: Raise on a box where the full suite genuinely needs longer than 30 minutes; lower to fail faster on a suspected wedge

name: HERD_SHELLCHECK_RETRY_SECS
description: Settle delay (seconds) before ONE retry of an empty-output nonzero shellcheck exit (HERD-421) — an empty nonzero is presumed a transient race (e.g. a concurrent script rewrite mid-read), never trusted as a real finding on the first empty-nonzero run; red only if the retry also fails empty. Non-numeric or unset → default 2. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep)
when_to_surface: Set 0 in a hermetic test fixture to skip the wait deterministically; raise only if shellcheck's transient race window is provably longer than 2s on a given box

name: HEALTHCHECK_BATS_REAP_GRACE
description: Grace period (seconds) the early-reap poll (`herd_bats_early_reap`, scripts/herd/bats-fd3-guard.sh, HERD-462) waits once every planned bats test has reported in the TAP stream but the wrapper process is still wedged (a leaked test child holding bats' own internal fd well after tests finished) before declaring the suite "reaped-wedged" and tearing down the timeout wrapper's whole process group — far sooner than waiting out the full HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_TIMEOUT backstop. Non-numeric or unset → default 15. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep)
when_to_surface: Lower to reap a wedged bats wrapper sooner (at more risk of reaping a suite still writing its final TAP lines); raise if HERD-462 false-reaps a suite that was genuinely still finishing

name: HERD_LEAKGUARD_SETTLE_SECS
description: Settle delay (seconds) the tab-leak guard (`_hk_orphans`, HERD-93/HERD-115) waits before re-snapshotting a detected orphan tab; a leak found on the settle re-snapshot is presumed real — transient control-room churn (a tab caught mid-spawn/mid-reap) clears within the window, while a genuinely leaked, agent-less tab persists and re-trips. Non-numeric or unset → default 4. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep)
when_to_surface: Raise if the tab-leak guard still false-reds on a very busy control room where tab churn takes longer than 4s to settle; lower for a snappier guard on a quiet box

name: HEALTHCHECK_BATS_FILTER
description: HERD-498 targeted retry-before-red: when set, .herd/healthcheck.project.sh passes it straight through as `bats --filter <value>` and forces the bats invocation SERIAL (never --jobs), instead of running the full tests/*.bats suite. The health worker (agent-watch.sh's _health_worker) is the ONLY setter — on a reproducible bats TAP failure it re-invokes healthcheck.sh for the solo retry with this set to an ERE alternation naming exactly the failing test(s) (_health_bats_retry_filter), and explicitly clears it (empty, not merely unset) on every OTHER invocation so an ambient value can never silently narrow the first/untargeted run. Unset (every caller except that solo retry) is byte-identical to before this lever existed. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep) — specific to herdkit's OWN .herd/healthcheck.project.sh copy, not a shared engine surface knob
when_to_surface: Not intended to be set by hand — it is an internal retry-targeting signal the health worker manages; a manual `export HEALTHCHECK_BATS_FILTER=<regex>` before a local `.herd/healthcheck.project.sh` run is useful only to reproduce a specific failing test without waiting on the full suite

name: HEALTHCHECK_PROGRESS_LOG
description: HERD-494: cross-file env-passthrough contract for a tailable live-progress companion file, not a .herd/config knob. The health worker (agent-watch.sh's _health_worker) sets it to the health log's own path as an env prefix around its healthcheck.sh invocation; healthcheck.sh's run_heavy() tees the heavy suite's raw output into it (truncating it fresh first) so a caller can tail real progress instead of seeing 0 bytes until the whole run exits, and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh separately writes one `suite: N tests` header line into it before the bats run starts (denominator for agent-watch.sh's live k/N counter) plus tests/herd.bats's herd_run_discovered_test appends one per-file completion line to it the instant each discovered test finishes — independent of bats' own --jobs-buffered TAP ordering. Unset (every caller except the health worker) is fail-soft: no header, no tee, no per-test lines, byte-identical to before this lever existed. Same dogfood-only framing as HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS (HERD-497 sweep) — specific to herdkit's OWN .herd/healthcheck.project.sh copy, not a shared engine surface knob
when_to_surface: Not intended to be set by hand — it is an internal live-progress plumbing signal the health worker manages; a manual `export HEALTHCHECK_PROGRESS_LOG=<path>` before a local `scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh --heavy` or `.herd/healthcheck.project.sh` run is useful only to inspect live tail output while the suite is still running

name: BASELINE_AWARE_GATE
description: Baseline-aware healthcheck gate (HERD-190): a heavy code error whose failing tests ALL already fail on the base (origin/main) is treated as INHERITED (a tolerated data/env warning), not a merge-blocking code error, so a fix-PR never deadlocks on a base failure it did not introduce. Only ever downgrades a red to a warning; byte-identical when the base is green (empty base known-failure set = every PR failure is introduced) and fully fail-soft (an unresolvable/unparseable base blocks exactly as before): on (default) | off
when_to_surface: Leave on so ungated base failures never deadlock the fix-PRs that clean them up (herdkit enables it); set off to force the classic absolute pass/fail gate. The watcher passes the base checkout as HERD_BASELINE_DIR=$MAIN so no throwaway worktree is created

name: APP_SURFACE_GLOB
description: Egrep pattern of diff paths that constitute the app surface; blank (default) disables the interaction gate with zero behavior change
when_to_surface: Set for projects with an interactive app (e.g. ^app/) so the healthcheck can gate or flag widget→output interaction tests on app-facing PRs

name: INTERACTION_TEST_CMD
description: Command that drives an input and asserts the dependent output changed (exit 0 clean, 1 code error, 2 data/env); framework-neutral — e.g. a UI test harness that sets a value, re-runs, and asserts the output moved
when_to_surface: Set alongside APP_SURFACE_GLOB so an app-surface PR is gated on real interactivity; when APP_SURFACE_GLOB matches but this is blank the healthcheck emits a loud warning that a render smoke cannot see widget→output causality

name: ATTRIBUTION_POLICY
description: Commit-attribution lint policy (HERD-121): '' (default off — lint absent, output byte-identical) | no-ai-coauthor. When no-ai-coauthor, the healthcheck scans the PR's commits (git log <DEFAULT_BRANCH>..HEAD) for AI co-author markers (Co-Authored-By: Claude*, 'Generated with Claude' lines) and fails as a code-error naming the offending sha+line. The 'Never co-author Claude' rule in AGENTS.md is advisory prose without this; set no-ai-coauthor to enforce it deterministically at the gate. The commit-walking helper (_herd_attr_scan in scripts/herd/commit-lint.sh) is reusable: the sibling COMMIT_CONVENTION lint sources it next. Ships dormant: default '' → zero behavior change
when_to_surface: Set to no-ai-coauthor to make AI co-authorship a hard healthcheck gate rather than a silently-violable convention

name: COMMIT_CONVENTION
description: Commit-message convention lint (HERD-124): '' (default off — lint absent, output byte-identical) | an egrep pattern. When set, the healthcheck walks the PR's commits (git log <DEFAULT_BRANCH>..HEAD, via the shared _herd_commit_shas helper in scripts/herd/commit-lint.sh that the HERD-121 attribution scan also rides) and requires every commit SUBJECT to match the pattern; a non-conforming subject fails as a code-error naming the offending sha + subject + pattern. Fail-soft: an INVALID regex WARNS and skips the lint (never a false red). Reuses HERD-121's commit-walking primitive rather than duplicating it. Ships dormant: default '' → zero behavior change. E.g. Conventional Commits: '^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|revert)(\(.+\))?!?: .+'
when_to_surface: Set to an egrep pattern (e.g. a Conventional Commits regex) to make commit-message shape a hard healthcheck gate rather than a silently-violable convention; leave empty (default) for byte-identical legacy behavior

name: SMOKE_CMD
description: Optional smoke test run by herd-resolve.sh after a conflict fix before pushing
when_to_surface: When a quick integration check is faster than the full healthcheck during conflict resolution

name: DENY_PATHS
description: Space-separated paths never committed; scribe and lanes are scoped away from these
when_to_surface: For secrets, credentials, or generated dirs that must never reach git (e.g. .herd/secrets)

name: REVIEW_CHECKLIST
description: Repo-relative path to a project risk checklist injected into the pre-merge review gate
when_to_surface: When the review gate should verify project-specific invariants beyond generic correctness

name: COORDINATOR_CMD
description: Slash command name for the rendered coordinator skill (default: /coordinator)
when_to_surface: When the project uses a non-default coordinator command name

name: HERD_DRIVER
description: Driver binding for the coordinator skill's runtime-specific control surface (multiplexer + agent runtime): selects templates/drivers/<name>.driver, whose DRIVER_* incantations are substituted into the coordinator skill at render time via the same token machinery as the other config-driven values. Four production drivers ship — herdr-claude (herdr multiplexer + Claude Code runtime; the default, which renders the skill functionally identical to before the abstraction), headless (no herdr panes — agents run detached and the watcher/journal/notifications run headless, for Windows/CI/headless Linux), codex (herdr mux + OpenAI Codex CLI runtime — the DRIVER_AGENT_* exec surface rebound to `codex`), and grok (herdr mux + xAI Grok Build CLI runtime — rebound to `grok`) — plus stub, a non-Claude PROOF/REFERENCE driver (HERD-177) proving the portability seam runs a non-Claude runtime end-to-end (not for production; use codex/grok). An unknown value fails the render loudly, listing the available drivers
when_to_surface: When adopting a non-herdr/non-Claude runtime for the coordinator control surface (list/focus/send-to agents); leave unset or herdr-claude for today's exact behavior

name: HERD_VERSION
description: Engine contract version pinned in .herd/config; herd upgrade reads and bumps this value
when_to_surface: Internal version pin; a mismatch triggers a warning on upgrade

name: HERD_REPO
description: GitHub repo where engine bugs escalate via herd report (e.g. owner/herdkit)
when_to_surface: Required for github-backed herd report: unset ⇒ it REFUSES rather than defaulting to a stranger's repo (only the herdkit engine repo self-targets)

name: TRACKER_REPO
description: GitHub repo (owner/repo) the work-tracker backend (backends/github.sh) files/lists/updates/closes items in — a SEPARATE key from HERD_REPO (HERD-534 / GH #651: the backend used to inject -R $HERD_REPO on every gh issue verb, so a project's own backlog silently filed onto its escalation target instead). The backend never falls back to HERD_REPO. Unset (default) ⇒ no -R flag is passed at all; gh resolves the repo from the CWD's origin remote, byte-identical to a project whose origin IS its tracker
when_to_surface: Set only when the work-tracker repo differs from this project's own origin remote (a tracker-only repo separate from the code repo); leave unset for the common case

name: HERD_BRAND
description: Display brand shown in user-facing doctor/preflight diagnostics (herd-preflight.sh); a consumer who has branded their own workflow sees THEIR name instead of the literal WORKSPACE_NAME. Defaults through WORKSPACE_NAME (then 'herdkit'), so unset output is byte-unchanged.
when_to_surface: Set when the display brand should differ from the workspace name.

name: WATCHER_AUTOMERGE
description: Legacy boolean lever (true/false); superseded by MERGE_POLICY when set
when_to_surface: Prefer MERGE_POLICY; kept for backwards compatibility with pre-v1 configs

name: MERGE_POLICY
description: Merge gate policy: auto (watcher merges on pass) | approve (coordinator approval required) | observe (watcher never merges)
when_to_surface: Primary merge control lever; when approve, coordinator uses herd-approve.sh to sign off PRs

name: HUMAN_VERIFY_POLICY
description: How the watcher treats a PR that declares a HUMAN-VERIFY: block under MERGE_POLICY=auto: hold (default — today's EXACT behavior: sha-keyed approve-style hold released by herd-approve.sh approve) | coordinator (keep the hold but notify loudly and flag it coordinator-actionable, so a coordinator/agent runs the declared steps then approves) | auto (treat the declared steps as informational only — journal + PR-comment them and merge on green gates). Unknown/empty falls back to hold. Honored by agent-watch.sh, surfaced by herd-approve.sh
when_to_surface: Set to coordinator for an auto pipeline where a coordinator/agent executes human-verify steps and signs off, or auto to let a PR's declared steps merge as informational; leave unset/hold (default) to keep every HUMAN-VERIFY PR held for explicit sign-off. Opt-in only, never self-activates; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: MERGE_METHOD
description: git merge strategy used by the watcher: merge | squash | rebase
when_to_surface: Controls how PRs land; merge preserves history, squash condenses, rebase linearizes

name: PR_FLOW
description: How builders open PRs: direct (open ready to merge — default, today's behavior) | draft (builder runs 'gh pr create --draft'; the watcher already holds DRAFT PRs until they are marked ready). Threaded into the LANE RULES text only (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh); an unknown value falls back to direct
when_to_surface: Set to draft to keep new PRs out of the auto-merge path until someone promotes them to ready; leave direct for today's open-ready flow

name: PR_READY_WHEN
description: Who promotes a DRAFT PR to ready-for-review: builder (self, once the healthcheck passes — default) | coordinator | human. Only consulted when PR_FLOW=draft; threaded into the LANE RULES wording only; an unknown value falls back to builder
when_to_surface: Set alongside PR_FLOW=draft to decide who moves a draft to ready (the builder itself, the coordinator, or a human); ignored when PR_FLOW=direct

name: PUSH_GATE
description: Gate-then-upload: hold a FINISHED builder for human review BEFORE anything reaches GitHub. '' (default, off) | human. With human, the builder lane completes work + healthcheck but STOPS before git push / gh pr create, recording a sha-keyed awaiting-push hold (push-gate.sh) the watcher shows as 'ready · awaiting push approval' with the worktree path; herd-approve.sh approve <slug> resumes push + PR creation. A new commit invalidates a prior approval (sha-keyed). Unknown value falls back to off. Complements PR_FLOW=draft (gates AFTER upload) and MERGE_POLICY=approve (gates AFTER review). Threaded into the LANE RULES (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh) and consumed by herd-approve.sh + agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Set to human to require human sign-off on the LOCAL diff before a builder pushes/opens a PR; leave unset/'' for today's open-on-finish flow. Watcher-affecting (console row) so it takes effect on the next watcher restart; opt-in, never self-activates

name: DELETE_BRANCH_ON_MERGE
description: Whether the merged head branch is auto-deleted: true | false (default false — branches are retained, today's behavior). When true the watcher passes --delete-branch to `gh pr merge` on the MERGE_METHOD path (composing with the HERD-156 --match-head-commit sha pin), so a merged feature branch is cleaned up instead of accumulating on the remote.
when_to_surface: Set true to have merged feature branches deleted automatically instead of accumulating.

name: LOCAL_REVIEW
description: Pre-PR local review mode: none (default) | pre-pr | risk-scoped. pre-pr makes every builder pass a local adversarial correctness review (herd-review.sh --local) before opening its PR. risk-scoped runs that review ONLY when the builder's diff surface (git diff DEFAULT_BRANCH...HEAD --name-only) matches LOCAL_REVIEW_GLOB, so low-risk diffs skip straight to the PR; the watcher's post-PR review gate is unchanged and remains authoritative either way. Consumed by herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh (threaded into the builder task spec)
when_to_surface: Set pre-pr to review every diff locally before its PR, or risk-scoped (with LOCAL_REVIEW_GLOB) to review only engine-risk diffs and skip low-risk ones; leave none to rely solely on the post-PR gate

name: LOCAL_REVIEW_GLOB
description: Egrep pattern of changed-file paths (git diff DEFAULT_BRANCH...HEAD --name-only) that make a LOCAL_REVIEW=risk-scoped builder run the pre-PR local review; a diff touching no matching path skips it and goes straight to the PR. Same egrep semantics as REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB / HEALTHCHECK_HEAVY_GLOB, but a DEDICATED key so the pre-PR risk surface is scoped independently of the post-PR review tiering. Blank (default) → dormant; under risk-scoped an empty or invalid glob fails SOFT (loud warn) to unconditional pre-pr, never to a silent skip. Ignored under LOCAL_REVIEW none/pre-pr
when_to_surface: Set (e.g. '^scripts/herd/|^bin/') alongside LOCAL_REVIEW=risk-scoped to spend pre-PR review quota only on engine-risk diffs; leave blank if not using risk-scoped review

name: CONTEXT_PROVISION
description: Builder context-provisioning surface: a SPACE-SEPARATED list of grounding sources injected into the STABLE region of every spawned builder's task-spec preamble (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh, via herd_context_provision_preamble in herd-config.sh), so builders start GROUNDED instead of re-exploring the repo each session. Empty/unset (default) → NOTHING injected, task specs byte-identical to today. Injected grounding lives entirely in the prompt-cache-shared STABLE prefix (before the per-item Refs trailer), never interleaved with per-task text. Supported sources: codemap → a pointer telling the builder to read the deterministic code map committed at docs/codemap.md (produced by 'herd codemap' — the herdkit engine tree in the engine repo, or the consuming project's OWN language-aware source tree elsewhere, auto-detected) FIRST to orient; symbol-index → a pointer to the function-level def→caller index committed at docs/symbol-index.md (produced by 'herd symbol-index') for jumping to a function's def or its cross-file callers, with its honest-scope caveat that it is a heuristic token scan (same-name defs and dynamic dispatch are ambiguous), not ground truth; agents-md → unlike the pointer sources, INLINES the CONTENT of the repo-root AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md if present) directly into the task spec (via herd_agents_conventions in herd-config.sh) so a runtime that does NOT auto-load CLAUDE.md (grok, codex) still carries the project conventions, not just a pointer it might skip — fail-soft (no such file → nothing inlined, byte-identical) and driver-agnostic (a claude spec and a grok spec stay byte-identical; the grok DRIVER additionally grounds its system prompt from the same helper). Extensible: future sources (project context notes, MCP tool hints) plug in as new tokens; an UNKNOWN token is ignored (forward-compatible), never an error
when_to_surface: Set to 'codemap' to inject a pointer to the committed docs/codemap.md into each builder's task spec so it loads the repo map instead of re-exploring the tree, and/or 'symbol-index' for the committed docs/symbol-index.md function-level def→caller index, and/or 'agents-md' to inline the repo-root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md conventions into every builder's spec (grounds non-Claude runtimes that do not auto-load CLAUDE.md); leave empty (default) for today's byte-identical task specs. Space-separate multiple sources (e.g. 'codemap symbol-index agents-md') as more grounding lanes ship

name: WATCHER_VIEW
description: Watcher lens — narrows WHICH open PRs the console displays/considers each tick: all (default; unset behaves identically to today — every open PR) | mine (only PRs authored by WATCHER_VIEW_AUTHOR, or the resolved gh user) | review-queue (only PRs whose reviewDecision is REVIEW_REQUIRED, i.e. awaiting review) | deps (only PRs carrying the WATCHER_VIEW_DEPS_LABEL label). SELECTION only: it never relaxes a merge gate and can never blind-merge a hidden PR; an unknown value falls back to all with a loud warning
when_to_surface: Set to focus a shared repo's watcher on a subset (your own PRs, the review backlog, or dependency PRs); leave unset/all to watch everything exactly as before

name: WATCHER_VIEW_AUTHOR
description: Filter/identity: only show PRs authored by this GitHub login; also supplies the identity for WATCHER_VIEW=mine (when blank, mine resolves the login via `gh api user`)
when_to_surface: Set to scope the watcher to one author, or to pin the identity for the `mine` lens without a gh lookup

name: WATCHER_VIEW_ASSIGNEE
description: Filter: only show PRs assigned to this GitHub login (ANDs with the lens and other filters)
when_to_surface: Set to watch only PRs assigned to a specific teammate

name: WATCHER_VIEW_LABEL
description: Filter: only show PRs carrying this label (ANDs with the lens and other filters)
when_to_surface: Set to scope the watcher to a single label (e.g. a release train or area label)

name: WATCHER_VIEW_STATUS
description: Filter: only show PRs whose mergeStateStatus equals this value, e.g. CLEAN | BLOCKED | BEHIND | UNSTABLE (ANDs with the lens and other filters)
when_to_surface: Set to focus on PRs in a specific gate state (e.g. only CLEAN, or only BLOCKED PRs needing attention)

name: WATCHER_VIEW_DEPS_LABEL
description: The label the `deps` lens matches on (default: dependencies)
when_to_surface: Override when dependency PRs in your repo use a different label

name: WATCHER_SCOPE
description: Team-mode auto-merge ownership gate: mine (default) | all — since HERD-653 backed by a real `: "${WATCHER_SCOPE:="mine"}"` in herd-config.sh, not just an inline fallback. Narrows WHICH open PRs the watcher may AUTO-MERGE, layered on top of the WATCHER_VIEW lens; a NARROWING gate — it can only ever WITHHOLD a merge, never authorize one the gates (healthcheck + review + re-verify) would deny. mine = today's exact SOLO behavior (auto-merge the operator's own PRs; the ownership probe stays dormant, byte-identical to before). all = team mode: teammates' PRs are DISPLAYED but auto-merge is STRICTLY scoped to PRs owned by WATCHER_OWNER — a teammate's PR shows "not mine — manual" and is NEVER auto-merged even when MERGEABLE+CLEAN+approved. Unknown value falls back to the safe default mine. HERD-653: giving this a real bash default means "absent from the python engine core's environment" can only ever mean a genuine wiring gap (a broken export chain) — the python core fails closed on THAT case (withholds auto-merge, journals scope_unresolved once) rather than degrading permissive, without adding any probe to the solo happy path
when_to_surface: Set to all on a SHARED repo so the watcher displays teammates' PRs but only auto-merges your own; leave unset/mine for a solo install (behavior unchanged). Fail-closed: in team mode an unresolvable owner WITHHOLDS auto-merge

name: WATCHER_OWNER
description: Operator identity (GitHub login) that OWNS auto-merge in team mode (WATCHER_SCOPE=all) AND owns every AUTOFIX_SCOPE=own write rail (HERD-655, independently of WATCHER_SCOPE — resolved every time an autofix rail needs it, not just in team mode). Resolution order: WATCHER_OWNER (explicit) → WATCHER_VIEW_AUTHOR (reuse the lens identity) → `gh api user`; resolved at most once per process. When the identity cannot be resolved, both consumers WITHHOLD for safety (fail-closed — a teammate's PR is never blind-merged, and never auto-healed, on unconfirmed ownership)
when_to_surface: Set alongside WATCHER_SCOPE=all, or simply to pin the AUTOFIX_SCOPE identity without a gh lookup, on any multi-operator repo; unnecessary on a solo install (gh api user resolves the same login the operator already is)

name: WATCHER_IDLE_CADENCE
description: IDLE-CADENCE (HERD-671 leg 2): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). GROUNDED 2026-08-13: three of four watchers on one machine sit idle (zero open PRs, zero local builder worktrees) most of the night yet still pay a REMOTE gh round-trip every ~4s tick — the render leg's `gh pr list` and the Python engine core's own pooled `gh api graphql` discovery both run unconditionally regardless of whether there is anything to look at, and at the next rate-limit window reset all four watchers resumed together and re-drained the shared 5000/hr GraphQL bucket instantly. on -> each tick RECONCILES idleness fresh from two LOCAL, no-gh signals (a fresh `git worktree list` under $WORKTREES_DIR, and the last tick's OWN successfully-fetched open-PR count) and, while BOTH read zero, widens the render leg's `gh pr list` and the engine tick's `gh api graphql` discovery together to WATCHER_IDLE_REMOTE_SECS instead of paying them every tick; the 4s LOCAL render/reconcile loop itself is untouched, repainting from the last-known-good snapshot exactly like the existing TEAM_PRESENCE/adopt/inbox throttles already do for their own ledgers. The countdown resets to zero — remote polling snaps back to full 4s cadence the very next tick — the instant either signal goes non-idle, so a freshly spawned builder or a newly opened PR is never left waiting out a stale window. A skipped engine tick is a quiet no-op, never a fault: the fault streak, the engine-down banner and its notification are all left untouched. off (default) -> byte-identical: both remote legs run every tick exactly as before this key existed. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on for a watcher that is mostly idle overnight (few/no open PRs, sporadic builders) and is contending for a shared GraphQL/REST rate-limit bucket with other watchers on the same machine; leave off (default) for a busy watcher or when the extra polling headroom does not matter. Pairs well with a per-project GH_TOKEN (see GH_TOKEN) when several watchers share one machine.

name: WATCHER_IDLE_REMOTE_SECS
description: The widened remote-leg poll interval in seconds (default 60) WATCHER_IDLE_CADENCE steps the watcher's render/gh pr list and engine/graphql discovery legs up to while genuinely idle; only consulted while that lever is on. A non-numeric or sub-4s value falls back to the built-in 60s. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Raise for a very quiet watcher to shave polling further, or lower toward 4s (the un-widened cadence) if a 60s idle-to-active detection lag is too slow for how this project gets used; unnecessary without WATCHER_IDLE_CADENCE=on.

name: PR_FETCH_UNIFY
description: HERD-675: unify the per-tick PR-list fetch — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). off -> byte-identical: the bash render leg's `_prs_fetch_tick` (`gh pr list --json ...`) and the Python engine core's own `discover_via_graphql` (`gh api graphql`) keep fetching independently every due tick, exactly as before this key existed (HERD-671 pooled/throttled both but deliberately left the two transports separate). on -> `discover_via_graphql` (the richer schema) becomes the FETCH OWNER: every successful graphql discovery writes its raw roster to a tick-scoped, seat-stamped cache file under the worktree pool (`$TREES/.pr-list-cache-<seat>.json`), and `_prs_fetch_tick` reads a projected view of it — skipping its own `gh pr list` round-trip — whenever that cache is still fresh; a missing/stale/malformed cache falls straight back to `_prs_fetch_tick`'s own live fetch, fail-soft. Cross-seat safe: the cache filename is stamped with `herd_engine_seat_id`, so two watchers sharing one worktree pool never clobber each other's roster. Consumed by scripts/herd/work-units/git-pr.sh + pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py
when_to_surface: Turn on to cut a busy multi-watcher pool's remote gh round-trips roughly in half (one PR-list fetch per due tick instead of two); leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior. Pairs with WATCHER_IDLE_CADENCE — both throttle the SAME due-tick gate, this one dedups what happens within it.

name: AUTOFIX_SCOPE
description: Author-scope for every AUTOFIX WRITE RAIL: own (default) | all (HERD-655, GitHub issue #771). GROUNDED (emberglen, two operators): a seat's RESOLVE_AUTOFIX rail adopted the OTHER operator's conflicting PR and dispatched a resolver against his branch — no author/operator filter existed on any autofix rail. Consulted by ONE shared check at every write surface (multi-seat doctrine): RESOLVE_AUTOFIX (resolver dispatch onto a conflicting PR), STALE_BASE_AUTOFIX (merge-up bounce or resolver dispatch onto a stale-base hold), REVIEW_AUTOFIX (re-task bounce on a BLOCK), HEALTHCHECK_AUTOFIX (re-task bounce on a reproduced CODE ERROR). own = the rail fires ONLY on PRs whose author matches the seat's own identity, resolved exactly like WATCHER_OWNER (WATCHER_OWNER → WATCHER_VIEW_AUTHOR → `gh api user`, memoized once per process — never one gh probe per candidate). FAIL-CLOSED: an unresolvable identity, or an author that does not match it, WITHHOLDS the write (never fires blind) and journals `autofix_scope_withheld` (pr, author, rail) so the coordinator sees it without a human pasting a pane. all = today's behavior, explicit opt-in: every rail fires on every PR regardless of author. Unknown value falls back to the safe default own. Read-only rails (gating, health verdicts, console display) are NEVER scoped by this key — only the four write rails named above. SHIP SAFE: default own is zero behavior change on a single-operator repo (every PR is already the operator's own — the identity always matches). Consumed by agent-watch.sh (all four rails' bash spec/tests) and pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (the STALE_BASE_AUTOFIX rail — the only one of the four with a live python consumer today; see docs/multi-operator-ownership.md for which rail's behavioral consumer is bash-live vs python-live vs currently unreachable since the P5b engine port)
when_to_surface: Leave at the default own on ANY repo more than one operator's automation might touch — it costs nothing on a solo install and is the guard that would have prevented the grounding incident. Set to all only to explicitly restore pre-HERD-655 behavior (every autofix rail fires on every PR) — rare, and only when every operator sharing the repo has agreed to it

name: REVIEW_CONCURRENCY
description: Maximum pre-merge reviews the watcher dispatches in parallel (default: 2)
when_to_surface: Raise for review throughput at higher model cost; lower to 1 to serialize reviews

name: SPAWN_AHEAD
description: Advisory spawn-rate lead over the review gate (default: 1). Governs two mechanisms: (1) the lane advisory gate (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh) HOLDS a new builder spawn when the review pipeline is saturated (live+queued reviews ≥ REVIEW_CONCURRENCY) AND in-flight builders already exceed REVIEW_CONCURRENCY + SPAWN_AHEAD — HERD-581 (HERD-557 P2) adds a THIRD reason under CAPACITY_BUDGET=on (the suite ledger is fully contended) and REVIEW_CONCURRENCY+SPAWN_AHEAD also becomes the flat COUNT cap the lane's own agent-class capacity lease (capacity-ledger.sh's 'agent' tenant) leases against before launching the runtime, no new key; (2) the watcher's durable spawn-queue drain (spawn.sh / spawn-step.sh) pops at most REVIEW_CONCURRENCY + SPAWN_AHEAD - active_builders intents per tick, so the queue never feeds faster than the review gate can process. Advisory only: --force / HERD_FORCE_SPAWN=1 bypasses the lane gate and the capacity lease for urgent items
when_to_surface: Keep at 1 to keep one build ahead of the gate so the pipeline stays fed; set 0 for strict no-surplus (never build past REVIEW_CONCURRENCY in-flight while the gate is full); raise to allow a deeper builder lead when review is fast relative to build time

name: INTENT_QUEUE
description: HERD-630 (Phase 1 of HERD-625; design doc docs/spikes/coordinator-work-queue.md): the durable spawn queue's INTENT POLICY — off (default, ship-dormant) | on. GROUNDING: the spawn queue already externalizes spawn EXECUTION but not spawn SELECTION, so a slot freed while the coordinator is between turns is repaired by nobody — 4h36m of idle review slot inside a 7h45m drain on 2026-08-10, bimodally ~30-60s when a coordinator turn happened to be live and 24-144min when one was not. off -> spawn-step.sh's `next` serves intents by the untouched `ls -1 <q>/*.req | sort` FIFO, no .prio sidecar is read, no re-ground read is issued, no intent can expire and no escalation ledger is written: byte-for-byte the pre-HERD-630 drain (tests/test-spawn-queue-drain.sh passes unmodified as the proof). on -> FOUR behaviors over the SAME queue dir and the same claim primitives: (1) PRIORITY ORDER — an optional .prio sidecar (spawn.sh's HERD_SPAWN_PRIO) names a band, lowest drains first, FIFO by INTENT_ID within a band (the HERD-443 invariant); an intent with no sidecar lands in the default band, so a queue where nobody published a priority is STILL today's FIFO and arming the lever alone re-orders nothing; (2) DRAIN-TIME RE-GROUNDING — the item's CURRENT tracker state is re-read (herd-claim.sh's read-only _herd_state_dispatch, the same read the lane's HERD-117 guard performs) before anything is created; a Done/Canceled item is a TERMINAL SKIP-AND-CONTINUE (journal spawn_skipped, drop the candidate, launch the NEXT one in priority order — no worktree, branch or agent); (3) INTENT_TTL AGING — an intent undrained past the TTL escalates instead of launching, with a LOUD needs-you row plus its ack (`herd intents ack`) and automatic age-to-retired sweep in the same slice (HERD-613 LEG 3); (4) the `cancel` op — `spawn-step.sh cancel <intent-id>` countermands a still-unclaimed intent atomically, racing the drain's own claim safely (the loser exits 3). INTENT_TTL itself is an internal constant with an env seam (default 86400s, 0 disables expiry), deliberately NOT a second config key. NOT MULTI-SEAT SAFE and not described as such: each watcher still computes its spawn budget from its own FEATS roster, so two seats draining one pool can each admit up to their own cap — Phase 4 closes that through the HERD-581 `agent` capacity tenant. Unknown value -> off (fail safe). Consumed by scripts/herd/spawn-step.sh and agent-watch.sh (_drain_spawn_queue + the escalation console section)
when_to_surface: Turn on when the coordinator is the throughput bottleneck — a non-empty backlog and idle review slots because spawn SELECTION still waits for a live coordinator turn — and publish bands with HERD_SPAWN_PRIO=<n> so the queue drains most-important-first as slots free; leave off (default) for a single attended seat that spawns interactively, and do NOT rely on it as multi-seat safe until Phase 4 lands

name: HEALTH_CONCURRENCY
description: Maximum healthcheck suites the watcher runs at once (default: 1 = serialize); all feature worktrees share one git object store, so overlapping suites race on shared .git locks and can paint a false-red for a clean PR — the watcher queues a PR ("health-check · queued") until a slot frees
when_to_surface: Keep at 1 unless the project's healthcheck is fully worktree-isolated (no shared object store); raise only if suites provably do not contend

name: LOCAL_SUITE_CONCURRENCY
description: HERD-529: maximum HEAVY healthcheck suites this BOX runs at once, across ALL worktrees and ALL callers — builder-local `scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh --heavy` runs AND the watcher's own dispatch (default: 2). Distinct from HEALTH_CONCURRENCY, which only serializes the watcher's OWN dispatch loop and has no visibility into a builder running the heavy suite locally, ahead of its own PR, in its own worktree. Enforced in healthcheck.sh's run_heavy() via a cross-worktree slot pool under $WORKTREES_DIR, namespaced `.local-suite-slot-*` (restart-safe pid+start-time markers, mirroring HEALTH_CONCURRENCY's own `.health-inflight-*` machinery under a distinct name so the two never collide); a waiter prints "waiting for a local suite slot (n ahead, cap N)" until a slot frees. Also feeds .herd/healthcheck.project.sh's dynamic HEALTHCHECK_SUITE_WORKERS default (max(2, cores / live slot count) when that var is unset)
when_to_surface: Keep at 2 (the default) on a typical dev box; lower to 1 to fully serialize every heavy suite on the box; raise on a big/idle box that can genuinely run more than 2 heavy suites concurrently

name: CAPACITY_BUDGET
description: HERD-557 P1 + HERD-581 P2: evolve LOCAL_SUITE_CONCURRENCY's flat slot cap into a priority-aware LEDGER (scripts/herd/capacity-ledger.sh; design doc docs/spikes/capacity-admission.md): off (default, ship-dormant) | on (yolo posture adopts on). off -> healthcheck.sh's run_heavy() calls the original, untouched `_lss_acquire` flat-cap path, byte-identical to before this key existed, and the lane spawn step / herd-spawn-gate.sh never touch the ledger either. on -> the same unit count is admitted through a reserved-slice partition (one watcher-only unit, one builder-local-only unit, so neither class can starve the other by POSSESSION even under a continuous burst from the other — time-based aging was tried and rejected, see the design doc) plus a RETRY-SOLO drain barrier for the HERD-546 flaky-retry re-run (waits for the whole ledger to drain, holds it alone, or gives up as env-suspect within its window) and an overload breaker (loadavg far past core count freezes admission regardless of ledger room). P2 (HERD-581) adds a SECOND tenant under the same lever: the lane spawn step (herd-feature.sh/herd-quick.sh) leases an 'agent' tenant 'spawn'-class unit (flat COUNT cap = REVIEW_CONCURRENCY+SPAWN_AHEAD, no new key) BEFORE launching the runtime, released liveness-based when the agent session ends; herd-spawn-gate.sh's advisory also defers while the SUITE tenant is fully contended (spawning-into-idleness). The acquire itself is one atomic, non-blocking flock (scripts/herd/capacity_flock_run.py, portable macOS/Linux) tied to the holding process's own fd, so a crashed/killed holder's unit is released by the kernel — no reconciler, no TTL escheat of a live holder. Fail-soft: no worktree pool, no python3, or this key off all fall back to the same untouched flat-cap / gate-only paths. Unknown value -> off (fail safe)
when_to_surface: Turn on (or adopt the yolo posture) on a fleet where watcher-dispatched suites, builder-local suites, and agent spawns genuinely contend for the box and a burst from one class has been seen to starve/slow another; leave off (default) for a quiet box or when the plain flat caps are enough

name: capacity-ledger.sh
description: HERD-557 P1 + HERD-581 P2: THE shared capacity ledger library (design doc docs/spikes/capacity-admission.md), now TWO tenants. SUITE (P1, healthcheck.sh's run_heavy()): capacity_acquire_and_run <tenant> <cap> <class> -- <cmd...> blocks (visible wait lines to stderr, journaled queued/admitted/env-suspect events) until admitted then runs <cmd...> with the unit held, returning its exit status; class: watcher | builder-local | retry-solo. AGENT (P2, the lane spawn step): capacity_agent_lease_reserve <cap> <slug> tries a non-blocking lease for class 'spawn' and backgrounds a detached capacity_agent_lease_hold holder (capacity-agent-lease-wait.sh) that releases + journals capacity_lease_released once the agent session ends; capacity_agent_lease_cap derives the flat count cap from REVIEW_CONCURRENCY+SPAWN_AHEAD (no new key); capacity_suite_queue_saturated lets herd-spawn-gate.sh consult SUITE-tenant contention. Both tenants route through the SAME capacity_candidate_slots comparator (own reserved slice first, then general) and the SAME overload breaker (capacity_overload_high). Gated end-to-end by CAPACITY_BUDGET; every function fails soft to a caller running unslotted/gate-only when the ledger is unavailable
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the reserved-slice sizing rule changes, a new lease class/tenant is added, or the overload-breaker threshold needs tuning

name: capacity_flock_run.py
description: HERD-557 P1: the ATOMIC ACQUIRE-AND-RUN backbone capacity-ledger.sh shells out to — a real, non-blocking flock(2) (Python's fcntl, portable macOS/Linux) on every given lock file, all-or-nothing, tied to THIS process's own file descriptors so a crashed/killed holder's unit is released by the kernel the instant it dies (no reconciler, no TTL, no pid-liveness scan needed for correctness). A single lock file is an ordinary "claim one unit" attempt; the RETRY-SOLO drain barrier passes every unit's lock file at once ("claim the whole ledger or nothing"). Exit 75 = busy (nothing acquired, command never ran); otherwise the command's own exit status
when_to_surface: Internal helper, invoked by capacity-ledger.sh only — not a standalone CLI a human runs

name: capacity-agent-lease-wait.sh
description: HERD-581 (HERD-557 P2): the CMD capacity_agent_lease_hold runs under an admitted 'agent' tenant flock — waits for <slug>'s agent SESSION to go alive (driver-agnostic: herd_driver_agent_liveness, works for both herdr panes and headless detached agents) within a start timeout (HERD_CAPACITY_AGENT_START_TIMEOUT_SECS, default 60s; exit 3 on timeout), then waits for that liveness to STOP for HERD_CAPACITY_AGENT_DEATH_CONFIRM_TRIES consecutive polls (default 3, debounced against a transient herdr hiccup) before exiting 0 — exiting either way is when capacity_flock_run.py's process exit releases the flock
when_to_surface: Internal helper, invoked by capacity-ledger.sh's capacity_agent_lease_hold only — not a standalone CLI a human runs

name: REVIEW_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT
description: Restart-safe review-dispatch timeout in seconds (HERD-185). A pre-merge reviewer runs in the BACKGROUND holding a REVIEW_CONCURRENCY slot via an on-disk inflight marker that records pid + pid-start-time + dispatch timestamp. The every-tick corpse sweep frees that slot the moment the reviewer is a corpse (pid dead/recycled) OR its age — computed FROM THE MARKER'S OWN timestamp, so ANY watcher instance including one that restarted mid-run can enforce it — exceeds this many seconds, in which case the live reviewer is SIGTERMed, an infra_event review_timeout is journaled, and the retry budget is counted. Set well above any legitimate review (Opus ~7 min) so a healthy reviewer is never killed. Non-numeric -> the built-in default. Default 1800 (30 min)
when_to_surface: Lower only if a hung reviewer must be reclaimed faster (at more risk of killing a legitimately slow review); raise for very slow reviewers. Leave at 1800 in almost all cases

name: HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT
description: Restart-safe health-dispatch timeout in seconds (HERD-185). The healthcheck suite now runs ASYNCHRONOUSLY in a background worker holding a HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot via the same restart-safe inflight marker as the review gate. The every-tick corpse sweep frees that slot when the worker is a corpse (pid dead/recycled) OR its marker age exceeds this many seconds, in which case the live suite is SIGTERMed, an infra_event health_timeout is journaled, and the slot is freed for a re-dispatch. A holder pid equal to the watcher itself is never SIGTERMed. Set well above the heaviest suite (main-health runs the full heavy suite). Non-numeric -> the built-in default. Default 1800 (30 min)
when_to_surface: Lower only if a hung suite must be reclaimed faster (at more risk of killing a legitimately slow suite); raise for very slow suites. Leave at 1800 in almost all cases

name: HEALTH_TIMEOUT_HEADROOM
description: Headroom margin in seconds between the observed max suite duration and HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT (HERD-281). When > 0, the every-tick gate-corpse sweep tracks completed-suite wall-clock durations and, when a live suite enters the window [HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT - HEALTH_TIMEOUT_HEADROOM, HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT + HEALTH_TIMEOUT_HEADROOM): (a) surfaces a loud console row + throttled journal advisory (health_timeout_headroom_advisory) to raise HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT, and (b) does NOT SIGTERM the dispatch within that window — giving the suite the full margin to complete before the kill fires. SHIP-DORMANT: 0 (default) → the corpse sweep is byte-identical to before (kills at HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT exactly); the advisory and deferred-kill paths are unreachable. Non-numeric → 0 (never activate on a typo). Fail-soft: a missing or unreadable duration record is treated as zero observed duration (the advisory and deferred-kill paths are suppressed). Set to ~20% of HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT as a starting point (e.g. 360 for the default 1800s timeout). Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Set > 0 when suites reliably run close to HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT and re-dispatches due to premature kills are observed (HERD-281 incident: suite finished CLEAN ~15s after the watcher declared the dispatch dead). The advisory fires continuously while the recorded max observed duration leaves less headroom than this value. Leave at 0 (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: HEALTH_EARLY_REAP_SECS
description: Seconds an in-flight healthcheck suite's tailable log may stay 0 bytes, with no live bats/suite descendant left in its process group, before the every-tick gate-corpse sweep reaps it EARLY instead of waiting out HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT (HERD-494). A suite dead-at-spawn or wedged before ever producing output otherwise sits holding a HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot for the full inflight timeout (many minutes) on a run that will never yield a verdict. A suite that has written ANY bytes, or still has a live descendant, is never touched — only a truly silent, childless worker qualifies. Reaps via the same group-kill seam (_health_terminate_worker) the ordinary timeout branch uses and journals health_early_reap. SHIP-DORMANT: 0 (default) → corpse sweep is byte-identical to before (the early-reap path is unreachable). Non-numeric → 0 (never activate on a typo). Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Set > 0 (e.g. 300 for 5 minutes) when a dead-at-spawn health worker has been observed wedging a HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot for the full HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT with an empty log. Leave at 0 (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: HEALTH_TRUST_BUILDER
description: SHA-MATCHED TRUST of a builder's own pre-PR heavy suite (HERD-531, hardened HERD-560): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> when a heavy healthcheck completes, scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh writes an engine-authored FORMAT VERSION 2 provenance record (version, sha, worktree path, profile, outcome, duration, provenance, tree_state, epoch, log_digest) into the shared worktree pool — plus, only for a CLEAN outcome, a companion suite-log file the digest is taken over — and the watcher's health dispatch, on finding a CLEAN heavy record for a candidate's EXACT head sha from a CLEAN tree at that same worktree whose digest matches the companion log and that is within the freshness window, runs the LIGHT profile as a smoke instead of re-running the full suite and journals health_trusted provenance=builder-local. The console row says 'light smoke (heavy trusted from …)' so a fast green is never mistaken for a full run, and the smoke still produces a real CLEAN/FLAKY/CODEERROR verdict — a red still blocks the merge. FAIL-CLOSED: no record, a pre-HERD-560 or unrecognized-version record (reads ABSENT, never an error), a stale sha, a non-CLEAN outcome, a dirty tree, a mismatched worktree, a record older than HEALTH_TRUST_MAX_AGE_SECS (default 21600s/6h) or older than the commit it claims, a digest mismatch/missing companion log, or a record the watcher itself wrote is a FULL re-run exactly as today. NO SIGNING: the single-tenant threat model is staleness, not forgery. off (default) -> byte-identical: no record is written and none is read. An unrecognized value reads off (a typo can never arm a path that skips the authoritative suite). WRITE side: scripts/herd/health-trust.sh, sourced by healthcheck.sh. READ side (HERD-555): pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's LiveGates.health, a direct port of the same herd_health_trust_check contract — a Python-core knob, so it is exported (_HERD_ENGINE_CORE_KEYS, HERD-449/465) for the `--tick` child process to see it. agent-watch.sh still sources health-trust.sh's read too, but only its bash-parity test/sim surface (_healthcheck_gate) ever calls it — zero production callers since the Python engine port.
when_to_surface: Turn on (set on) once builders reliably run the heavy profile themselves before opening a PR and the watcher's duplicate re-run of the same sha is the gate's dominant wall-clock cost; leave off (default) for a byte-identical gate that always re-runs the full suite itself. Watcher-affecting, takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: HEALTH_SOURCE
description: WHERE the PR health verdict COMES FROM (HERD-578, the CI-AS-GATE lever): local | ci (default local, ship-dormant). local -> unchanged: the watcher dispatches the local healthcheck suite per (pr, sha), serialized behind HEALTH_CONCURRENCY, and that run is the verdict. ci -> the watcher stops dispatching local PR suites entirely and READS the PR's OWN GitHub Actions conclusion for its exact head sha instead — the same suite CI has already run in parallel, at zero local slot cost. FIVE mappings, all decided by ONE shared implementation (pysrc/herd/ci_verdict.py, which agent-watch.sh's main-health CI leg and CI_FAST_BOUNCE leg also read through `python3 -m herd.ci_verdict`, so the three can never disagree): a GREEN checks-run for the head sha -> CLEAN (merges through the ordinary rails); a RED whose failed jobs name a real test (the same run-suite.sh '✗ <test>' honest-identity parse HERD-476 built) -> CODEERROR carrying that test as the bounce evidence, on the SAME kind=health rail (same sha-keyed once-guard, same REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget) a local red bounces on — HEALTHCHECK_AUTOFIX drives it, one rail, never two; PENDING (queued/in-progress) -> WAIT; a CANCELLED-run chain -> WAIT, QUALIFIED with the cancelled count (never a red — a cancel is no signal); CI ABSENT entirely (no Actions run in the window, or an unreachable/unauthenticated gh) -> FALL BACK to the local suite and journal `ci_health_fallback` saying so (never a silent skip, never an invented verdict). TWO HARD RULES FROM LIVE INCIDENTS: (1) HERD-609 — a failure whose failed jobs carry PLATFORM-INFRA signatures (Failed to resolve action download info / Service Unavailable / job not acquired by runner / concurrency cancel) and name NO test classifies WAIT-infra-transient with ONE bounded, journaled `gh run rerun --failed` per run id (plus a global cooldown), and is NEVER a CODEERROR — only a completed run whose failures carry real test output is a code red (grounded: the 2026-08-06 GitHub Actions outage held main red overnight); (2) HERD-612 — the verdict is a per-tick RECONCILED READ of live CI state: no dispatched worker, no marker, no sha-cache, so a tick that dies mid-read costs one re-read and can never strand a verdict (grounded 2026-08-07/10: a dispatched verdict-collector chain died between suite-pass and verdict-write and stranded a MAIN RED for three days). MERGE_RESULT_GATE=on takes precedence (its claim — the suite ran against head MERGED WITH base — is one no branch CI run can attest); that combination journals `ci_health_skipped reason=merge-result-gate` once per (pr, sha) rather than silently ignoring either lever. Builder-local scoped runs stay an opt-in dev tool via healthcheck.sh, unchanged, and trust records/scoping keep today's behavior for HEALTH_SOURCE=local consumers. An unrecognized value reads as local (fail toward the authoritative local suite). off-path guarantee: with the default local, NO gh call, NO ci_* journal event and NO behavior change of any kind. Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (LiveGates.health)
when_to_surface: Set ci in a repo whose GitHub Actions workflow ALREADY runs the same suite the local gate runs, on every PR head sha — then the watcher's health slots (HEALTH_CONCURRENCY) stop being the pipeline's bottleneck and PR gate latency collapses to CI's own wall-clock. Requires a working, authenticated `gh` with Actions read access AND `gh run rerun` write access for the infra-transient auto-rerun; a repo whose CI covers only SOME PRs, or whose workflow is slower/weaker than the local suite, should stay local (the default) — a CI read is only as authoritative as the workflow behind it. Surface it when an operator asks why every PR waits on a local suite while CI has already gone green on the same commit, or when suite capacity (not review latency) is the measured bottleneck

name: CORE_SURFACE_GLOB
description: The LOAD-BEARING CORE gate (HERD-577): an egrep of changed diff paths (repo-root relative) whose diffs must carry a GREEN sandbox-sim scorecard before they may merge, and which merge ONE AT A TIME. EMPTY (the default) = feature OFF, byte-identical -- no diff is read, no sim dispatched, no marker written, no core_surface_* event journaled. GROUNDING (the blast-radius insight): every compound failure this engine has had lives in ~6 load-bearing files -- the gate loop / dispatch / verdict-cache regions of scripts/herd/agent-watch.sh, the decide + health paths of pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py, pysrc/herd/ci_verdict.py, scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh, .herd/healthcheck.project.sh and scripts/herd/herd-review.sh's dispatch -- while 40+ other merges flow through the same gate harmlessly, so a uniform gate spends the same proof budget on a TSV row edit and on a rewrite of the merge decision. ARMED -> two things, BOTH scoped to matching diffs only. (1) SCORECARD LEG: a THIRD gate leg in the decide path requires result=pass from the sandbox-sim scenario(s) covering the touched seam (gate / concurrency / limit / panes, mapped by scripts/herd/core-surface.sh). It is its OWN leg, sequenced after the health verdict and before the reviewer -- NOT a rider on the local suite dispatch -- so it composes IDENTICALLY with HEALTH_SOURCE=local and HEALTH_SOURCE=ci (under ci no local suite is dispatched at all, and a requirement bolted onto that dispatch would silently evaporate). The sim is dispatched async, sha-keyed, nonce-guarded and capped at ONE in flight project-wide, exactly like the health rail; the verdict is cached per head sha so an unchanged commit never re-runs it. A red scorecard bounces on its OWN `coresim` refix rail (same REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget shape, never sharing the health rail's), then escalates needs-you when that budget is spent. (2) SERIALIZE: among core-matching candidates that would merge, only the deterministic front (lowest PR number -- the SAME total order MERGE_QUEUE derives, so the two can never disagree about who merges) lands per window; every other core candidate HOLDS (`core_surface_wait`) with a visible calm console row naming the PR it waits on, and is re-gated against a base that CONTAINS the first once it lands. Non-core diffs are never consulted and never held. FAIL-SOFT NEVER SILENT: an absent scenario script SKIPs loudly (journaled `core_surface_skipped`, verdict SKIP -- never PASS). STRICT the other way: a diff whose paths cannot be read at all is gated AS core (journaled `core_surface_unreadable`) because the scenarios are hermetic and cheap, so being wrong that way costs one ~30s run while being wrong the other way is exactly the merge this gate exists to stop. Same egrep semantics as HEALTHCHECK_HEAVY_GLOB / REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB. Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (LiveGates.core_surface, LiveTick._core_prepass) and scripts/herd/core-surface.sh; a Python-core knob, so it is in _HERD_ENGINE_CORE_KEYS and stays exported (HERD-449/465)
when_to_surface: Arm it once a project can name the handful of files whose breakage is COMPOUND rather than local -- the gate loop, the dispatch/verdict cache, the health decide path, the health command itself. Surface it when a post-mortem finds two individually-green changes that broke the engine together, when a core file has been reverted more than once, or when an operator asks why a one-line TSV edit and a rewrite of the merge decision pay the same gate. Keep it EMPTY in a project with no sandbox-sim rig (the gate would only ever SKIP loudly), and keep it NARROW: every matching PR pays a sim run and gives up parallel merging with other core PRs, which is the point for six files and pure latency for sixty

name: HEALTH_TRUST_MAX_AGE_SECS
description: Freshness bound for a builder-local health-trust provenance record consumed by HEALTH_TRUST_BUILDER (HERD-560). Default 21600s (6h). A CLEAN record older than this many seconds since its epoch is refused regardless of outcome — the world may have moved on (a dependency bump, a config drift landing on default) since the run, and only a fresh suite run would see it. 0/unset stays the pre-HERD-560 unbounded default; a non-numeric override falls back to it too, so a typo can never widen the trust window. Read by scripts/herd/health-trust.sh's herd_health_trust_check, the SAME contract consulted by both agent-watch.sh's bash-parity test surface and pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's LiveGates.health. Inert whenever HEALTH_TRUST_BUILDER is off, since no record is read at all in that state.
when_to_surface: Lower to shrink the window a builder-local heavy run is trusted for (a fast-moving repo where staleness risk is higher); raise to trust older builder-local runs for longer on a slower-moving repo. Watcher-affecting, takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: HEALTH_SUITE_SCOPE
description: DIFF-SCOPED test selection for the heavy suite: diff | full (default full, ship-dormant). full -> the project healthcheck wrapper runs the whole curated set, byte-identical to before. diff -> it maps the worktree's changed paths to the tests that can actually cover them via scripts/herd/suite-shard.sh's herd_suite_tests_for_diff: (1) the gate-coverage pairing convention (tests/test-<name>.sh <-> scripts/herd/<name>.sh, HERD-292), (2) DOCS MAPPING (HERD-733): README.md/docs/**/*.md at any depth (outside tests/) select the enumerated doc-drift/caps-sync/conformance lint tests instead of failing closed — a test that asserts on one SPECIFIC doc's real content (e.g. test-driver-abstraction.sh, test-map.sh) declares its own suite-deps header instead of relying on this rule, (3) an optional per-test '# suite-deps: <path-or-glob>' header for cross-file coverage, and (4) an always-run core of cross-cutting manifest/lint/hermeticity proofs unioned into every selection. FAIL-CLOSED: any non-docs changed path that is unmappable or wide-blast (bin/herd, scripts/herd/herd-config.sh, scripts/herd/agent-watch.sh, either healthcheck wrapper, templates/capabilities.tsv, the selection library itself, the bats discovery surface) selects the FULL curated set — an unprovable diff runs everything, never nothing. When the selection comes back as the whole curated set the allow-list is left unset, so the ordinary full run is reached by exactly the same code path as before. An unrecognized value reads full. Consumed by scripts/herd/suite-shard.sh (herd_suite_scope_mode) and honored by tests/discover-tests.bash
when_to_surface: Set diff when the heavy gate's wall-clock is dominated by tests a small change provably cannot break and the pairing/suite-deps mapping covers the tree well; leave full (default) for the byte-identical whole-suite gate. Watcher-affecting, takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: DELTA_REVIEW
description: Delta-scoped review carry-forward (HERD-204): off (default) | on. off → byte-inert: every new head sha gets the full pre-merge adversarial review exactly as today (sha-keyed review-once). on → BEFORE dispatching a reviewer for a new sha, the watcher tries to PROVE that sha differs from this PR's LAST review-PASSED sha ONLY by a merge of DEFAULT_BRANCH (a pure INTEGRATION push — the newly-merged main commits are already-reviewed main, and the merge itself carries no authored content); if proven it CARRIES FORWARD the prior PASS onto the new sha (records a sha-keyed PASS with source=carried-forward + journals review_carried_forward with from_sha provenance) instead of re-reviewing, saving the redundant Opus pass. The proof is CONSERVATIVE + FAIL-CLOSED: it requires the new sha to be a 2-parent merge whose branch-side parent IS the last-passed sha (already reviewed), whose other parent is already contained in DEFAULT_BRANCH (already-reviewed main), AND whose tree equals a clean 3-way auto-merge of those parents with ZERO manual edits (no authored conflict resolution). Any authored change beyond the merge, a conflicted/hand-edited merge, a missing sha/worktree/main-ref, or any inability to prove integration-only → a normal FULL review. Unknown value → off (fail safe). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (the shipped live review dispatch, HERD-580 port); the bash body (agent-watch.sh) is unreachable since P5b and kept only for its own unit test.
when_to_surface: Set to on to stop re-reviewing pure merge-from-main integration pushes (a builder absorbing DEFAULT_BRANCH into an already-PASSED PR) — the review is carried forward for zero correctness loss since the delta is provably already-reviewed content. Leave off (default) to keep every sha fully re-reviewed, byte-identical. Watcher-affecting (next watcher restart); opt-in only

name: GATE_STATUS
description: Whether the watcher posts a `herd/gates` COMMIT STATUS as it clears each (pr,sha): on (default) | off. on → on both-gates-green (healthcheck + adversarial review) the watcher posts state=success — EXACTLY ONCE per (pr,sha) via a sha-keyed ledger ($GATE_STATUS_STATE), best-effort + fail-soft (a failed API write re-tries next tick since the blessing MUST land). It posts ONLY success: it NEVER posts a non-passing pending/failure status, because a non-passing commit status flips a CLEAN sha to mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE (neither CLEAN nor BLOCKED) in the default unprotected config, stranding the PR out of the merge loop and silently breaking the block/override/auto-refix paths. A gate FAIL posts NOTHING — the fail-safe rests entirely on the ABSENCE of success. The blessing is posted ONLY by a watcher that actually RAN the gates, so pairing it with `require herd/gates` GitHub branch protection (recipe: docs/governance-gates.md) makes the gate FAIL-SAFE across seats and collaborators who keep merge rights: anyone may merge, but nothing UNGATED can — a commit no watcher blessed has no success status and is unmergeable under protection. Under protection a fresh PR reports BLOCKED (missing required check); the watcher gates such a PR specially (runs gates, posts the blessing, but still merges only when CLEAN) so requiring herd/gates never deadlocks. --match-head-commit in do_merge stays as the belt. In team mode (WATCHER_SCOPE=all) the watcher checks the sha's existing status BEFORE dispatching gates and does not re-gate a sha another seat already blessed (cross-seat dedup, ledger-healed so a ledger loss never strands an owned PR). off → byte-inert: no status posted, no read. Unknown value → on. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Leave on (default) so branch protection can require herd/gates and merges stay gated even for collaborators with merge rights; apply the one-time branch-protection recipe in docs/governance-gates.md. Set to off only where the watcher must never touch commit statuses (e.g. a repo with no branch protection where the extra check row is unwanted). Watcher-affecting (next watcher restart)

name: GATE_STATUS_PENDING
description: Whether the engine posts a `herd/gates` state=PENDING commit status at GATE-CYCLE START: on | off (default off, ship-dormant, STRICT — any unrecognized value reads off). Requires GATE_STATUS=on. THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES: under `require herd/gates` branch protection the PR page shows GitHub's own bare 'herd/gates — Expected — Waiting for status to be reported' for the entire gate cycle — a placeholder that names no owner and no phase and looks identical whether a suite is running, a reviewer is mid-verdict, or no watcher will ever gate this PR. on → the moment a candidate enters the gate DAG the engine posts state=pending description='review in progress', EXACTLY ONCE per (pr,sha) via the same at-most-once ledger the success post uses (recorded only on a landed write, so a network blip retries next tick); the terminal success post is unchanged and overwrites it. Journals `gate_status` with state=pending — the same event family as the blessing, so every existing consumer reads it unchanged. A gate FAIL still posts NOTHING. THE HAZARD, and why this is opt-in rather than the default: a non-passing commit status flips a CLEAN sha to mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE in the DEFAULT UNPROTECTED config — neither CLEAN (drops out of the merge path) nor BLOCKED (not gate-eligible) — silently stranding every PR and breaking the block/override/auto-refix paths with it. Where herd/gates IS a required check that sha is ALREADY BLOCKED on the missing required check, so a pending status changes nothing about mergeability and only changes the words the operator reads. off (default) → byte-identical to the pre-HERD-453 SUCCESS-ONLY contract: no pending post, no journal, no ledger. Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py
when_to_surface: Enable ONLY where `herd/gates` is a REQUIRED check under GitHub branch protection (recipe: docs/governance-gates.md) AND operators are asking why a PR page shows an unexplained 'Expected — waiting'. NEVER enable it on a repo without that protection — the UNSTABLE hazard above strands every PR. Leave off (default) everywhere else. Watcher-affecting (next watcher restart)

name: NATIVE_BURST
description: Master switch for the native-burst bounded read-only FAN-OUT seam (scripts/herd/burst.sh): off (default) | on. OFF → today's EXACT serial behavior, byte-identical — the research drainer's Explore fan-out is un-hinted and the pre-merge review runs as a single reviewer. ON → read-only work may BURST (fan out several CONCURRENT calls bounded by REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, the ceiling): the research lane (research.sh) hints the drainer a bounded concurrent-Explore width, and the review gate (herd-review.sh) may run a bounded REVIEW PANEL (see REVIEW_PANEL). WRITE lanes (scribe/backlog/merge) NEVER burst — they stay strictly serial. Unknown/blank → off (fail safe)
when_to_surface: Set to on to cut wall-clock on read-only research + review by fanning out concurrent calls bounded by REVIEW_CONCURRENCY; leave unset/off (default) to keep behavior byte-identical. Additive + opt-in

name: REVIEW_PANEL
description: How many CONCURRENT read-only reviewer passes the pre-merge review runs over the SAME diff when NATIVE_BURST=on — a bounded 'review panel' (more independent eyes catch more correctness bugs). Effective panel size is min(REVIEW_PANEL, REVIEW_CONCURRENCY). Default 1 → a single reviewer, i.e. today's byte-identical behavior; the panel only engages at >1 AND with NATIVE_BURST=on, on the HEADLESS reviewer path. Verdict combination is FAIL-SAFE: ANY member's BLOCK blocks the merge, a merge needs >=1 PASS and zero BLOCKs, and a total-death of all members is an INFRA-FAIL retry (never a cached BLOCK)
when_to_surface: Raise (with NATIVE_BURST=on) to run 2-3 independent reviewer passes per diff for higher bug recall at proportional model cost; keep at 1 for a single reviewer

name: REVIEW_PANEL_MODELS
description: MIXED-VENDOR review panel (HERD-276): a space-separated list of model refs, each optionally runtime-qualified as '<driver>:<model>' (HERD-151) — ONE PANELIST PER REF, each dispatched through its OWN runtime via the driver seam's one-shot exec. Independent vendors have independent blind spots, so a mixed panel raises real-bug recall where N copies of one model cannot. Unset (default) → DORMANT: the panel stays single-model on REVIEW_MODEL, byte-identical. Set → panel size is the REF COUNT (REVIEW_PANEL is not consulted) and the panel engages even at one ref; NATIVE_BURST only decides whether panelists run CONCURRENTLY (bounded by REVIEW_CONCURRENCY) or serially. A panelist whose driver binary is missing at dispatch reports INFRA, NEVER a false BLOCK; 'herd config set' validates every ref eagerly against templates/drivers/*.driver
when_to_surface: Set (e.g. "opus codex:gpt-5 grok:grok-4") to review each diff with several vendors at once; leave unset for today's single-model panel. Pair with REVIEW_PANEL_POLICY to choose how their verdicts fold

name: REVIEW_PANEL_POLICY
description: VERDICT MERGE POLICY for the review panel (HERD-276): how the per-panelist verdicts fold into the ONE verdict the merge gate reads. any-block (default) → any BLOCK blocks, else any PASS passes, else INFRA — today's exact fail-safe fold. all-pass → every DISPATCHED panelist must PASS; a panelist that reached no verdict is a coverage gap and folds to INFRA (a retry), never a pass. majority → blocks >= passes blocks (ties fail safe toward BLOCK), so a lone dissenting vendor no longer gates the merge. Resolved in ONE place (scripts/herd/review-panel.sh) so the local pre-PR review and the watcher's pre-merge gate can never disagree. A non-empty unrecognized value is a typo and fails STRICT to any-block, never to the laxest policy. A non-reporting panelist can only ever move the fold toward INFRA, never toward BLOCK
