when_to_surface: Leave at any-block for the strictest practical gate; all-pass when an unreachable vendor must halt the merge rather than be shrugged off; majority when a mixed panel's lone false-positive BLOCK is costing more than it catches

name: INFRA_BREAKER_MAX
description: INFRA-timeout circuit breaker threshold (HERD-110): after this many CONSECUTIVE INFRA failures — non-verdict reviewer deaths (a claude exec-hang / env failure / a dispatched reviewer that died WITHOUT writing a verdict), tracked GLOBALLY across all PRs — the watcher OPENS a circuit breaker and STOPS dispatching new pre-merge reviews/healthchecks into what looks like a dead/hung environment, surfacing a loud 'infra circuit open' status row + journal event. After INFRA_BREAKER_COOLDOWN seconds the breaker goes HALF-OPEN for a SINGLE probe: a real verdict CLOSEs it (env recovered), another non-verdict death RE-OPENs it. CRITICAL: a real code BLOCK or PASS verdict proves the env is alive and RESETS the counter — it NEVER trips the breaker; only non-verdict deaths count. 0 (default) = OFF, byte-inert
when_to_surface: Turn on (a small N like 3-5) for unattended/overnight runs so a dead reviewer environment (exec-hang, transient infra outage) is detected after N consecutive non-verdict deaths and the watcher stops burning cycles re-dispatching into it, instead of hammering every PR forever; leave 0 (default) to keep behavior byte-identical

name: INFRA_BREAKER_COOLDOWN
description: Seconds the INFRA circuit breaker (HERD-110, INFRA_BREAKER_MAX) stays OPEN before it admits a SINGLE half-open probe retry. While open, new review/health dispatch is suppressed; once the cooldown elapses the next candidate becomes the lone probe whose outcome closes (real verdict) or re-opens (another death) the breaker. Non-numeric → 300. Only consulted when INFRA_BREAKER_MAX >= 1
when_to_surface: Tune the recovery cadence: shorter → probe a possibly-recovered environment sooner (more retries into a still-dead env); longer → wait out a longer outage before re-probing. Default 300s (5 min)

name: WATCH_CLAUDE_PROBE_TIMEOUT
description: Claude exec-hang probe timeout in seconds (HERD-108): on some environments `claude` WEDGES on invocation — every exec hangs before the process finishes starting (e.g. the macOS com.apple.quarantine _dyld_start hang) — so every review dispatch spawns a corpse and burns a REVIEW_CONCURRENCY slot forever against a hang it cannot see. When armed (N>=1), the watcher probes `claude --version` under a HARD N-second timeout at most ONCE per tick BEFORE dispatching a reviewer; a timeout HOLDS that tick's dispatch (a cached-PASS PR still merges) with a loud 'claude exec-hang' status row + a journal infra_event, journaled once per hang episode. Complements the HERD-110 INFRA_BREAKER (which only reacts AFTER reviewers die without a verdict) by catching the wedge up front; `herd doctor`'s own `claude responds` check reports the same hang at diagnosis time. Only a genuine TIMEOUT counts as a hang — a broken (non-zero exit) or absent claude is fail-soft and never holds the queue. 0 (default) = OFF, byte-inert (no probe exec, no journal). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (the shipped live review dispatch, HERD-580 port); the bash body (agent-watch.sh) is unreachable since P5b and kept only for its own unit test.
when_to_surface: Arm (a small N like 5) for unattended/overnight runs so a wedged claude is DETECTED and surfaced instead of silently stalling every review; leave 0 (default) to keep behavior byte-identical

name: WATCH_HOTKEYS
description: In-console hotkey (HERD-674): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). Arms a bounded, fail-soft keypress listener on the watcher's OWN tick loop — the render loop had NO keypress/stdin handling anywhere before this (the HERD-661 descope finding). Pressing 'v' flips WATCHER_VIEW mine<->all IN-MEMORY, for THIS PROCESS ONLY: it reassigns the shell variable, never writes .herd/config or config.local — `herd config set` remains the durable path, and a watcher restart (or a second seat) reverts to whatever the file says. ARMED ONLY when the watcher's own stdin is a real interactive tty ([ -t 0 ]) — headless, sim, lib-mode, or a piped/redirected stdin degrade SILENTLY (no listener, no row, no error). NON-BLOCKING BY CONSTRUCTION: the tick loop itself never reads the tty — a single background listener process (spawned once at startup) owns the one blocking read (stty -icanon -echo min 1 time 0 + a plain `read -n 1` loop, costing zero CPU while idle) and drops a counter into a marker file on each keystroke; the tick side only ever stats/reads that ONE regular file, so its added per-tick cost is a constant few milliseconds whether or not a key was ever pressed. A minimal seam for this ONE keymap — not a keymap framework. off (default) => byte-inert: no stty call, no stdin read, no listener process, no rendered hint. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on for a solo/team operator running the watcher attached to its own interactive pane who wants to flip between "my PRs only" and "everything" without leaving the console or running `herd config set`; leave off (default) for a headless/CI/sim watcher, where it is inert anyway

name: REVIEW_AUTOFIX
description: Auto-bounce BLOCK reviews to the builder agent: true | false (default false); when true, the watcher delivers a re-task prompt and re-tasks the idle builder on each new BLOCK sha, up to REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS
when_to_surface: Enable to remove the human re-task step after a BLOCK review; disable (default) for projects that prefer explicit coordinator approval before re-work

name: REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS
description: Maximum auto-refix rounds per RAIL (review | health | stale-base) before escalating to "needs you" (default: 3); counts across all shas for a PR. HERD-229: each rail carries its own budget, a rail's counter is ZEROED when that rail's red resolves (review PASS, health CLEAN, base freshened), and a derived per-PR total ceiling of 3x this value bounds a PR that fails across every rail
when_to_surface: Raise for longer fix cycles; lower to 1 for a single bounce with immediate escalation; requires REVIEW_AUTOFIX=true

name: REFIX_COMPLETE_MIN
description: Minutes after a refix wake (refix_wake_result woke=1) before the watcher checks that the SAME (pr, sha) actually SHIPPED a fix (HERD-420). A woke=1 result only proves the builder's pane came back to "working" — not that it committed or pushed anything; the once-guard (refix_attempted) then holds silently forever on that sha with nothing watching for the gap. Live incident: PR #531 — a review-BLOCK bounced the builder, it edited bin/herd, then went back to "done" with the edit never committed or pushed, and the PR sat blocked on the same sha indefinitely until a human happened to notice. Past this window, if the SAME (pr, sha) still shows the builder agent done/idle (a read-only pane peek, never another wake attempt) AND no new sha has landed on the PR, the watcher journals refix_incomplete (pr, sha, round, agent_status, dirty=yes/no from a worktree probe) and re-bounces ONCE — reusing the SAME rail's REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget and bounce/wake-verify machinery, no parallel path — with a "finish your uncommitted work" prompt instead of the original problem restated; exhausting that budget escalates through the identical needs-you path a normal BLOCK exhaustion uses. Default 10 (ships ON, unlike WEDGE_GRACE_MIN/FINISH_STALL_MIN's off-by-default convention, because this closes a proven silent-failure class rather than adding new autonomous behavior); an explicit 0 disables the leg (byte-identical to pre-HERD-420: the once-guard just holds). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py — the review and health rails, the only ones whose bounce dispatch is still live post-P5-cutover (bash's review-kind bounce path is dead code since the HERD-306 bash-core deletion)
when_to_surface: Lower for a faster safety net on unattended/overnight runs where a silently-stuck builder should be caught quickly; raise to give a slow/loaded builder more slack before the completion check fires; set 0 to disable and rely on a human noticing (pre-HERD-420 behavior)

name: HERD_REFIX_WAIT_TIMEOUT
description: Seconds the watcher waits, backed off across several checks, for a bounced builder's agent pane to flip to "working" before giving up on that wake attempt (default: 15). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's refix bounce/wake-verify path (LiveGates) and by the equivalent bash wait helpers in agent-watch.sh. HERD-449: no `: "${HERD_REFIX_WAIT_TIMEOUT:=default}"` line lives in herd-config.sh — each call site inlines its own `${HERD_REFIX_WAIT_TIMEOUT:-15}` fallback — so herd-config.sh only carries a bare `export` for it
when_to_surface: Raise on a slower agent pane / driver where "working" takes longer to observe; lower to fail a stuck wake attempt faster

name: HEALTHCHECK_AUTOFIX
description: Auto-bounce a reproduced pre-merge healthcheck CODE ERROR to the builder agent, exactly as REVIEW_AUTOFIX bounces a BLOCK review: true | false (default false); the re-task prompt carries the failing test line + the tailable suite log path, is delivered once per (pr,sha), and spends the HEALTH rail's own round budget (REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS per rail, refunded when the suite next goes CLEAN; a per-PR total ceiling of 3x still bounds the PR). Limit-parked and dead/missing agents are preflighted (never typed at); a tab-leak-guard trip is infra and never bounced; exhausting the budget escalates to a needs-you row carrying the blocker and the remedy
when_to_surface: Enable to close the loop on a red healthcheck without a human re-task step; disable (default) when a code-error red should wait for explicit coordinator triage

name: CODEMAP_AUTOREFRESH
description: Keeps the committed code maps fresh — docs/codemap.md (file-level; the engine tree in the engine repo, or the consuming project's own language-aware source tree elsewhere — codemap.sh auto-detects the mode) AND docs/symbol-index.md (function-level def→caller index) — via their deterministic, LLM-free native scans. TWO paths share this lever: (1) do_merge fast path — after THIS seat merges a PR, regenerate and, only when content changed, commit STRAIGHT to the default branch (messages "chore: refresh codemap after PR #N" / "chore: refresh symbol-index after PR #N"); (2) tick-level reconcile (HERD-218 multi-seat invariant) — every watcher tick, probe with the read-only --check seams and, when STALE regardless of WHO merged (another seat / gh UI), regenerate+commit ONCE with provenance=reconcile (messages "chore: refresh codemap (reconcile)" / "chore: refresh symbol-index (reconcile)"). Protected-branch handling (HERD-338): a push rejected by a protected-branch hook rolls back the commit immediately (git reset --hard HEAD~1) so local main never drifts ahead of origin; the journal records result=error reason=push-rejected (LOUD, never the silent pushed=no corpse). The tick-level reconcile also resets to origin on a push-rejected heal path instead of holding push-failed forever. herd update self-heals: when local main is ahead of origin with only regenerable artifact commits, it auto-resets to origin and retries. Fully fail-soft — a map problem never blocks a merge or a tick. off → byte-inert: the watcher never touches either map
when_to_surface: Leave on (default) so the committed engine maps stay fresh for coordinator/builder context at zero token cost across every seat; set off to freeze them and refresh only manually via herd codemap / herd symbol-index. Independent of the read-only staleness probes (herd codemap --check / herd symbol-index --check / the herd status CODEMAP row), which always work regardless of this lever

name: MAIN_HEALTH_TICK
description: Main-health as a RECONCILED INVARIANT (HERD-129, generalized in HERD-222): every OBSERVED default-branch sha ends with a collected health verdict, whoever merged it. Each tick the watcher dispatches the healthcheck suite against the current default-branch HEAD when that sha has no verdict yet — this seat's merge, ANOTHER seat's merge, a gh-UI merge, a run deferred because the health slot was busy, or a worker killed mid-suite (all four holes of the old merge-event-only tick). Catches the failure class the per-PR gate structurally cannot see: two independently-green PRs merging into a broken COMBINATION (e.g. the #226 advise exit-code collision that left main red ~2h, found only when later unrelated PRs inherited it). sha-keyed so each main sha runs ONCE; runs the FULL (heavy) suite — a 'light' check against the default-branch checkout is a zero-file vacuous green that could silently clear a real red; honors HEALTH_CONCURRENCY. On a reproduced red it raises a LOUD persistent 'MAIN RED — <failing test> (since #N)' console row + a notification, cleared when a later sha goes green: on | off (default). An ALARM only — never a merge gate, revert, or re-merge; fully fail-soft (a suite that cannot run journals an infra_event, never a false-red). off → byte-inert: no suite, no journal, no row
when_to_surface: Turn on in a repo that wants a default-branch health tripwire that holds across SEATS (herdkit enables it for itself). Leave off (default) elsewhere: zero behavior change, and the pre-merge health gate still proves every PR green in isolation. Distinct from that gate — this catches only the broken-combination class the per-PR gate structurally cannot see. Pair with MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS to self-heal a stale red and MAIN_HEALTH_AUTOFIX to file the fix

name: MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS
description: While MAIN_HEALTH_TICK holds the default branch RED, RE-VERIFY the CURRENT main sha every N minutes (HERD-222). A red is sticky by design — it persists until a LATER sha goes green — so a red whose cause was already fixed out-of-band, or that a one-off environment blip painted, kept shouting until the next merge happened to land (one stood 19h). This lever lets the red re-run the suite for the sha it is standing on: a stale red then clears itself through the ordinary green→clear path (recovery notified once), and a real red is simply re-confirmed. Rate-limited to at most one re-verify per N minutes (measured from the last collected verdict for that sha), and subject to the same HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot and per-sha dispatch guards, so it can never stack suites: 0 (default) | N minutes. Any non-numeric value reads as 0 — a typo can never arm it. 0 → byte-identical: a sha that already has a verdict is never re-run
when_to_surface: Set (e.g. 30) in a repo where MAIN_HEALTH_TICK is on and merges are infrequent, so a MAIN RED row is never trusted stale — the row you see is at most N minutes old. Leave 0 when merges are frequent enough that the next green sha clears the alarm anyway

name: MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_ONESHOT
description: Guarantee a standing MAIN RED always has at least ONE armed clearing trigger (HERD-612 leg 5) — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). GROUNDED 2026-08-10, hours after this project flipped HEALTH_SOURCE=ci: a red pinned during the Aug-6 GitHub Actions outage had, at that moment, ZERO reachable clearing triggers left. Its sha already carried a run-once verdict marker (so the observed-sha reconcile never re-dispatches it), MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS was 0 (its default — no cadence), and main was QUIESCENT, so no newer sha's green could supersede it either; branch CI was green at head the whole time and nothing in the engine could ever ask again. The reconciled-invariant doctrine's "every observed sha ends with a verdict" has to include "and that verdict can still change". on (REQUIRES MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on) → whenever a LOCAL-suite identity stands red with no cadence armed, the watcher fires EXACTLY ONE re-verify of the CURRENT main sha — the same sha MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS would re-verify, so the two paths differ in CADENCE only, never in what they verify; the result clears the red through the ordinary green→clear path (recovery notified once) or simply re-confirms it. Bounded three ways: a shared $TREES per-sha marker, so a restart loop can never re-spend it (the once-guard is keyed on the RED's sha, not on a boot event — which is what makes "fire at watcher boot" reconciled rather than event-driven); the marker is written only on a REAL dispatch, so a busy HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot defers the one-shot instead of consuming it; and it is scoped to the LOCAL identity, because a CI-scoped red always has the MAIN_HEALTH_CI_GATE leg itself as a trigger and a local green cannot clear a CI identity anyway (HERD-372 scope rules). off (default) → byte-identical: no marker, no dispatch, no journal line, and MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS=0 still means a sha with a verdict is never re-run. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Arm it in any repo running MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on WITHOUT a MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS cadence — that composition is exactly the one with no clearing trigger, and it is the DEFAULT pair, so most consumers are in it. Especially worth arming where main goes quiet for long stretches (a small team, a weekend, a merge freeze) or where the local suite is only one of several verdict sources (HEALTH_SOURCE=ci). Surface it when an operator asks why a MAIN RED row is still up after the failure was fixed, or when a red's last-verified stamp keeps aging with no re-verify behind it. Prefer MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS when you want a repeating cadence — this is the floor beneath it, not a replacement, and the two compose (a nonzero cadence takes over and this never fires)

name: MAIN_HEALTH_AUTOFIX
description: AUTO-REMEDIATION for a reproduced MAIN RED (HERD-222): on | off (default off, ship-dormant) | spawn (HERD-476). on/spawn → when the main-health suite reproduces a red whose failing-test identity is HONEST, the watcher enqueues ONE scribe item citing that test and journals `main_health_autofix result=enqueued`. HONEST means a TAP 'not ok' line, or an identity that resolved to concrete test/source file tokens — never healthcheck.sh's content-free '❌ CODE ERROR' banner, never a PASS-marked line, never a tab-leak-guard infra trip (those journal `result=skipped reason=dishonest-identity` and file nothing, so the alarm never cries wolf into the tracker). HERD-476: a kind=ci red (MAIN_HEALTH_CI_GATE) is no longer automatically dishonest — its bare 'CI <workflow>: <conclusion>' render names no test, so this leg first re-derives the identity from the failing run's OWN logs (`gh run view --log-failed`, parsing the same 'real-failed tests:' block a local red already gets); a log that cannot be read or names no test skips instead with reason=ci-log-unreadable, never falling back to file off the generic conclusion string. Enqueued at most once per distinct failing identity while main is red, so a MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS re-verify that reproduces the SAME failure re-files nothing while a red that MUTATES into a different test files the new one; the guard is dropped when main goes green. spawn (HERD-476, opt-in ABOVE the on/file-only default) additionally dispatches ONE tracked+claimed quick-lane builder against that same identity, through the SAME durable spawn queue the coordinator's own spawn.sh uses (HERD_ITEM_REF carries the identity as the spawn's tracker ref, so the builder's PR carries a 'Refs:' line and, under CLAIM_REQUIRED, is claimed before any worktree/agent exists) — RISK: this is the one path in the feature that writes code UNATTENDED; the ordinary pipeline (the builder's own light healthcheck, then the watcher's authoritative heavy gate + adversarial review) still stands between it and a merge, but a bad main can now spawn several concurrent builders across an unlucky run of distinct failures with no human in the loop until review time. on (the safer default once this lever is armed at all) stays file-only — it never spawns, reverts, or touches the branch. off (default) → byte-identical: no scribe item, no journal line, no spawn
when_to_surface: Enable 'on' in a repo where a red default branch must always have a tracked item behind it (herdkit's own posture once the lever bakes). Reach for 'spawn' only once 'on' has proven itself and unattended-fix risk is accepted — a human still reviews the PR before merge, but the builder starts without one. Leave off (default) when a human triages the MAIN RED row directly, or when the tracker must never be written by the watcher. Requires MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on (a red is what triggers it) and SCRIBE_BACKEND to be configured; spawn additionally benefits from CLAIM_REQUIRED=on (so the tracker ref is actually claimed, not just carried)

name: MAIN_HEALTH_CI_GATE
description: Make the DEFAULT BRANCH's own GitHub Actions CI conclusion an input to the MAIN RED alarm (HERD-434, the "Branch-CI main-red leg", HERD-334) — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). GROUNDED — main merged 5 PRs (#548-#552, 2026-07-28) while GitHub Actions CI stayed red on every one and MAIN_HEALTH_TICK reported green throughout: MAIN_HEALTH_TICK's local re-suite runs on the WATCHER'S OWN host, which can be green on a sha CI itself reds (a differently-provisioned runner, or — the root cause here — a chaos/timing test with a too-tight local assumption). on (REQUIRES MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on — reuses its state file, console row, notify-once path, and HERD-372 identity merge so a standing local-suite red is never clobbered) → each tick (throttled, ~every 10 ticks) probes `gh run list` for the default branch's latest COMPLETED run against the current main HEAD; a FAILURE conclusion raises the SAME 'MAIN RED' row + notification a local red does, a later PASS clears the CI identity. FAIL-SOFT throughout: offline/unauthenticated gh, no matching run, or a run still IN PROGRESS all read as nothing-to-report — NEVER a red row, NEVER a false clear. off (default) → byte-inert: no `gh run list` call, no state file write, no row, no notification
when_to_surface: Enable in a repo where CI (not just the operator's own machine) must be able to trip the MAIN RED alarm — herdkit enables it for itself after HERD-434. Leave off (default) elsewhere, or in a repo with no GitHub Actions CI at all: zero behavior change, and MAIN_HEALTH_TICK's local re-suite still catches the broken-COMBINATION class it always has. Requires MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on

name: RED_LEDGER
description: The shared RED-ROW LEDGER (HERD-539) — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → every red row this project wires through red-ledger.sh (today: MAIN RED, the 'unlinked merges' alarm) caches its diagnosing text into a keyed ledger the moment it is diagnosed or reverified, and the row renders back an extra ' · verified Xm ago' suffix read from that SAME ledger, so the text on screen is provably what was journaled, with an honest freshness clock beside it. A red clearing through the ordinary reverify path additionally journals `red_cleared key <k> reason reverified` exactly once, so a clear is as visible in the journal as the red was — closing a real gap: the 'unlinked merges' alarm (HERD-522) had NO clear mechanism at all before this. off (default) → byte-inert: no ledger file, no extra journal line, every red row's text byte-identical to before this key existed
when_to_surface: Turn on for an unattended/multi-seat control room where an operator needs to trust a red row's freshness at a glance instead of wondering whether it is stale. Leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Pair with RED_ROW_RECHECK_MINS to also arm the auto-clear reverify on classes beyond main-health

name: RED_ROW_RECHECK_MINS
description: Extends the MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS pattern (HERD-222) past main-health (HERD-539) — while RED_LEDGER holds a red for a class this project wires a reverify for (today: the 'unlinked merges' alarm), RE-PROBE it every N minutes so a red whose cause was already fixed out-of-band (a PR body edited after merge to add the `Refs:` line it was missing) self-heals through the ordinary red_cleared path instead of standing forever. 0 (default, off) → byte-identical: a standing alarm is never re-probed. N>0 → at most one re-probe per N minutes per row (measured from that row's own last-verified stamp), REQUIRES RED_LEDGER=on — the cadence clock and the clear both live in the ledger. A non-numeric value reads as 0
when_to_surface: Set alongside RED_LEDGER=on in a repo where the 'unlinked merges' alarm should self-heal instead of waiting for an operator to notice and relink the item by hand. Leave 0 (default) where a human relink is preferred or the alarm rarely fires

name: RED_AUTOESCALATE
description: HERD-547 (HERD-539 leg 4): engine-shaped red auto-escalation — on | off (default off, ship-dormant), REQUIRES RED_LEDGER=on (this reads the SAME diagnosing text red-ledger.sh already caches). on → the moment MAIN RED notes a sha's why-text into the shared ledger, that text is classified against the routing rule templates/coordinator.md.tmpl documents at 'Routing: APP bug vs HERD-ENGINE bug' — a project's own code vs the workflow machinery itself (bin/herd, scripts/herd/**, pysrc/herd/**), via the new herd_red_ledger_engine_shaped predicate (red-ledger.sh): an ENGINE-shaped why files automatically via the EXISTING `herd report` path (composes with its own title-dedup rather than reimplementing it; --diagnosis attaches the red-ledger why-text as its own body section), and journals `red_escalated`. A shared-pool once-guard (mirrors HERD-371's main-health-fix marker, via the generic `--once` store primitive) claims the filing per dedup key across every seat, so a repeat observation of the SAME key no-ops; a project-shaped why is NEVER escalated. Fail-soft throughout: no HERDKIT_HOME/bin/herd, no gh, or `herd report` itself declining (no HERD_REPO, a likely duplicate) all skip WITHOUT filing and journal the reason. off (default) → byte-inert: no shellout, no journal line, no filing. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on alongside RED_LEDGER=on in an unattended/multi-seat control room where an engine bug surfacing as a project red should reach HERD_REPO without waiting for an operator to notice and file it by hand. Leave off (default) for a byte-identical watcher, or where every red in this project is genuinely this project's own code

name: ENV_SUSPECT_TIMEOUT
description: Classify a per-test health-suite TIMEOUT observed while this box is under load as env-suspect, not a bare code red (HERD-546, HERD-539 leg 3; re-hung onto the live path by HERD-567) — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → when the LIVE health worker's (pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's _HEALTH_WORKER_SH, the shipped async suite runner) run-1 failure is a per-test TIMEOUT (bats' "# timeout after Ns" TAP suffix, or run-suite.sh's HERD-478 per-test-cap-ledger "(TIMEOUT after Ns)" suffix) AND this box looks contended (loadavg1m >= HEALTH_LOAD_THRESHOLD, or another HERD-529 local-suite slot — the cross-worktree `.local-suite-slot-*` pool — is live), the SAME tailable log the running row already reads gets a '[env-suspect] env-suspect · timeout under load · solo re-run queued' marker line (_health_inflight_note/_health_env_suspect_marker, agent-watch.sh, painted by either engine) and a health_env_suspect journal event lands once the terminal verdict is collected — the SAME existing HERD-498 retry-before-red solo re-run plays out unchanged: a solo pass clears to FLAKY as always, a solo fail still reds CODEERROR as always — this only changes what a still-pending retry renders and what gets journaled. off (default) → byte-identical: no marker line, no journal event, the running row is unchanged
when_to_surface: Turn on for an unattended/multi-seat control room where an operator needs to tell "this might just be box load" from "this is a real red pending confirmation" while a solo re-run is still in flight. Leave off (default) for a byte-identical console

name: HEALTH_LOAD_THRESHOLD
description: The loadavg1m reading (whole number) at/above which this box counts as "under load" — default 4. Consulted by TWO independent levers, each gated on its own switch, neither on HEALTH_LOAD_THRESHOLD itself: ENV_SUSPECT_TIMEOUT (HERD-546, per-test timeout classification) and ANOMALY_BASELINES (HERD-618, `_anomaly_load_high` — widens the phase-anomaly rail's FILING bar to 2x its normal threshold while the box looks contended, so a marginal p95 exceedance journals load_qualified instead of filing a tracker item). Byte-inert while BOTH levers are off. A non-numeric value falls back to the default
when_to_surface: Raise on a box whose idle loadavg legitimately sits near/above 4 (more cores, more routine background contention) so neither lever fires on ordinary load; lower on a quiet/small box where even a modest concurrent suite should count as contended

name: AGING_PR_TTL
description: AGING-PR alarm TTL in SECONDS (HERD-334): how long an engine-approved PR (herd/gates PASSED) may sit blocked on a required CI check before the watcher calls it AGING. GROUNDED — PRs #440/#441 sat 7h with gates PASSED but a required CI suite red, zero alarms, because the console treats required-check-blocked as a quiet steady state; no TTL covered 'engine approved it, branch protection blocks it, nothing is progressing'. Past this TTL the render pass AGES the PR off OBSERVED state each tick (a first-seen marker keyed by pr+sha in $WORKTREES_DIR, so a second seat reads the same clock) and, once the sha still carries a herd/gates=success blessing AND a required check is still red/pending, grows a LOUD advisory continuation line ('aging Nh · engine-approved but CI failed: <check> — nothing is merging') and journals a `pr_aging` event ONCE per (pr,sha) crossing. journal-audit.sh (when JOURNAL_AUDIT=on) reports the matching `gates_passed_no_merge` finding from a gates-passed journal marker (`gate_status` state=success context=herd/gates, or the python engine core's `blessing` state=success) with no later `merge` for the pr. Both surfaces read this TTL through the ONE shared getter in aging-pr.sh, so they can never drift. Default 3600 (60m); 0 DISABLES the alarm on both surfaces (byte-inert, mirrors DEP_STALE_TTL=0); a non-numeric value reads as the default. ADVISORY only — never a hold, revert, or re-merge; fully fail-soft (a gh/CI API miss skips the leg silently, never a red row)
when_to_surface: Leave at the 60m default for an unattended coordinator so an engine-approved PR stuck behind a red/pending required CI check surfaces loudly instead of sitting invisibly for hours; lower where a blocked-on-CI PR must be triaged sooner, raise where a long required CI matrix legitimately runs past an hour, 0 to turn the alarm off entirely. Never a merge gate

name: WATCHER_FLAIR
description: Watcher status-console FLAIR pack (HERD-147): on | off (default). ADDITIVE cosmetic layer on the live 'herd watch' console — (a) a merge CELEBRATION: the status tick after a merge prints one theme-colored line '🐑 #<pr> joins the flock · <n> grazing'; (b) a PASTURE HEADER: one line rendering the in-flight herd by state — 🐑 grazing (building), 💤 idle, ✅ in the pen (done). Colors come ONLY from the active theme's C_* vars (theme.sh); NO_COLOR / non-tty renders plain. HARD RULE: flair NEVER softens a red/dead/needs-you state — a 💀 dead or ⚠️ needs-you builder is exactly as loud as today, and OFF (default) is byte-inert: every console byte is identical to before this feature
when_to_surface: Turn on for a cosmetic morale layer on the watcher console (herdkit enables it for itself after this ships); leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart; opt-in, never self-activates and never changes a gate or a merge decision

name: WATCHER_SELF_RESTART
description: Watcher SELF-RESTART on stale engine code (HERD-251): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). The watcher executes the engine code it loaded at startup, so a merge that lands new engine code leaves it running a stale image; HERD-233 detects exactly that and raises a 'restart recommended' note the operator has to act on by hand. HERD-651 widened WHAT counts as stale: the watcher does not only run agent-watch.sh, it sources a dozen-plus siblings out of scripts/herd/ and shells out to pysrc/herd/ + bin/herd, and $MAIN's HEAD moves by routes the freshness reconcile never sees a delta for (do_merge's own fast-forward after this seat's merge, an operator pull). So the note now arms whenever OBSERVED $MAIN HEAD differs from the sha THIS image loaded from AND that delta touched a loaded path (scripts/herd/, pysrc/herd/, bin/herd) -- an allowlist, so docs/ and templates/ never arm it: templates are render inputs, not code the watcher runs. Live 2026-08-11: a sweep.sh reaper merged at 13:31 and the watcher missed the dead row it fixes for ~7 hours with this key on. on -> that same note instead ARMS a QUIESCE-THEN-EXEC. QUIESCE: the watcher stops dispatching NEW gate work -- reviews (_review_gate_step / _dispatch_review), healthchecks (_healthcheck_gate), conflict-resolver spawns (spawn_resolver) and the stale-base heal that dispatches them (_handle_stale_dup) all refuse -- while every in-flight worker runs to completion and its verdict is COLLECTED normally (the collect paths sit upstream of every hold, so nothing in flight is lost and nothing is killed). Each hold sits ABOVE its call site's own ledger write -- notably above _handle_stale_dup's record_refix -- so a refused dispatch never strands a spent once-guard behind it; already-green PRs still merge. EXEC: once zero live REVIEW/HEALTH workers are observed for 2 CONSECUTIVE ticks (resolvers and builders are panes that outlive the exec, so they are deliberately outside that count), or the inline 15-minute max-wait cap expires, the watcher replaces its own process image in place -- same pane (exec keeps the tty), same argv0 herd-watch-<workspace> tag (passed explicitly via exec -a), same singleton lock (exec keeps the pid, and _acquire_watcher_singleton adopts a lock whose recorded pid is its own), so no window exists in which the workspace is unlocked. Journals watcher_quiesce at the arm and watcher_self_restart reason=engine-update shas=<old>..<new> at the exec; the console's restart note becomes 'restarting on new engine code - draining N workers'. FAIL-SOFT: an unreadable engine script, or a hermetic-test guard, disarms and restores the recommendation row rather than dying. off (default) -> byte-identical to HERD-233: no arm, no dispatch hold, no exec, no journal, and the recommendation row renders exactly as before. Never arms in dry-run. Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) once you trust the engine's merge gate, so a watcher never keeps grading PRs with code its own repo has already replaced -- the operator restarted by hand six times on 2026-07-09; leave off (default) to keep the advisory 'restart recommended (`herd reload`)' row and restart the watcher yourself.

name: WATCHER_SINGLETON_RECONCILE
description: The watcher SINGLETON as a RECONCILED INVARIANT (HERD-450): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). The invariant is EXACTLY ONE live process carrying this workspace's argv0 AND a lockfile that NAMES it — before this key that was an assertion made once at launch (the acquire gate) and never re-checked. GROUNDED 2026-07-31: a watcher SURVIVED a `herd reload`, ticked 41 minutes re-parented to init alongside its replacement (both gating the same PRs, both counting the same concurrency slots) while the lockfile stayed EMPTY throughout — and an empty lockfile blinds every seat at once, since `herd status`, sweep.sh, the launch paths' adopt-or-refuse read and clause (2) of the fork exemption ALL key off the recorded pid. on -> every tick the watcher classifies the invariant through the ONE shared identity seam (watcher-exempt.sh's watcher_singleton_verdict, the same seam `herd status` and the sweep count with): a DUPLICATE journals watcher_singleton_violation once per signature and holds a loud persistent console row naming the pids and the remedy (`herd reload`); a drifted, stale or EMPTY lockfile is REPAIRED in place by the sole live main recording itself (journals watcher_lock_repaired), which un-blinds every one of those seats at once; a WATCHER_SELF_RESTART exec window reads as a benign, TTL-bounded HANDOFF. It NEVER kills: a 'duplicate' is very often a legitimate review-tick FORK (the tick loop forks constantly and every fork inherits the argv0), and reaping one caches a bogus BLOCK verdict against a PR nobody reviewed — the fork/orphan discrimination and the verified kill stay in `herd reload`'s stop leg, an explicit operator action. off (default) -> byte-inert: no ps sample, no journal event, no console row, no lockfile write. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on for an unattended control room, or on any seat where a watcher has ever survived a reload or a `herd status` watcher count has ever looked wrong: it converts 'exactly one watcher' from a launch-time assumption into a per-tick reconciled invariant that says so on the console within a tick. Leave off (default) for a byte-identical console

name: WATCHER_STOP_REAP_MAIN_HEALTH
description: Stop the MAIN-HEALTH chains a watcher was running when it is stopped (HERD-450): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). A watcher restart (`herd reload`, `herd pane watch`, sweep leg 5) ORPHANS its gate chains — they re-parent to init — rather than stopping them, so an orphaned main-health worker keeps holding its .health-inflight-main-<sha> marker, and therefore a HEALTH_CONCURRENCY slot, for the rest of a ~9-minute heavy suite whose verdict the departed watcher will never collect: the marker is ABANDONED and only ages out on HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT (HERD-451) while PR healthchecks queue behind a corpse. on -> the stop leg SIGTERM->poll->SIGKILLs each LIVE main-health worker that descends from a watcher it just stopped (its parent is one of them, or it has already been re-parented to init), removes the marker only on CONFIRMED death, frees the slot, and journals main_health_chain_reaped (or main_health_chain_reap_failed) per pid. Safe by construction because MAIN_HEALTH_TICK is itself a reconciled invariant: a killed chain costs exactly one re-run on a later tick. The PR-gate families are NEVER touched — a review or per-PR health worker writes a result file the NEXT watcher DOES collect, so killing one would destroy real work. off (default) -> byte-identical: no glob, no signal, no journal line. Consumed by bin/herd
when_to_surface: Turn on where main-health runs (MAIN_HEALTH_TICK=on) and reloads are frequent, so a restart does not leave a ~9-minute heavy suite holding the health slot for a watcher that no longer exists. Leave off (default) if you would rather an orphaned main-health suite run to completion and age out on HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT

name: WATCHER_RESURRECT
description: External-cadence WATCHER RESURRECTION (HERD-489): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). GROUNDED 2026-08-02: a dead watcher stayed dead for 5 HOURS — every existing revival lever (WATCHER_SELF_RESTART, WATCHER_SINGLETON_RECONCILE, COORDINATOR_WATCHDOG) is code the watcher's OWN tick loop runs, so all three are inert against the one failure that actually happened: the process is not running AT ALL, and nothing is ticking to notice. This key gates scripts/herd/watcher-resurrect.sh (`herd watcher-resurrect`), a SEPARATE short-lived probe an operator cron/launchd job drives on an external cadence — the one place code CAN run when the watcher itself cannot. on -> each invocation classifies this project's watcher through the shared watcher-exempt.sh seam (watcher_singleton_verdict, the same argv0 + lockfile/flock reconciled check `herd status` and WATCHER_SINGLETON_RECONCILE use); it acts ONLY on a CONFIRMED zero-mains verdict (state NONE) -- OK / LOCK_DRIFT / DUPLICATE / HANDOFF all mean at least one main is alive and are left STRICTLY alone, so a live watcher is NEVER doubled. On NONE it journals watcher_resurrect_detected (loud, before acting) and relaunches through the VERIFIED stop/start seam (`herd reload`, issue #579) -- never its own kill/spawn logic -- then journals watcher_resurrected with the new pid on a confirmed live relaunch, or watcher_resurrect_failed otherwise. off (default) -> byte-inert: no verdict call, no journal write, no relaunch, exit 0, even when the probe is invoked. Consumed by scripts/herd/watcher-resurrect.sh
when_to_surface: Wire an operator cron/launchd job to run `herd watcher-resurrect` on a schedule (e.g. every 5-15 min) and turn this on for any unattended/overnight control room — it is the one revival path that survives the watcher process itself being gone, which no in-process watchdog lever can reach. Leave off (default) if the watcher is only ever restarted by a human running `herd reload`

name: WATCHER_CRASHLOOP_GUARD
description: The pane wrapper's CRASH-LOOP hard stop (HERD-548): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). GROUNDED 2026-08-05: post-reload the watcher crash-looped silently for ~2 minutes (repeated fast child deaths, zero journal, zero console beyond the header) then self-resolved with nobody the wiser. on -> herd-watch.sh (the pane wrapper every launch path ultimately runs) stops using a bare exec and instead runs agent-watch.sh in a supervising loop: a death that is not a deliberate stop signal (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP end the wrapper cleanly, never fought) and that survived less than HERD_WATCH_CRASHLOOP_FAST_SECS (default 5s) counts as FAST; after HERD_WATCH_CRASHLOOP_N (default 3) CONSECUTIVE fast deaths the wrapper stops respawning, prints the last captured child stderr loudly to the pane, journals watcher_crashloop, and trips the shared watcher-exempt.sh marker (watcher_crashloop_trip) -- cleared automatically once a later watcher PROVES it survives past the same settle window. Child stderr is captured to a bounded per-attempt file so the loud print never scrolls the real fault out of the pane's scrollback. watcher-resurrect.sh checks the same marker before ever calling `herd reload`, so the external cron cadence never fights a standing loop by relaunching the identical broken build on a timer; a plain operator-run `herd pane watch` is not gated by the marker. off (default) -> byte-identical to before this key: a bare exec, no loop, no capture file, no marker, no journal from the wrapper. Consumed by scripts/herd/herd-watch.sh, scripts/herd/watcher-resurrect.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on for any unattended/overnight control room, or any seat where a watcher has ever silently crash-looped after a reload/engine-update — it converts an unbounded, invisible respawn churn into a bounded, loud, journaled hard stop. Leave off (default) for a byte-identical pane wrapper

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT
description: Journal-driven self-audit / gap-finder (HERD-238): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → the watcher runs journal-audit.sh on the housekeeping sweep cadence (~3 min), replaying a BOUNDED journal window (default 24h) for invariant violations: merge without reap; *_dispatched with no terminal past family TTL; refix_bounce without refix_wake_result; a merged HUMAN-VERIFY PR with no sha-keyed approval record (HERD-272); MAIN RED older than TTL; pushed=no never followed by pushed=yes; known-fixture slugs. Each NEW finding journals a journal_audit event (component=audit) and appends an operator-inbox row (source=audit, glyph 🔎). ADVISORY ONLY — never gates, never mutates. off (default) → byte-inert: no journal read, no write, no inbox row. FAIL-SOFT: empty/short/unreadable journal is silent exit 0. Pair with OPERATOR_INBOX=on to render the audit rows in the console section
when_to_surface: Turn on for an autonomous/unattended coordinator so journal-visible lifecycle gaps surface automatically instead of only when a human greps herd log; leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Watcher-affecting (takes effect on the next watcher restart). Never a merge gate

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_WINDOW_SECS
description: Lookback window for the JOURNAL_AUDIT self-audit (HERD-238): only journal events from the last N seconds are replayed for invariant violations. Default 86400 (24h). Bounds the audit's cost and keeps a long-healed incident from being re-found forever. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Raise in a repo whose journal is quiet enough that a 24h window misses violations that opened earlier; lower to make each sweep cheaper on a very busy journal

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_DISPATCH_TTL
description: Seconds a `*_dispatched` event may sit with no terminal outcome before the JOURNAL_AUDIT auditor reports a dispatch_no_outcome finding (HERD-238). Default 2700 (45 min) — comfortably longer than a full healthcheck suite, so a slow-but-live run is never a finding. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Raise when a legitimately long gate (a big heavy suite) trips false dispatch_no_outcome findings; lower to notice a genuinely lost dispatch sooner

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_REFIX_TTL
description: Seconds a `refix_bounce` may sit with no matching `refix_wake_result` (same pr + sha + round) before the JOURNAL_AUDIT auditor reports a refix_bounce_no_wake finding (HERD-238). Default 300 (5 min) — a wake is near-immediate, so a bounce still unmatched after this is a lost wake. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Raise if a slow agent pane makes the wake round-trip exceed 5 min; lower to catch a lost refix wake within one sweep

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_RED_TTL
description: Seconds a `main_health result=red` state may stand with no later green before the JOURNAL_AUDIT auditor reports a red_state_stale finding (HERD-238). Default 7200 (2h) — the class the 19h stale MAIN RED incident belongs to. Advisory only: the auditor never clears or re-runs the red. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Lower in a repo where a red default branch must be triaged within the hour; raise where merges are infrequent enough that a multi-hour red is expected and MAIN_HEALTH_RECHECK_MINS owns the recheck

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_MERGE_GRACE
description: Seconds after a `merge` event before a missing worktree reap for that pr/slug becomes a merge_without_reap finding for the JOURNAL_AUDIT auditor (HERD-238). Default 600 (10 min) — the reap runs on a later sweep, so a just-merged PR is inside the grace and never a finding. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Raise when the housekeeping sweep cadence is slow enough that a fresh merge false-flags; lower to notice a genuinely stranded worktree sooner

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_PUSHED_GRACE
description: Seconds after a `pushed=no` refresh event (codemap / symbol_index) before a missing later `pushed=yes` becomes a pushed_no_unresolved finding for the JOURNAL_AUDIT auditor (HERD-238). Default 1800 (30 min) — a commit awaiting the next push window is inside the grace. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the audit.
when_to_surface: Raise where pushes are batched on a long cadence; lower to catch a refresh that committed but never pushed within one sweep

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT
description: Journal-audit findings become ACTIONS — the universal never-stuck invariant (HERD-544): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). Requires JOURNAL_AUDIT=on, whose findings it acts on (with the auditor off there are no findings and this key is inert). GROUNDED in the operator north star of 2026-08-05 ("we keep getting stuck at points or hung up — there needs to be a way to ensure that doesn't happen, or if it does it can auto resolve and keep churning"): the engine already had the DETECTION half, but every finding was advisory, so stalls survived in the seam between rails — work that exists and no rail owns. on → each class maps to ONE bounded action via scripts/herd/journal-act.sh: a *_dispatched with no terminal past its family TTL frees the gate slot it still holds (HERD-185 corpse hygiene) so the next tick re-dispatches once; a refix_bounce with no wake is re-delivered ONCE to the builder's agent pane, and a wake that LANDS journals the missing refix_wake_result (closing the finding) while one that does not leaves it standing; a MAIN RED past JOURNAL_AUDIT_RED_TTL arms the main-health re-verify for the current HEAD; a merge with no reap runs the retirement invariant (HERD-164) now; ANY class with NO mapped action auto-files ONE dedup-keyed tracker item via the scribe so the gap becomes WORK. Each action fires AT MOST ONCE per finding key ACROSS SEATS (the shared-pool once-guard, pysrc/herd/store.py --once) and is journaled `audit_acted class=… result=…` with an operator-inbox row; a finding STILL standing after its action escalates loudly exactly once (journal + loud inbox row + a filed item) and is then silent forever — it never re-acts, so no action can loop. BOUNDED: at most 3 actions per housekeeping sweep and each rail wrapped in `timeout`, so a wedged rail delays a sweep by seconds and never holds the tick loop open; nothing is dropped, since the guards are keyed by finding and a skipped one acts on the next sweep. NEVER a merge gate, never a tracker-state write. off (default) → byte-inert: findings report exactly as the HERD-238 auditor always did. FAIL-SOFT everywhere (an unavailable store/rail/scribe degrades to an honest result token, never a red row). Adopted by the `yolo` posture (templates/postures.tsv)
when_to_surface: Turn on together with JOURNAL_AUDIT=on for an unattended/autonomous coordinator that must keep churning without a human unsticking it — it is the safety net under every other auto lever, and the only thing that turns an unhealable stall class into a filed work item. Leave off (default) when you want the auditor to observe and report only, or while you are still reading its findings to decide which classes deserve a rail. Watcher-affecting (the action pass runs on the housekeeping sweep). Never a merge gate

name: JOURNAL_AUDIT_ESCALATE_AFTER
description: Re-observations a MAPPED journal-audit finding may survive, still standing, before JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT's lifecycle pass escalates it loudly exactly once (HERD-564/573). Default 2 — one sweep of grace before escalating, so a finding that clears on its own between sweeps is never escalated. Shares JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT's SAME per-sweep action budget (HERD_JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT_MAX) — an escalation is a real scribe shellout, not a free journal line — but is the SEPARATE "how many sweeps of grace" knob, not a per-class action cap. Read by scripts/herd/journal-audit.sh, which re-sources herd-config.sh on every sweep, so a change takes effect on the next audit run with no watcher restart. Any non-numeric value reads as the default (_num_or), so a typo can never widen or narrow the grace window. Inert whenever JOURNAL_AUDIT_ACT is off, since no action pass runs at all in that state.
when_to_surface: Lower (e.g. 1) to escalate a standing finding on its very next sighting for a coordinator that wants the loudest possible signal; raise to grant a slower-cadence sweep more rounds of grace before an unresolved finding becomes a filed tracker item. Watcher-affecting, takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: LIFECYCLE_CONTRACTS
description: Supervised-process contract (HERD-193): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> every population herdkit spawns records the four lifecycle properties at spawn via lifecycle.sh (OWNER: which component spawned it, journaled at spawn; DEADLINE: the max lifetime after which it is presumed hung, REUSED from that population's existing timeout — REVIEW_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT for reviewers, HEALTH_INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT for health/main-health workers, DRAINER_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT for the scribe/research drainers, and a deliberately generous 30 min for the backgrounded builder-lane / resolver-lane workers (HERD-268), whose spawn epoch is stamped at dispatch, before they queue behind the resolver lane lock — so no new tunables appear; LIVENESS: a worker pid or a drainer heartbeat file; RETIRE: the existing owner an expiry routes to), and a per-tick watcher sweep (_sweep_lifecycle) journals lifecycle_spawn / lifecycle_retire / lifecycle_expired and appends one operator-inbox row per newly-expired process. OBSERVABILITY-ONLY: never kills, never gates, never merges — teardown stays with each population's existing owner (gate corpse sweep, drainer reclaim, stall detector, resolver escalation). A process that has EXITED is retired by the sweep (the reconcile layer: a worker that died before its teardown is still accounted for) — after a short grace so the population's own teardown journals the TRUE reason first; a process that goes healthy again re-arms the once-only expiry notice. A stale drainer heartbeat is CORROBORATED against the agent's real liveness before it is called a hang (HERD-122): a dead agent is retired, only a live-but-silent one expires, and an unprobeable one is left alone. off (default) -> byte-inert: no record written, no journal event, no inbox row, no sweep read. FAIL-SOFT: an unreadable pid/heartbeat is treated as ALIVE (blindness is never evidence of death). Pair with OPERATOR_INBOX=on to render the expiry rows in the console
when_to_surface: Turn on for an unattended/autonomous coordinator so a lingering process (a hung drainer, a reviewer past the corpse-sweep deadline, a health worker that died verdictless) is attributable in the journal and visible in the operator inbox instead of requiring process archaeology; leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Watcher-affecting (takes effect on the next watcher restart). Never a merge gate

name: OPERATOR_INBOX
description: Cross-seat OPERATOR INBOX (HERD-184): so coordination messages left as comments reach an autonomous coordinator automatically. off (default) | on. OFF -> byte-inert: no inbox reader runs, no fetch, no console section, output identical to today. ON -> each watcher tick (throttled on an interval, not every 4s repaint) surfaces NEW comments by OTHER authors as a 'operator inbox' console section (needs-you-adjacent, above the in-flight rows) plus one notify-once per comment id. TWO feeds, one surface: (1) PR-COMMENT feed -- new comments by non-self authors on the open PRs this seat authored or is gating (the tick's already-fetched PR set), read with a dedicated gated `gh pr view --json comments` (the core tick's --json field set is UNCHANGED); (2) TRACKER feed -- new comments by other operators on items this seat claimed/marked, read via the active SCRIBE_BACKEND's OPTIONAL _backend_list_inbox_comments op (implemented for linear; absent on file/github/jira -> that feed is simply empty). Comment ids are cached in a seen-ledger so each surfaces/notifies exactly ONCE; the section renders the most-recent entries newest-first. ADDITIVE + FAIL-SOFT by contract: a missing reader, an api error, or absent credentials yields an EMPTY inbox, NEVER a red row; scoped strictly to display/notify and never touches the gate loop or a merge decision. Opt-in, never self-activates; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart
when_to_surface: Set to on for an autonomous/unattended coordinator so cross-seat requests left as PR or tracker comments (e.g. a 'don't self-merge, main broke' note) are surfaced automatically instead of being silently missed; leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Pairs with the tracker backend (linear) for the tracker feed

name: ORPHAN_PR_ROWS
description: ORPHAN-PR advisory console section (HERD-330): off (default) | on. Surfaces open PRs the worktree-gated watcher never adopts. The watcher discovers work via git worktrees, so an OPEN PR with no live builder worktree in this workspace — a collaborator PR, a main-checkout PR, or a PR whose worktree was reaped — sits ungated and today invisible. ON -> every render/reconcile tick REWRITES a ledger with one row per such PR, computed from the tick's ALREADY-fetched open-PR roster (PRS_JSON) minus the PRs the discovered worktrees claim (DYNAMIC discovery: zero extra gh, self-correcting the instant a worktree adopts the PR or it closes), and renders an 'orphan PRs' section (needs-you-adjacent, above the in-flight rows) via the shared bounded-section helper (console-section.sh). OFF -> byte-inert: no scan, no ledger, no section, output identical to today. ADVISORY + FAIL-SOFT by contract: never gates, never merges, never a red row; a failed open-PR fetch (PRS_LOOKUP_OK=0) is never fabricated into 'no orphans'. Opt-in, never self-activates; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart
when_to_surface: Turn on for an autonomous/unattended coordinator so an open PR no local builder owns (a teammate's PR, a hand-pushed branch) is visible on the watcher console instead of silently ungated; leave off (default) for a byte-identical console. Never a merge gate

name: ADOPT_REMOTE_PRS
description: Auto-ADOPT ungated remote PRs into the worktree pool (HERD-369): off (default) | on. Builds ON TOP of the ORPHAN_PR_ROWS (HERD-330) open-PR-vs-pool diff (same already-fetched roster, zero extra gh): on a throttled ~60s cadence (not the 4s repaint), for each OPEN, NON-DRAFT PR that diff finds no discovered worktree owns, and whose branch is not already checked out ANYWHERE (this workspace's pool, the main checkout, or a stray manual worktree) — `git fetch` + `git worktree add` its branch into WORKTREES_DIR/<slug> (slug = the branch name with every "/" flattened to "-"), so the worktree-gated watcher discovers and gates it on the VERY NEXT tick instead of sitting ungated until a human hand-runs `git worktree add` (GROUNDED: PRs #462/#463 sat ~16-18h on 2026-07-13, #478 ~18h on 2026-07-15). A SUCCESSFUL adopt is sha-keyed once-guarded ($WORKTREES_DIR/.agent-watch-adopted-prs) so a re-tick never re-adopts an already-adopted branch. A FAILURE is deliberately NOT once-guarded — a transient fetch/worktree-add failure (network blip, momentary ref lock) is not a completed operation and self-heals on the next scan, so the attempt retries every ~60s; only the `adopt_failed` journal EVENT is deduped per (pr,sha) ($WORKTREES_DIR/.agent-watch-adopt-failed-seen, a separate ledger) so a still-broken branch never spams the journal — a new sha (a fresh push) always re-journals. Never adopts a draft. FAIL-SOFT throughout: never a red row, never an abort; a failed open-PR fetch (PRS_LOOKUP_OK=0) is never fabricated into "nothing to adopt". Multi-seat: keyed off observed GitHub PR state each tick (any seat may adopt); `git worktree add` is naturally exclusive per branch within one seat's checkout. off (default) -> byte-inert: no scan, no fetch, no worktree add, no ledger, output identical to today. INDEPENDENT of ORPHAN_PR_ROWS — either works without the other. Opt-in, never self-activates; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart
when_to_surface: Turn on for an autonomous/unattended coordinator so an open collaborator/fork PR with no local worktree is pulled into the gated pool automatically instead of sitting invisible until a human runs `git worktree add`; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior. Never a merge gate — only widens what the watcher discovers

name: TEAM_PRESENCE
description: TEAMMATE BUILDER VISIBILITY on the ungated-PR rows (HERD-527/HERD-663/HERD-661, GitHub issue #639 phases 1+2): off (default) | on | live. The watcher discovers work through LOCAL git worktrees, so a PR a TEAMMATE is actively building on THEIR machine has no builder record here and renders in the unconditional 'ungated PRs' section as 'ungated - no builder record - enable ADOPT_REMOTE_PRS or git worktree add to adopt'. Under WATCHER_SCOPE=all (the team posture) that nudge is not merely uninformative, it is actively WRONG: adopting a branch someone else is mid-build on is the last thing an operator should do, and the console reads 'nobody is on this' about work that is very much being done (GROUNDED: emberglen-godot, two operators). ON -> on a throttled ~60s cadence (never the 4s repaint) the watcher REUSES the existing claim machinery rather than inventing a presence channel: a claim already sets the item's assignee AND moves it to in-progress (HERD-50/HERD-244), and every PR body already carries `Refs: <id>` (HERD-522). So each UNGATED PR is resolved to its tracker item -- first through the SHARED decoration-tolerant `Refs:` parser (scripts/herd/pr-ref.sh, so a `## Refs:` heading resolves here exactly as it does at merge-time reconcile), else through a TOKEN-EXACT branch-name match (feat/herd-527-x -> HERD-527; never a prefix/substring, so HERD-52 can not claim HERD-527's branch) -- and that item's live state + assignee are read through the active SCRIBE_BACKEND's OPTIONAL read-only rich roster op (_backend_list_open_rich, the same op `herd backlog --rich` reads): ONE tracker round-trip per scan no matter how many PRs are ungated, cached in a ledger ($WORKTREES_DIR/.agent-watch-team-presence, rewritten whole each scan so it self-corrects) that every 4s repaint reads from memory. An item that is IN PROGRESS (state TYPE started|indeterminate -- the machine key, never the renameable human label) and ASSIGNED renders the compact person-emoji row '👤 #<pr> <title> · <name> - building <id>' (HERD-663; replaces the older, wordier 'ungated here - <assignee> building <id> on their machine'; <name> honors TEAM_ALIASES when configured, else the tracker's own display name) with the adopt nudge SUPPRESSED on that row; in-progress but UNASSIGNED, not started, or resolving to nothing all keep today's row verbatim. STRICTLY READ-ONLY: it writes no tracker state, opens no channel, and never gates or merges. FAIL-SOFT by one rule -- the ledger is only ever the product of a COMPLETE successful resolution, so a tracker that is down, a backend with no rich op (file/github/changelog), or no python3 leaves it EMPTY and every row renders exactly as today; a transient `gh` body-fetch failure instead leaves the last-known ledger untouched and retries next scan (the PRS_LOOKUP_OK discipline), so a blip never silently degrades the join. LIVE (HERD-661, GH #639 phase 2) -> everything ON does, PLUS a real cross-machine live channel (team-presence-live.sh), REUSING resolver-claim.sh's proven substrate rather than inventing a new one: on the SAME throttled ~60s tick, this seat PUBLISHES a versioned, epoch-stamped, HTML-hidden marker comment (never a Statuses/Check-Run write) onto each of ITS OWN open PRs it is actively building (no PR = nothing published -- the tracker claim already covers pre-PR intent; a PR ADOPTED from another author is never published to, since this seat is gating it, not building it), and CONSUMES every already-attributed PR's marker to append a freshness clause to the compact row: '👤 #<pr> <title> · <name> — building <id> · active 2m ago' inside the 300s staleness window, else '· last active 3h ago (stale?)'. Seat-symmetric (multi-seat doctrine): every seat runs the identical publish leg for its own PRs and the identical consume leg for every teammate's -- no seat-specific special-casing. FAIL-SOFT per row: an absent/unreachable marker (channel down, or a teammate still on plain ON) leaves that row exactly ON's rendering, never a stale-looking blank or a crash. OFF (default) -> byte-inert: no gh, no backend call, no ledger written or read, every console byte identical to before. Opt-in, never self-activates; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart
when_to_surface: Turn on for a MULTI-OPERATOR project (especially with WATCHER_SCOPE=all) so a teammate's in-flight PR reads as 'someone is building this' instead of an adopt nudge that would fight them for the branch; step up to live once phase 1's join is trusted, to also see WHETHER that build is still actually running or has gone quiet; leave off (default) for a solo seat and a byte-identical console. Surface it when an operator asks why a teammate's PR shows 'ungated - no builder record', when explaining that who-is-building comes from the CLAIM (assignee + in-progress) while liveness comes from the marker channel, or when a '(stale?)' row prompts "is that build still going?" Never a merge gate

name: TEAM_ALIASES
description: Machine-scoped display-name overrides for the ungated-PR person-emoji rows (HERD-663): both the TEAM_PRESENCE attributed row (👤 #<pr> <title> · <name> - building <id>) and the AUTHOR FALLBACK row below (👤 #<pr> <title> · authored by <author> (no tracker claim)) resolve their displayed identity through this SAME lookup. Format: comma-separated handle=Name pairs, e.g. 'nouvertnec84=Chase,anotherhandle=Other Name' -- <handle> is matched case-insensitively against the tracker assignee (TEAM_PRESENCE) or the PR author login (author fallback); a hit substitutes <Name>, a miss (or the key left empty/unset) falls back to whatever was already resolved -- a tracker's own display name when the backend provides one, else the raw handle. Empty (default) -> byte-inert passthrough: every row shows exactly what the tracker/gh already gave it. FAIL-SOFT: a malformed pair (no '=', an empty name) is silently skipped, never a crash, never a red row. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Set on a machine (via `herd config set --local TEAM_ALIASES ...`) where the tracker or `gh` only surfaces a raw login for a teammate/collaborator, to show a friendlier name on the ungated-PR rows; leave unset for a byte-identical console. Purely cosmetic, never a merge gate

name: OSS_TRIAGE
description: OSS auto-triage (HERD-255 / HERD-168 part 1/3): off (default) | on. OFF → byte-inert: `herd triage` / oss-triage.sh touch no gh, no research queue, no report files. ON → list open issues on HERD_REPO, enqueue a research-lane classify+draft request per NEW issue (bug/feature/question/duplicate + suggested reply/labels), write a ranked shortlist under $WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/oss-triage/ for human approval. NEVER auto-posts (no issue comment/close/label). FAIL-SOFT (missing HERD_REPO / gh error → empty shortlist). Additive + opt-in; never self-activates
when_to_surface: Set to on for an OSS project that wants automated issue classification + draft replies surfaced to the coordinator without auto-posting; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: BUDGET_DAILY
description: Daily spend CEILING in USD (HERD-95): ENFORCE a budget, don't just MEASURE it. `herd cost` already prices every builder/review/agent session and journals a `cost` event at merge; this key turns that ledger into a rail. EMPTY (default) = DORMANT: byte-identical to no budget. Set it to a USD number and, when TODAY's (UTC) recorded spend — summed from the journal's `cost` events by cost.sh cost_day_total, so NO cost math is reimplemented — EXCEEDS it, TWO enforcement points engage: (1) the watcher PAUSES draining the durable spawn queue (agent-watch.sh _drain_spawn_queue), journaling budget_drain_paused once per over-budget stretch and budget_drain_resumed when spend falls back under; (2) each builder lane (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh) REFUSES a new spawn with one loud 🛑 line BEFORE any worktree/tab is created, journaling budget_spawn_refused. OVERRIDABLE: HERD_FORCE_SPAWN=1 (or a lane's --force) spawns anyway and journals budget_spawn_forced. FAIL-SOFT: a missing journal / no python3 / a non-numeric value never blocks a spawn. Consumed by agent-watch.sh + the lanes via cost.sh.
when_to_surface: Set to a USD ceiling (e.g. 25) for an unattended/autonomous run so a runaway day stops spawning new builders automatically instead of only surfacing when a human reads `herd cost`; leave empty (default) for no ceiling. This is the ENFORCEMENT half of the cost program — `herd cost` measures, BUDGET_DAILY enforces. Watcher-affecting (drain pause) on the next watcher restart; the lanes read it live per spawn.

name: MODEL_ESCALATE_GLOB
description: Egrep -i pattern of task text that forces the escalation target model in either lane — MODEL_ESCALATE if set, else MODEL_FEATURE — overriding MODEL_QUICK and any per-spawn HERD_QUICK_MODEL/HERD_FEATURE_MODEL override (deterministic model step-up, analogous to HEALTHCHECK_HEAVY_GLOB); blank (default) → off
when_to_surface: Set when judgment-heavy engine surfaces keep getting routed through the cheap quick lane and misbuilding, so those tasks deterministically get the escalation-tier model without a per-spawn override

name: MODEL_ESCALATE
description: The model a matched MODEL_ESCALATE_GLOB forces (HERD-376); blank (default) → the glob forces MODEL_FEATURE exactly as before (byte-identical). Accepts a bare model id or a runtime-qualified '<driver>:<model>' ref (HERD-151), resolved through the same shim as every other MODEL_* key
when_to_surface: Set when MODEL_FEATURE itself has been lowered to a cheaper default (e.g. HERD-102's sonnet default) so the escalation glob no longer provides a stronger-model backstop on its own — name a specific stronger model here for judgment-heavy surfaces without raising the whole feature lane's default

name: REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB
description: Egrep pattern of changed-file paths that opts into RISK-TIERED pre-merge review (analogous to HEALTHCHECK_HEAVY_GLOB / MODEL_ESCALATE_GLOB); blank (default) → off, every PR gets the full $MODEL_REVIEW (Opus) review UNCHANGED. When set: paths matching it (engine surface) or a diff over REVIEW_ESCALATE_MAXFILES files → STRONG tier ($MODEL_REVIEW); a docs/test-only diff (only *.md and tests/) → review SKIPPED with a source=skipped-low-risk PASS recorded (no reviewer spawned, still sha-cached); any other small low-risk diff → CHEAP tier ($REVIEW_MODEL_CHEAP). Classification fails SAFE (unreadable/empty diff → STRONG)
when_to_surface: Set to reserve the expensive Opus review for engine-critical paths and large diffs, cutting the single biggest recurring engine cost. Tradeoff: a cheaper reviewer can miss subtle bugs and glob/size classification can misjudge a risky diff, so scope the glob to genuinely engine-critical paths

name: REVIEW_MODEL_CHEAP
description: Cheaper reviewer model tier used for small, low-risk diffs when REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB tiering is active (default: claude-sonnet-4-6); ignored when REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB is blank
when_to_surface: Override to pick the low-risk reviewer tier (e.g. a different sonnet/haiku model); only takes effect once REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB opts into tiered review

name: REVIEW_ESCALATE_MAXFILES
description: Under REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB tiering, a diff touching MORE than this many files escalates to the STRONG tier even without a glob match (default: 10; non-numeric → 10); ignored when REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB is blank
when_to_surface: Lower to send more diffs to the full review, raise to let larger low-risk diffs use the cheap tier

name: DOCS_ONLY_GLOB
description: Egrep pattern (HERD-89) that opts a PR's review into the cheapest DOCS tier when EVERY changed path matches it; blank (default) → off, byte-identical. Activates the risk-tiered review on its own (REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB need not be set): a diff where every path matches routes to $REVIEW_MODEL_DOCS (a real, cheap adversarial review — NOT the *.md/tests SKIP). ESCALATION WINS: a docs diff also matching REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB, or over REVIEW_ESCALATE_MAXFILES files, is STRONG regardless. Classification fails SAFE (unreadable/empty diff → STRONG)
when_to_surface: Set (e.g. '\.(md|txt)$') to review pure-docs diffs on the cheapest model instead of the full/cheap tier; pin engine-dir docs (e.g. templates/) into REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB so they escalate rather than downgrade

name: REVIEW_MODEL_DOCS
description: Cheapest reviewer model tier used for pure-docs diffs when DOCS_ONLY_GLOB matches every changed path (default: claude-haiku-4-5); ignored when DOCS_ONLY_GLOB is blank
when_to_surface: Override to pick the docs-tier reviewer model; only takes effect once DOCS_ONLY_GLOB opts a diff into the docs tier

name: REVIEW_MODEL_ESCALATED
description: Reviewer model tier the pre-merge gate ESCALATES to once a PR has burned enough failed refix rounds: the next review is forced up to this strong tier regardless of the REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB size/path classification. Default claude-opus-4-8. Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (the shipped live review dispatch, HERD-580 port); the bash body (agent-watch.sh) is unreachable since P5b and kept only for its own unit test.
when_to_surface: Override to pin the repeated-failure escalation tier; leave default for Opus-on-struggling-PR.

name: REVIEW_PREGATE
description: Mechanical-red PRE-GATE before the LLM review (HERD-559): off (default) | on. off -> byte-inert, every (pr,sha) reaches the reviewer exactly as today. on -> the cheap deterministic lint set (caps-sync, config-manifest ghost/dead-key scan, journal-emission, pipe-safety, git-scope, doc-drift, via scripts/herd/review-pregate.sh) runs FIRST; a red records a sha-keyed BLOCK with provenance source=pregate, journals review_pregate_red, bounces the builder with the lint output, and dispatches NO reviewer — so a mechanical red costs zero review slot and the adversarial reviewer only ever sees mechanically-clean diffs. BASELINE-SUBTRACTED: a finding also present at the merge base is not this diff's and never bounces anyone. Any inability to compute that baseline SKIPS the pre-gate (the reviewer runs as today) — a false pre-gate red would wedge a PR on a red its builder cannot fix. Consumed by agent-watch.sh, herd-review.sh and pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py
when_to_surface: Set to on once the lint set is trusted, to stop spending a ~5-minute adversarial review to report what a lint answers in seconds. Leave off (default) for byte-identical dispatch; watcher-affecting, so it takes effect on the next watcher restart

name: REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR
description: Small-mechanical-diff FLOOR on the review tiering (HERD-559): off (default) | on. on -> a diff whose every changed file is a TSV row edit, a pure (100%-similarity) rename, or a version bump, and which is within REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR_MAXFILES / REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR_MAXLINES and matches no REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB path, routes to $REVIEW_MODEL_CHEAP even when no tiering glob is configured — such a diff carries no correctness surface for an adversarial reviewer, so paying the strong tier for it is pure latency. A FLOOR, never an override: it is consulted ONLY where the tier would otherwise be the STRONG default, so it can lower a tier and never raise one, and the evidence-triggered escalation still wins. Fails safe in one direction: any shape it cannot positively recognize keeps today's tier. off -> no classification, byte-inert
when_to_surface: Set to on alongside REVIEW_PREGATE to stop spending the strong reviewer on manifest-row, rename and version-bump commits; leave off (default) for byte-identical tier selection

name: REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR_MAXFILES
description: Under REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR, a diff touching MORE than this many files is never treated as small-and-mechanical whatever its shape (default: 5; non-numeric -> 5); ignored when REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR is off
when_to_surface: Raise to let a slightly larger mechanical diff (a wide manifest edit) still take the cheap tier; lower to tighten the floor

name: REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR_MAXLINES
description: Under REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR, a diff changing MORE than this many lines is never treated as small-and-mechanical whatever its shape (default: 40; non-numeric -> 40); ignored when REVIEW_MECH_FLOOR is off
when_to_surface: Raise to let a longer run of manifest rows still take the cheap tier; lower to tighten the floor

name: REVIEW_TIERING
description: Activate the RISK-TIER classification inside the LIVE Python engine core (HERD-559): off (default) | on. The bash reference path in agent-watch.sh has always tiered on REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB / DOCS_ONLY_GLOB alone and is unchanged by this key; the HERD-306 engine port never carried that classification across, so on the live core every PR dispatches $MODEL_REVIEW regardless of those globs. on -> the ported classifier runs: a docs/test-only diff SKIPs the reviewer with a source=skipped-low-risk PASS, an escalate-glob or over-REVIEW_ESCALATE_MAXFILES diff takes $MODEL_REVIEW, a DOCS_ONLY_GLOB diff takes $REVIEW_MODEL_DOCS, and anything else takes $REVIEW_MODEL_CHEAP. Ship-dormant on purpose: flipping it changes WHICH model reviews a PR and whether a docs-only diff is reviewed at all, which is the operator's call and never an upgrade's side effect. off -> the live core's dispatch is byte-identical to today's
when_to_surface: Set to on to make an already-configured REVIEW_ESCALATE_GLOB / DOCS_ONLY_GLOB actually take effect on the live engine core; leave off (default) until the tier choice has been reviewed, since a cheaper reviewer can miss subtle bugs

name: REVIEW_LATENCY
description: Journal a review_latency event as each review verdict is collected (HERD-559): on (default) | off. The event carries the dispatch->verdict wall-clock seconds together with the verdict that produced them, so the review ceiling the fast path attacks is MEASURED rather than estimated (per tier on the bash leg). Pure TELEMETRY: no gate, dispatch or merge decision reads it, which is why it ships on rather than dormant. off is a hard no-op — no event, byte-identical journals
when_to_surface: Leave on to keep review latency measurable in the journal (herd log / journal-audit); set to off only to keep a journal byte-identical to a pre-HERD-559 baseline

name: REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ESCALATE_ROUNDS
description: How many failed REVIEW-rail refix rounds a PR must accumulate before a cheap-tier reviewer PASS is distrusted and the next review is forced up to REVIEW_MODEL_ESCALATED. Default 2; unset/empty → 2, any other non-numeric value → never escalate (fail safe). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py (the shipped live review dispatch, HERD-580 port); the bash body (agent-watch.sh) is unreachable since P5b and kept only for its own unit test.
when_to_surface: Lower to escalate sooner on a struggling PR; raise to give the cheap tier more rounds first.

name: REVIEW_LOG_KEEP
description: How many pre-merge review logs to retain per PR in the rolling review-log tracker (herd-review.sh); older logs fall off. Default 5; non-numeric → 5.
when_to_surface: Raise to keep more review history per PR; lower to trim disk use.

name: RUBRIC_FILE
description: Repo-relative path to a structured per-unit REVIEW RUBRIC (HERD-400, docs/rubric-primitive.md): TSV rows id/text/weight(required|advisory)/pass_condition. Resolved with the SAME worktree-then-main lookup as REVIEW_CHECKLIST.
