When set and the file exists, herd-review.sh renders the criteria as an explicit checklist in all four reviewer prompt sites and asks for one 'RUBRIC: <id> | PASS|FAIL | <reason>' line per criterion, written into the review result file ahead of the final verdict; pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's parse_rubric_verdicts extracts them into a rubric_verdicts journal event. The rubric is advisory input to the reviewer's own judgement ONLY — the single REVIEW: PASS/BLOCK/INFRA-FAIL line still alone decides the merge, unchanged. Default '' (off) is byte-identical: no rubric block in any prompt, no rubric_verdicts event
when_to_surface: When a project wants its pre-merge reviewer to explicitly reason about (and leave a forensic trail for) a small set of named per-unit criteria, beyond the freeform REVIEW_CHECKLIST risk list

name: DEP_POLL_MIN
description: Initial dep-watcher poll interval in seconds; also the value a state change resets the capped-exponential backoff to (default: 30)
when_to_surface: Lower for snappier dep pickup at more polling cost, raise to poll less often; consumed by dep-watcher.sh

name: DEP_POLL_MAX
description: Maximum dep-watcher poll interval in seconds after backoff widens it while open deps sit unchanged tick-over-tick (default: 300)
when_to_surface: Raise to let long-pending deps be polled even less aggressively over time, lower to keep a floor on responsiveness; consumed by dep-watcher.sh

name: DEP_STALE_TTL
description: Seconds a still-open dep may go without movement before it surfaces as `stalled` (loudly, but never a freeze); dep-watcher applies it to blocked-on deps, agent-watch applies it to a HELD spawn intent (after=<dep>, HERD-94); 0 disables stall surfacing (default: 86400)
when_to_surface: Lower to be warned about a stalled upstream / held spawn sooner, raise to tolerate longer-pending deps, 0 to turn stall surfacing off entirely

name: .herd/links
description: Cross-repo link registry: name|owner/repo|backend|target rows; enables herd report --to and herd link list
when_to_surface: When filing issues against peer repos or routing engine bugs to specific trackers across services

name: .herd/deps
description: Cross-repo dependency list polled by dep-watcher.sh; each row marks a feature as blocked-on an upstream PR
when_to_surface: When a feature waits on a peer-repo PR to merge first; dep-watcher transitions state when upstream merges

name: .herd/secrets
description: API-backend credentials (e.g. LINEAR_API_KEY; jira: JIRA_BASE_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/JIRA_API_TOKEN [+optional JIRA_PROJECT_KEY, JIRA_ISSUE_TYPE]); gitignored and sourced by scribe-step and cmd_backlog
when_to_surface: Required for linear, jira, or other API backends; never put credentials in the committed .herd/config

name: HUMAN-VERIFY:
description: PR-body marker a builder emits to declare manual steps it could not run itself (one step per line); the watcher parses it and holds that PR for sha-keyed approval instead of auto-merging, a new commit re-holds
when_to_surface: When a change has a manual/live verification step (smoke test, UI or pane check, running-app dependency) that the automated gates cannot exercise before merge

name: herd-watch-<workspace>
description: Per-workspace argv0 the watcher (agent-watch.sh) re-execs itself under at startup, so a running watcher is attributable to exactly one workspace in ps/pgrep; herd reload/stop reap only THIS project's watchers (lockfile PID union argv0 match) and never a sibling workspace's, even though both run the identical engine script
when_to_surface: When attributing or reaping a watcher across parallel projects: match pgrep -f "herd-watch-<WORKSPACE_NAME>" / ps -o command= first token, not the bare agent-watch.sh which is process-indistinguishable across projects

name: HERD_REQUIRE_PROJECT_CONFIG
description: Console-strict config binding: set to 1 by the long-running consoles (agent-watch/herd-watch/backlog-view/coordinator) before sourcing herd-config.sh, so a console whose config resolves ONLY via the rule-3 engine-dogfood fallback (no HERD_CONFIG_FILE, no .herd/config walking up from $PWD) REFUSES rather than silently binding to the engine repo (issue #60); normal `herd <cmd>` CLI usage never sets it, so its intentional dogfood fallback is unchanged
when_to_surface: Internal guard the consoles set themselves; surface only when explaining why a console refused to start or how the launch-binding guard works

name: HERD_ALLOW_FOREIGN_CWD
description: Escape hatch for the launch-binding guard (issue #60): set to 1 to let a console start from a $PWD outside its resolved PROJECT_ROOT and to permit the rule-3 engine-dogfood config fallback under HERD_REQUIRE_PROJECT_CONFIG; the startup banner still prints the resolved WORKSPACE_NAME/PROJECT_ROOT
when_to_surface: When a console is intentionally launched from outside its project tree (a deliberate cross-dir or dogfood run) and the foreign-cwd/config refusal must be bypassed

name: HERD_CONFIG_ENV_OK
description: Escape hatch for the HERD-465 engine-core RESET: set to 1/true/yes/on to skip the pre-source unset of the engine-core config keys (MERGE_POLICY, HEALTH_CONCURRENCY, HUMAN_VERIFY_POLICY, the INFRA_BREAKER_* pair, etc. — the full list is _HERD_ENGINE_CORE_KEYS in herd-config.sh) so a caller's own pre-exported values win even when a real .herd/config or config.local exists to read. Without it, herd-config.sh always treats an on-disk config file as authoritative over inherited/stale exported env (fixing the WATCHER_SELF_RESTART re-exec sticky-env bug) — EXCEPT when HERD_CONFIG_FILE points at a path that does not exist on disk (no config.local sibling either), which is the hermetic test/sim seam (scripts/herd/sim/sandbox-*-scenario.sh, many tests/test-*.sh) that deliberately pre-exports these exact keys with no config file at all; that seam already works without setting this flag
when_to_surface: Only when a caller genuinely needs its own pre-exported engine-core value to beat a REAL on-disk project config — no shipped caller needs this today

name: scripts/herd/cost.sh
description: The token/cost SUMMER + PERISHABLE model→$ price table (single source of truth, dated "as of 2026-06-24"). Sums a Claude transcript's assistant-message usage (input/output/cache-read/cache-write) deduped by message id, classifies builder vs in-worktree review sessions by a stable reviewer fingerprint, prices each by model, and journals `cost` events at merge time (agent-watch.sh do_merge). Override the table via HERD_COST_PRICE_FILE (also the hermetic test seam); read the results with `herd cost`
when_to_surface: When updating pricing after an Anthropic price change or new model, verifying cost figures, or explaining where cost-per-merged-PR numbers come from — this file is the perishable price table to keep current

name: .herd-limit-sentinel
description: Per-worktree sentinel file written by the rate_limit StopFailure Claude Code hook (generated into <worktree>/.claude/settings.json by herd_write_ratelimit_hook on worktree creation) when a builder's turn ends on the account usage limit; its contents are the reset time from the banner. The watcher (agent-watch.sh _detect_limit_hit) polls it as the PRIMARY, version-robust limit-hit signal — far better than scraping the banner — then schedules an in-place `claude --continue` resume at the reset. A banner-scrape fallback (last assistant transcript line matches the usage-limit banner) covers environments where the hook is unavailable
when_to_surface: When explaining how the watcher detects a builder frozen on the usage limit, or why a builder shows a "limit-hit · auto-resume at HH:MM" row instead of "idle · no PR"

name: HERD_LIMIT_HOOK
description: Set to off to skip generating the rate_limit StopFailure hook into new worktrees (herd_write_ratelimit_hook); the watcher then relies on the banner-scrape fallback for limit detection
when_to_surface: When a project cannot use the project-level hook (unsupported Claude Code version) or wants to opt out of the generated .claude/settings.json hook

name: HERD_LIMIT_DETECT
description: Set to off to disable usage-limit detection + auto-resume entirely (kill-switch for agent-watch.sh _detect_limit_hit); default on
when_to_surface: When the limit-auto-resume feature must be turned off wholesale, e.g. debugging a false-positive limit detection

name: HERD_FORCE_SPAWN
description: Set to 1 to bypass the advisory pre-spawn review-gate saturation check (herd-spawn-gate.sh) and the no-tracker-ref spawn refusal, forcing a builder spawn through and journaling the bypass; equivalent to passing --force/-f before the slug on herd-quick.sh/herd-feature.sh. Off (default) → gates apply unchanged
when_to_surface: When an urgent item must spawn a builder despite a saturated review queue or with no tracker ref, and the operator accepts the override — the explicit escape hatch the gate points to

name: HERD_AGENT
description: Set to an agent-definition NAME (.herd/agents/<name>.md) to build ONE item with that SPECIALIST AGENT (HERD-667). Honored by herd-feature.sh, herd-quick.sh and spawn.sh (which threads it to the watcher's drain through the durable queue's .agent sidecar, so a QUEUED spawn selects the same agent a direct lane invocation would). Set + the runtime has a by-name selector → the driver's DRIVER_AGENT_SELECT_FLAG is appended to the spawn's <flags>; set + it has none → the definition body is injected into the task spec. A name the verify cache says does NOT resolve prints a LOUD warning and spawns ANYWAY — never a block. UNSET (default) → byte-identical spawn argv and task spec. Companion knobs, all optional and all env-only (never .herd/config keys): HERD_AGENTS_DIR overrides the roster location, HERD_AGENT_VERIFY_MODEL picks the model `herd agents verify` probes with (default MODEL_QUICK), HERD_AGENT_TEMPLATE overrides the scaffold template, and HERD_AGENT_DEFINITION_ROOT rebinds the user-scope lookup root a driver's DRIVER_AGENT_DEFINITION_DIR expands (the same knob shape $HERD_TRANSCRIPT_ROOT gives DRIVER_AGENT_SESSION_ID)
when_to_surface: When one item wants a domain specialist rather than a generic builder — prefix the lane or the enqueue: HERD_AGENT=<name> scripts/herd/spawn.sh <slug> feature "<task>". Run `herd agents verify <name>` first on a machine where that runtime is installed, or the selection can be silently ignored

name: HERDKIT_HOME
description: Install/checkout path for the herdkit engine (default ~/.herdkit). Used by install.sh (managed install target), `herd update` (git pull --ff-only in the engine checkout), and packaging (npm/homebrew) — not a .herd/config key; an operator/installer env override only
when_to_surface: When installing the engine somewhere other than ~/.herdkit (`HERDKIT_HOME=/path bash install.sh`) or pointing tooling at a non-default engine checkout

name: HERD_LIMIT_RESUME_BUFFER
description: Seconds to wait AFTER the parsed reset time before relaunching a limit-blocked builder via `claude --continue` (default 60); avoids racing the account quota's exact reset instant
when_to_surface: When resumes fire a hair too early and re-hit the limit — raise the buffer; the reset time itself is parsed from the banner/sentinel

name: HERD_LIMIT_UNKNOWN_WAIT
description: Seconds to hold a limit-blocked builder before resuming when the reset time could NOT be parsed (default 18000 ≈ one 5h rolling window); better to wait out a window than hammer a still-blocked account
when_to_surface: When the banner format changes and reset times stop parsing, tune how long the watcher waits before a blind resume attempt

name: COORDINATOR_WATCHDOG
description: on | off (default off): opt-in coordinator auto-resume. When on, the watcher revives a limit-parked coordinator the same way it revives builders — at the reset+buffer it relaunches the coordinator in place via `claude --continue`. Only ever acts on a CONFIRMED park (limit sentinel/banner present AND its agent not 'working'); never touches a healthy coordinator; a WORKSPACE_NAME-keyed launch lock prevents double-launch; a failed resume escalates via notification without looping. Ships DORMANT: default off, and activation also requires restarting the watcher
when_to_surface: Turn on for unattended/overnight runs so a coordinator that hits the account usage limit is auto-resumed at reset instead of stranding all orchestration until a human intervenes; leave off (default) to keep the coordinator human-managed

name: COORDINATOR_AUTONOMY
description: Coordinator spawn autonomy posture: human (default) | gated | full. human (today's byte-identical behavior) → the coordinator surfaces backlog items and waits for explicit user approval before spawning. gated → the coordinator may spawn items automatically when constraints are met (no unresolved conflicts, within budget, review capacity). full → coordinator makes all spawn decisions autonomously (for long-running unattended runs). The constraint checks — impact analysis, budget, concurrency gates — run either way; autonomy only changes whether a final human click is required. Unknown value → human. Applied on coordinator launch
when_to_surface: Set to gated or full for unattended/autonomous coordination; leave unset/human (default) for interactive operator control where each spawn requires explicit approval. Choose gated for an autonomous coordinator that still respects review bandwidth and conflict analysis, or full for a truly hands-off night/weekend run

name: DEAD_BUILDER_AUTORESPAWN
description: on | off (default off): opt-in AUTO-RESPAWN for a silently-dead pre-PR builder (agent-watch.sh). The watcher already DETECTS + surfaces a DEAD builder (worktree present, no live agent, no PR, past grace); with this on it also RESTARTS one — surgically, once. When a slug crosses into DEAD it respawns a FRESH agent in the EXISTING worktree pointed at the same $WORKTREES_DIR/<slug>.task.md (reuses the spawn pattern, NOT the full lane: no new worktree/branch, no app-preview pane). Bounded by two hard rails: it respawns ONLY when the worktree has NO commits ahead of base AND no staged/unstaged/untracked changes (never blows away work — a dead builder with work escalates instead), and AT MOST ONCE per slug via a slug-keyed ledger (a second death after the one respawn escalates, never loops). Ships DORMANT: default off and byte-inert until opted in
when_to_surface: Turn on for unattended/overnight runs so a builder whose agent silently dies before making any commits is auto-restarted in place instead of stranding an empty worktree until a human notices; leave off (default) to keep dead-builder handling detect-and-surface only

name: DEAD_GRACE_MIN
description: Minutes a builder's DEAD signature must persist before the watcher surfaces it as dead (agent-watch.sh) — long enough to cover a slow spawn-to-agent-register gap, short enough that a real death surfaces promptly. Non-numeric/unset → 2 minutes.
when_to_surface: Raise on a slow host where spawns register late; lower to surface deaths faster.

name: WEDGE_GRACE_MIN
description: Minutes a builder's WEDGE signature must persist before the watcher surfaces it (agent-watch.sh, HERD-278). The signature: the agent reads 'done', the open-PR roster positively has NO PR for its branch, and the tree holds nothing pushable (no commits ahead of base, or uncommitted changes). A builder inside `gh pr create` shows that exact signature for a few seconds, so the grace window is what makes the '⚠️ finished without PR · wake or inspect' row a verified-real red rather than a race. Non-numeric/unset → 10 minutes; a literal 0 is honored.
when_to_surface: Raise on a slow host (or a repo whose `gh pr create` round-trip is long) if a mid-PR-create builder ever flickers as wedged; lower to surface an abandoned builder faster.

name: WEDGE_AUTOWAKE
description: on | off (default off): opt-in AUTO-WAKE for a WEDGED builder (agent-watch.sh, HERD-278) — an agent that reads 'done' over a branch with no PR and nothing pushable. The watcher already DETECTS + surfaces the wedge as a red '⚠️ finished without PR · wake or inspect' attention row; with this on it also sends ONE nudge prompt to the builder's agent pane through the same driver send-text seam the auto-refix bounce uses (pane run + explicit Enter — HERD-186), verifies agent_status flips to "working", and journals wedge_wake / wedge_wake_result exactly like a refix wake. This is the remedy a coordinator applied by hand, successfully, three times on 2026-07-09. Bounded by two rails: AT MOST ONCE per wedge record (a nudge that does not take escalates back to the red row rather than typing into the pane every tick), and only at the WEDGED crossing — never during the grace window. Ships DORMANT: default off, and with it off the function is a hard no-op that touches no pane, writes no journal event, and leaves the console byte-identical
when_to_surface: Turn on for unattended/overnight runs so a builder that finishes without opening its PR is nudged back to life instead of sitting wedged until a human reads the console; leave off (default) to keep wedge handling detect-and-surface only

name: FINISH_STALL_MIN
description: Minutes a builder's agent may read 'done' or 'idle' continuously, over a worktree that carries genuine unshipped work (uncommitted tracked changes, or commits ahead of its OWN remote branch — never "ahead of base", which is what WEDGE_GRACE_MIN measures and deliberately exempts as "in flight") with NO open PR and no account-usage-limit park, before the watcher's finish-line watchdog (agent-watch.sh, HERD-392) acts. SHIP-DORMANT, more strictly than WEDGE_GRACE_MIN: unset/non-numeric/<=0 is a HARD no-op — zero extra git probes, zero python3 shellouts against the shared-pool clock (pysrc/herd/store.py finish_stall_* accessors), byte-identical console. Once set to a positive integer, on the FIRST crossing the watcher delivers ONE re-task nudge through the same driver send-text seam the auto-refix bounce uses, verifies agent_status flips back to "working", and journals finish_stall_wake / finish_stall_wake_result; a delivered nudge resets the clock from that OBSERVED wake transition. On a nudge that does not land, OR a SECOND full stall past this threshold after a delivered nudge, it records a needs-you row naming the slug + remedy and journals finish_stall_escalated (terminal — never fires a second nudge). Never fires while a PR exists for the branch or while the agent is working. The clock is a SHARED-POOL anchor, not seat memory, so multiple coordinator seats ticking the same worktree converge on one first-seen epoch. HERD-432: the SAME lever ALSO covers an idle builder over a PR that IS open but still a DRAFT (PR_FLOW=draft, PR_READY_WHEN=builder) — a livelock this leg previously could not see at all, since a draft PR reads as fully shipped by the worktree-scoped signature above. That detection uses its own namespaced anchor ("draftpr:<slug>") and needs no new config key; see DRAFT_AUTO_PROMOTE for its opt-in remedy.
when_to_surface: Set to ~30 (the suggested default) for unattended/overnight runs so a builder that finished real work but never opened its PR gets pushed across the line instead of sitting silently until a human reads the console; leave unset (default) for detect-nothing, byte-identical behavior

name: DRAFT_AUTO_PROMOTE
description: on | off (default off): opt-in AUTO-PROMOTION for the draft-PR leg of the finish-line watchdog (agent-watch.sh, HERD-432). The watcher already DETECTS + surfaces an idle builder's unpromoted draft PR as a red '⚠️ needs-you · draft PR stalled' row once FINISH_STALL_MIN is set (no new key needed for that); with this ALSO on, the FIRST time a draft PR crosses FINISH_STALL_MIN idle the watcher runs `gh pr ready <pr#>` itself — an action that needs no live agent pane, so it works even when the builder is limit-parked or dead, exactly the failure mode that let the grounding incidents (PR #549, #550, 2026-07-29/30) run 4-6+ hours unnoticed. Guarded by a PERMANENT once-per-PR-number store key (draft_promoted::<pr#>), separate from the per-anchor once-guard the ladder already uses for multi-seat safety: the engine auto-promotes a given PR NUMBER at most once, ever, so a human who deliberately re-drafts a PR it already promoted is never fought with a second auto-promotion — the ladder still detects and escalates on the re-draft, it just never re-acts. A failed attempt (gh error, permissions, the PR no longer existing) falls back to the SAME needs-you row FINISH_STALL_MIN alone renders; fail-soft, never blocks the gate or the reap. Ships DORMANT: default off, and with it off the leg is detection-and-surface only — no gh mutation, byte-identical PR state to before the feature.
when_to_surface: Turn on for unattended/overnight runs so a builder's finished-but-unpromoted draft PR gets pushed into the gate automatically instead of sitting invisible until a human reads the console; leave off (default) to keep the draft-PR leg detect-and-surface only, mirroring WEDGE_AUTOWAKE's own posture

name: STALL_QUIET_MIN
description: Minutes a working builder's worktree may stay quiet before the watcher warns of a stall (agent-watch.sh). Non-numeric/unset → 5 minutes.
when_to_surface: Raise for lanes with long quiet compute phases; lower to catch stalls sooner.

name: STALE_DUP_DETECT
description: Pre-merge STALE-DUPLICATE gate (HERD-188): on (default) | off. on → the watcher's action pass runs scripts/herd/stale-dup-gate.sh FIRST for each candidate — before the healthcheck and the review pre-dispatch (HERD-227: the gate is deterministic and its hold supersedes the sha, so a later evaluation burned a full heavy suite + an Opus review per stale cycle) — and HOLDS (never auto-merges, surfaces a loud 🛑 needs-you row + one PR comment + notification, journals stale_dup_hold) any PR that is a PROVABLE stale duplicate — either (1) DUPLICATE: its tracked 'Refs: <ID>' item is already Done via ANOTHER merged PR carrying the same ref (the #236-vs-shipped-#185 incident that force-merged onto newer main → revert #280), or (2) STALE BASE: the files it touches were materially changed on the base branch (DEFAULT_BRANCH) by a merge this branch predates, so a clean-but-behind merge would silently clobber that newer work (deterministic git set-intersection, only when the branch is behind base). PROVABLE-ONLY + FAIL-SOFT: no item ref, an offline gh, a missing base ref, or any probe failure yields NO hold, so default-on cannot false-hold a legitimate PR. off → byte-inert (no probe, no hold, no rows). Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Leave on (default) so the watcher refuses to auto-merge work that already shipped or sits on a base a merge would silently revert; set to off to disable the gate entirely (e.g. a repo whose PRs never carry tracker refs and whose branch protection already requires up-to-date branches)

name: STALE_BASE_AUTOFIX
description: Auto-heal STALE-BASE holds from the pre-merge stale-duplicate gate (HERD-199): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → when the gate holds a PR for STALE-BASE (touched files moved on DEFAULT_BRANCH after the branch's merge-base), the watcher auto-bounces the live builder with a `git merge $DEFAULT_BRANCH` re-task via the EXISTING refix rails (sha-keyed once-guard kind=stale, the STALE rail's own REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget — refunded when the base is freshened, bounded by the per-PR 3x total ceiling, honest console row `rebasing · awaiting push`); if there is no live builder (foreign/reaped/dead/missing pane) it dispatches the conflict resolver instead. Only bounce-exhaustion escalates to needs-you. The DUPLICATE flavor (re-implements shipped work) stays a human judgment call. off (default) → byte-identical to the pre-HERD-199 hold path (🛑 needs-you, no bounce, no ledger write). Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) in high-churn repos where base-stale holds fire repeatedly for purely mechanical merge-up work; leave off (default) so a stale-base hold still waits for a human. Pair with STALE_DUP_DETECT=on (the gate that produces the hold).

name: CI_AUTOREPAIR
description: CI auto-repair for INHERITED reds (HERD-250): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → when a PR is MERGEABLE but UNSTABLE with a FAILING required CI check, herd/gates already PASSED for the head sha, AND the branch is BEHIND DEFAULT_BRANCH, the watcher dispatches a base-refresh (merge $DEFAULT_BRANCH into the branch — the SAME mechanical heal as STALE_BASE_AUTOFIX, but keyed on CI-red+behind-base rather than touched-file overlap, which missed PR #353 whose diff did not touch the files main already fixed). Sha-keyed once-guard kind=ci on the shared refix rails, the CI rail's own REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget, honest console row `ci-repair · awaiting push`; if no live builder remains it dispatches the conflict resolver. Only bounce-exhaustion escalates to needs-you. NEVER silently merges a red PR — a REAL new-code CI failure (failing CI on an up-to-date branch, or without a herd/gates blessing) stays the existing needs-you · CI failed row. Journals `ci_repair` events. off (default) → byte-identical to the pre-HERD-250 UNSTABLE-fail path (needs-you, no bounce, no ledger). Consumed by agent-watch.sh via scripts/herd/ci-repair.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) when GitHub Actions required checks regularly fail on behind-main PRs because main already shipped the hermetic/suite fix (the inherited-red case); leave off (default) so every CI failure stays a human-action stop. Pair with GATE_STATUS=on so the gates blessing is visible.

name: MAINTENANCE_GARDENER
description: The maintenance gardener (HERD-673, tuned HERD-730): periodic doc-drift sweep — on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on → `gardener.sh run` files ONE rollup tracker item per run, grouping every surface file (bin/herd, scripts/herd/*.sh, templates/capabilities.tsv, templates/conformance.tsv) that changed in a merge without README.md/docs/**/templates/*.tmpl (or templates/capabilities.tsv itself) changing in the SAME merge, by subsystem — gated by a per-signature filing cooldown so a standing drift is not re-included every run, and by a per-run filing cap (HERD_GARDENER_MAX_FINDINGS) that truncates loudly rather than silently and holds the cursor back for an honest rescan; zero findings still advances the cursor and journals one `gardener_run findings=0` event. FILES, NEVER EDITS — it never writes a doc file itself. off (default) → byte-identical: `gardener.sh run` prints one disabled notice and returns 0, touching no journal, no state dir, no scribe call. Consumed by scripts/herd/gardener.sh, scheduled via .herd/triggers.tsv.
when_to_surface: Set to on to let the weekly maintenance-gardener trigger (and the docs-gardener specialist it spawns) actually file doc-drift findings; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: CI_FAST_BOUNCE
description: Fast-bounce on the PR's OWN CI failure conclusion, ahead of the local suite (HERD-495): on | off (default off, ship-dormant; yolo posture adopts on). on → when a PR's CI concludes FAILURE naming a real test (the SAME honest-identity `gh run view --log-failed` extraction HERD-476/#600 built for the main-health CI leg, reused verbatim) and `_handle_ci_repair` did NOT already heal it as an inherited red (off, or genuinely not behind/gates-not-green), the watcher bounces the builder IMMEDIATELY with that evidence marked PROVISIONAL — the local healthcheck suite is still the AUTHORITATIVE verdict and may disagree. Deliberately SHARES the HEALTH rail rather than opening a new one: kind=health, the SAME sha-keyed once-guard and REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS budget a local CODE ERROR bounce (HEALTHCHECK_AUTOFIX) also spends, so the two never double-bounce the same sha and a later local CLEAN/FLAKY retracts this red via the EXISTING kind=health reset — zero new state. Same limit-parked / dead-missing / self-restart / suite-write-interlock preflights as every other refix rail; only bounce-exhaustion escalates to needs-you. Grounded cost this removes: PR #610 sat red ~50 minutes (full local suite + full-suite retry) for a failure CI had already named in ~4 minutes. off (default) → byte-identical to the pre-HERD-495 needs-you path: no extra gh calls, no bounce, no ledger write. Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) when the local healthcheck suite is slow relative to CI and a red PR should get an early, provisional heads-up instead of waiting the full suite out; leave off (default) so every CI failure stays a passive needs-you row until the local suite itself verdicts. Pair with HEALTHCHECK_AUTOFIX=true (the rail this shares) so the local-suite half of the same red also auto-bounces.

name: RESOLVE_AUTOFIX
description: Auto-dispatch the conflict resolver on a genuine git CONFLICTING PR (HERD-541): on | off (default off, ship-dormant; yolo posture adopts on). on → when the classifier's CONF_* dispatch queue holds a conflicting PR (_classify_conflict already decided a resolver is due — a first conflict, a new commit that reshaped it, or a dead resolver, each already past its own sha-keyed once-guard and REFIX_MAX_ROUNDS cap) AND the PR's own builder agent is NOT working (done/idle/absent — a live builder is NEVER yanked out from under its own WIP), the resolve pass (_dispatch_conflict_autofix) dispatches herd-resolve.sh for that slug through the SAME spawn_resolver every other healer rail uses: RESOLVE_CLAIM (if armed) is consulted exactly as for every other caller, an ESCALATE stays the existing needs-you + PR comment (terminal for that sha), and a live builder still working the conflict itself is left alone — the row stays the honest needs-you. Journals `resolve_autodispatch`; the console row while the resolver runs reads `resolving · auto (round N/M)`. off (default) → byte-identical to before: CONF_* is computed and dropped every tick, and a true git conflict is always the pre-HERD-541 needs-you row. Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) in repos where genuine merge conflicts are common and mostly mechanical (adjacent edits, moved helpers) so an idle builder's conflicting PR heals itself instead of waiting for a human; leave off (default) so a real conflict always surfaces needs-you. Pairs with RESOLVE_CLAIM=on in team mode so two seats never dispatch onto the same commit.

name: ANOMALY_BASELINES
description: Self-observation: PER-PHASE DURATION BASELINES + anomaly self-filing (HERD-496): on | off (default off, ship-dormant; yolo posture adopts on). on → the watcher records every completed phase's wall-clock duration — healthcheck start→verdict, review dispatch→verdict, the post-merge main-health suite, a refix bounce→wake, and its own tick cadence — into a rolling (last 40 samples) per-phase median/p95 baseline persisted in the shared pool (pysrc/herd/store.py phase_duration_observe, mirroring refix_rounds' dual flat/sqlite backend shape). Once a phase has LEARNED enough samples (≥5), an instance that runs past its filing threshold — max(1.5x its own p95, p95 + 30s), HERD-645's absolute floor on top of the pct multiplier so a phase whose p95 sits within jitter of its nominal period does not alarm on jitter — journals a `phase_anomaly` event, paints a calm advisory 'phase anomalies' console row ('health-check 28m — p95 19m', ages out after 2h like builder notes), and FILES ONCE via the SAME shared-pool dedup marker MAIN_HEALTH_AUTOFIX's filing leg uses (HERD-371's `_main_health_fix_mark`/`_main_health_scribe`), keyed by an HONEST identity — phase + this measurement + the baseline it beat — so a re-observed identical reading dedups (result=dedup journaled) while a worse or different reading of the same phase files fresh. Below threshold, or before the baseline has learned enough samples, is SILENT: no journal, no row, no filing. HERD-618: while this box looks contended right now (`_anomaly_load_high`, reusing ENV_SUSPECT_TIMEOUT's own loadavg1m/HEALTH_LOAD_THRESHOLD probe, independent of whether that lever is itself on), the FILING bar widens to 2x the (HERD-645-floored) normal threshold — a reading past the normal threshold but short of the widened one still journals `phase_anomaly` and paints its row (tagged load_qualified in the ledger and on the console), but withholds the tracker filing (`phase_anomaly_filed result=load_qualified`); a quiet box, or an exceedance beyond the widened margin even under load, files exactly as before. GROUNDED: a 5h dead watcher (2026-08-02) was a tick-silence anomaly a learned cadence baseline would have caught within minutes; a learned ~19m suite-baseline never false-files a routinely-slow-but-typical 28m run the way a hardcoded threshold would; two tick-cadence items false-filed 2026-08-10 under a ~11 15m-loadavg on 14 cores (HERD-618) for exceedances only marginal against a baseline learned on a quieter box. off (default) → byte-inert: no store write, no journal line, no row, no filing, no python3 shellout. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) in a repo that wants the watcher to notice ITS OWN slow/stuck phases (a hung tick, a suite that quietly regressed) without a human eyeballing durations — herdkit enables it for itself via the yolo posture. Leave off (default) elsewhere: zero behavior change, zero extra shellouts. Pair with MAIN_HEALTH_AUTOFIX (the seam this reuses) so the filed anomaly item lands the same way a MAIN RED fix does.

name: ANOMALY_FILE_COOLDOWN_SECS
description: Seconds a phase must wait after ACTUALLY FILING an anomaly item before that SAME phase may file another (HERD-512) — default 1800 (30 min); 0 = off, i.e. the pre-HERD-512 behavior where every above-threshold reading may file. Only consulted while ANOMALY_BASELINES is on, so off stays byte-inert (no stamp file is ever written). ANOMALY_BASELINES' honest-identity dedup only collapses an IDENTICAL re-reading (same phase+seconds+p95), so a phase that stays degraded files a FRESH tracker item every tick it reads differently — GROUNDED 2026-08-04: one overnight suspend window produced 4 separate items telling the same tick-cadence story. Inside the window the anomaly is STILL journaled (`phase_anomaly`) and STILL painted on the 'phase anomalies' console ledger — the operator loses no visibility — only the tracker filing is withheld, journaled `phase_anomaly_filed result=cooldown`. The last-filing epoch is stamped per phase key in the shared pool dir ($TREES/.agent-watch-phase-anomaly-filed-<phase>) and written ONLY on a real enqueue, never on a dedup or a store-unavailable skip. A non-numeric value reads as the DEFAULT (not 0): a typo must not silently restore the filing storm this key exists to stop. Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Lower it (or set 0) in a repo that WANTS every distinct anomaly reading on the tracker; raise it when a genuinely-degraded phase is filing repeat items faster than anyone can triage. Leave at the 1800 default otherwise — it is the anti-spam companion to ANOMALY_BASELINES, not an independent feature.

name: MERGE_FAIRNESS
description: Merge fairness — READY-PR PRIORITY in the watcher's action pass (HERD-231): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> before the pass dispatches any new gate work, candidates whose gates are ALREADY green for their current head sha (a cached CLEAN/FLAKY healthcheck result AND a review PASS, or a BLOCK a human overrode for that same sha) are stably partitioned to the FRONT of the candidate order, so a merge-eligible PR merges on this tick instead of waiting behind health/review dispatches for its siblings -- dispatches whose eventual merge is precisely what re-stales it (PR #328 lost four conflict/stale laps on 2026-07-09, PR #347 three, each re-staled by a merge landing faster than a review completes). ORDERING ONLY, and it never merges anything that has not fully passed: a promoted candidate still runs the pre-merge re-verify, the UNCONDITIONAL stale-base re-check against the current base tip, the cross-seat BLOCK-precedence guard and the merge-policy decision, exactly as a demoted one does. Deterministic: stable within both partitions and computed from the ledgers alone (no gh, no git), so two seats reading the same ledgers derive the same order; a tick with nothing to promote is byte-quiet. Journals merge_fairness_priority only when the order actually changes. off (default) -> the candidate arrays are never touched and every event, dispatch and merge is byte-identical to before the feature. INDEPENDENT of the always-on re-stale counter (the `starving · N re-stale laps` console row plus the pr_restale / pr_starvation journal events), which is display-only and never gated by this knob. Consumed by agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) in a high-churn repo where a gates-green PR repeatedly loses its sha to a sibling merge before it can land -- the `starving · N re-stale laps` row (always on) is the signal that it is time; leave off (default) for the byte-identical discovery-order pass. Cross-seat fairness needs a shared ledger substrate (the seat-local ledgers this reorder reads are per-$TREES), so today it orders THIS seat's candidates only.

name: MERGE_FAIRNESS_STARVE_THRESHOLD
description: Consecutive re-stale laps (agent-watch.sh's `starving · N re-stale laps` counter) before a candidate is considered starving for the always-on display row and, when MERGE_FAIRNESS=on, before it earns front-of-order priority (default: 3, matching agent-watch.sh's own _RESTALE_STARVE_THRESHOLD constant). Consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py; a non-numeric value falls back to the default
when_to_surface: Lower to flag/prioritize starvation sooner in a high-churn repo; raise to tolerate more re-stale laps before treating a candidate as starving

name: MERGE_RESULT_GATE
description: Merge-result gate (HERD-296, docs/engine-contract.md §6.4): on | off (default off, ship-dormant), a STRICT validated key (an unrecognized value reads off, never accidentally on). Today the pre-merge healthcheck runs the branch worktree AS-IS -- two PRs can each test green on their own stale base, merge textually clean, and interact only through behavior (one changes a function's contract, the other consumes the old contract in a file it never touched) -- every gate passes and the default branch breaks (docs/spikes/merge-result-gate.md). on -> before gating, materialize a THROWAWAY detached worktree at the PR's exact head sha merged with the CURRENT default-branch tip, and run the healthcheck suite against THAT tree instead of the branch as-is -- ONE suite run, never a doubled gate latency. A real merge conflict is resolver-owned and fails soft into the SAME honest hold the stale-dup gate uses (never a red, never a bounce). The tested (head, base) pair is cached so a base move RE-ARMS the gate, and journals a `merge_result_gate` event carrying the tested base sha; supersession (a new head sha) cancels an in-flight merge-result worker exactly like the classic health/review rails. off (default) -> byte-identical: the classic per-branch healthcheck dispatch is untouched and no `.merge-result-*` file is ever written. FOLDED INTO THE PYTHON PORT ONLY (EPIC HERD-300 P3) -- never built into the retired bash action pass; consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py, NOT agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) once a project has repeat semantic-conflict incidents (two textually-disjoint PRs individually green, main red after both merge) -- the merge-result gate closes that window pre-merge instead of relying on the main-health monitor to catch it after landing; leave off (default) for the byte-identical branch-as-is healthcheck.

name: MERGE_QUEUE
description: Ordered integration queue / merge train (HERD-273, docs/engine-contract.md §6.3): on | off (default off, ship-dormant), a STRICT validated key (an unrecognized value reads off, never accidentally on). Today candidates merge independently, each verified only against its own base -- nothing stops two blessed siblings landing in the same window in whichever order they happened to turn green, or a later one lapping an earlier one still finishing its final gate. on -> a deterministic queue (ascending PR NUMBER -- the one stable, collision-free order every seat derives with no shared ledger) forms over every open, non-stale candidate whose merge policy would land it once green; ONLY the queue FRONT may apply a merge THIS window -- every OTHER candidate that reaches gates-green now HOLDS instead (`queue_wait`), even one whose own gates are green, so two siblings never land out of order, and a front stuck red/CONFLICT never lets a later candidate merge past it. Implies the SAME per-slot verification MERGE_RESULT_GATE=on provides, UNCONDITIONALLY -- not a second, independently-toggleable requirement a project could leave mismatched. Because a REAL merge (not a synthetic chain) advances the base each time the front lands, the virtual tip needs no speculative chaining: by the time a later position becomes front, every already-ordered candidate ahead of it has ALREADY really merged, so the plain current base tip already IS the virtual tip. off (default) -> byte-identical: candidate order, dispatches, events, argv and merge behavior are untouched, no `queue_wait`/`merge_queue_*` event is ever journaled. FOLDED INTO THE PYTHON PORT ONLY (EPIC HERD-300 P3) -- never built into the retired bash action pass; consumed by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py, NOT agent-watch.sh.
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) once a project runs enough concurrent seats that two individually-green PRs landing in the same window (or out of PR-number order) has caused a real incident -- the queue trades throughput (a stuck front blocks everyone behind it until a human/resolver clears it) for a structural lapping guarantee; leave off (default) for today's independent per-candidate merges.

name: RESOLVER_PANE
description: The conflict RESOLVER as a RETIRING PANE (HERD-280): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> herd-resolve.sh places the resolver agent as a bottom SPLIT PANE inside the builder's existing tab (the tab labelled exactly <slug>) instead of opening a standalone resolve·<slug> tab, falling back to that standalone tab in the control-room workspace when no builder tab exists, when herdr is unavailable, or when the split start fails; the lane then records the pane it created in a sha-scoped dispatch registry ($WORKTREES_DIR/.resolve-registry-<pr>-<sha>, one row: pane tab placement pr sha). Each tick the watcher RECONCILES that registry against the OBSERVED verdict file (.resolve-result-<pr>-<sha>) rather than any dispatch-seat event, so any seat retires the pane once the verdict lands: a `RESOLVE: DONE` closes the pane immediately through the HERD-134 guarded close (a stale/recycled id naming the builder is REFUSED, journaling pane_close_refused) and journals `resolver_pane_retired reason=result-consumed`, dropping the registry row and, in standalone-tab placement, the now-empty tab plus its sweep-allowlist row; a `RESOLVE: ESCALATE` KEEPS the pane open for the human its needs-you row addresses, and no later tick may retire it. The WORKTREE lifecycle is unchanged -- the retirement invariant still reaps the tree at merge. off (default) -> byte-identical to the pre-HERD-280 lane: a standalone tab, no registry seam handed to herd-resolve.sh, no registry row, no reconcile, no retire. An unrecognized value reads off (a typo can never arm a pane-closing path). Consumed by agent-watch.sh + herd-resolve.sh
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) so a finished conflict resolver stops squatting a tab/pane the way reviewer panes used to before HERD-113 -- the resolve session disappears the moment its DONE verdict is consumed, while an ESCALATE stays on screen as the evidence a human needs; leave off (default) for the standalone resolve·<slug> tab that only the stale-tab reaper closes

name: HEALTH_PANE
description: The in-flight HEALTHCHECK as a DISPOSABLE WATCH PANE (HERD-313 leg a; placement fixed by HERD-568): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> each render tick the watcher RECONCILES the OBSERVED in-flight suites (the sha-scoped `.health-inflight-<pr>-<sha>` markers, written by whichever engine dispatched the suite) against the panes that exist, BOTH ways rather than off any dispatch event (HERD-554). A live suite with no pane gets a stamped `health·<slug>` pane, PLACED (HERD-568) as a SPLIT off the builder's own tab's ROOT pane (below/beside the task-spec-viewer pane, never the agent's own pane) when that tab is still found (_health_builder_tab: the $TREES/.herd-tabs registry row, sanitized/truncated-label tolerant, else `herdr agent list`'s tab_id) -- a fresh standalone tab is now only the FALLBACK when no builder tab is found, journaled `infra_event component=health_pane reason=no-builder-tab`. The pane execs scripts/herd/health-pane-view.sh directly (never types into the pane's own still-greeting shell) over the sha-scoped health log ($TREES/.health-log-<pr>-<sha>) AND its inflight marker -- a sidecar-aware tail (the live `.progress` companion while the suite runs, the log's own one-shot final verdict once it lands) with NO model and NO gate authority, a VIEW only -- recorded in a sha-scoped registry ($TREES/.health-pane-registry-<pr>-<sha>, one row: pane tab placement health·<slug>); and ANY seat retires the pane the instant the suite ends (marker gone / worker dead): the pane is closed through the HERD-134 guarded close (a stale/recycled id naming a neighbour is REFUSED, journaling pane_close_refused) and journals `health_pane_retired`, dropping the registry row and -- ONLY in `tab` (fallback) placement, never `split`, which would take the builder's shared tab down with it -- closing the now-empty tab too. Additive to, and independent of, the always-on live progress row (leg b) which needs no lever. off (default) -> byte-identical: no pane, no registry file, no reconcile side effect. An unrecognized value reads off (a typo can never arm a pane-closing path). Consumed by agent-watch.sh
when_to_surface: Enable (set on) to WATCH the live suite output in its own disposable pane while a healthcheck runs -- the pane appears alongside the builder's own tab when it is still open (else a standalone fallback tab) when the suite starts and disappears the moment it ends; leave off (default) for a byte-identical console where the leg-(b) progress row is the only in-flight signal. Watcher-affecting, takes effect on the next watcher restart; opt-in, never self-activates and never changes a gate or a merge decision

name: AGENTS_PANE
description: The specialist AGENT ROSTER as a compact READ-ONLY control-room pane (HERD-668, epic HERD-666, child 2 of the agent-roster CLI HERD-667/PR #784): on | off (default off, ship-dormant). on -> coordinator.sh (fresh control room) and herd reload / herd pane agents (in-place) split the WATCH pane RIGHT (ratio 0.72 -- the watcher keeps ~72% of the width, this pane the remainder), launch scripts/herd/agents-pane-view.sh in the new pane, label it agents·<WORKSPACE_NAME> (herd_driver_pane_rename, same convention as watch·/backlog·), and register it as a 4th ROLE ROW (agents <pane> <tab> <ws>) in $WORKTREES_DIR/.herd-panes via the shared layout_write_registry writer -- an older registry with no such row still loads fine. The pane RENDERS on a slow tick, RECONCILED from OBSERVED state each pass (never a live probe on the render path): every scripts/herd/agents.sh roster definition with its CACHED resolve verdict (herd_roster_cache_get), and which specialist agent (if any) each in-flight builder was spawned under, read from the per-worktree $WORKTREES_DIR/.herd-agent-<slug> marker herd-feature.sh/herd-quick.sh write only when HERD_AGENT was set (blank marker -> rendered "general", mirroring the HERD_ITEM_REF/.herd-ref-<slug> marker convention) -- an empty or uninstalled roster renders one hint line, never blank. STRICTLY read-only: never spawns, mutates, gates, or merges, and never blocks a merge (no gate consumes it). off (default) -> byte-identical: no split, no registry row, no renderer, no marker file is ever consulted. An unrecognized value reads off. Consumed by coordinator.sh, bin/herd (cmd_reload, herd pane agents), scripts/herd/agents-pane-view.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on for a live, at-a-glance view of the specialist agent roster (resolve state) and which in-flight builders were spawned under a specialist agent, without leaving the control room; leave off (default) for a byte-identical layout with no extra pane. Never affects gating or merging.

name: SWEEP_AUTO
description: Control-room SWEEP triggers (HERD-191): off | advise (default) | auto. The watcher runs a CHEAP debris scan (registry tabs whose slug has no worktree, dead-pid inflight markers, orphaned ppid=1 bats/healthcheck trees) on its orphan-sweep cadence (~60 s) — filesystem + kill -0 + one `ps -e`, no network. advise (default) → render one '🧹 sweep recommended: N stale tabs · M dead markers' console row and journal `sweep_advice` ONCE per distinct condition-set (an unchanged mess is silent; a changed one speaks again). auto → additionally run the SAFE legs itself: dead markers, orphan processes, PROVABLY-disposable worktrees, and registry-matched tabs (in that order — reaping frees a slug before the tab leg judges it stale). JUDGMENT legs — a worktree carrying real dirt or a closed-PR branch with unpushed unique commits — are FLAGGED WITH EVIDENCE and never auto-deleted in ANY mode, so `auto` cannot destroy unrecovered work; it also never restarts the watcher (leg 5 is CLI-only). An unrecognized value degrades to advise, never to auto. off → byte-inert: no scan, no row, no journal. Consumed by agent-watch.sh via sweep.sh
when_to_surface: Leave at advise (default) for a quiet nudge when debris accumulates; set auto in a long-running control room that should self-clean the provably-safe debris between sessions; set off for a byte-identical console. Watcher-affecting (takes effect on the next watcher restart). Run `herd sweep` for the full on-demand cleanup including the judgment findings and the watcher restart

name: scripts/herd/layout-reconcile.sh
description: The shared EYES-ON-LAYOUT helper. Classifies every pane in a tab by its live foreground process (herdr pane list + process-info → backlog|watch|agent|bare|busy|gone), then layout_snapshot scans a tab, layout_reconcile adopts live role panes / flags duplicate viewers / names missing roles (registry pane-ids trusted only when still observed — neutralising a stale or poisoned .herd-panes), layout_write_registry rewrites the registry from OBSERVED state, and layout_fold_stray_tabs closes standalone watch-/backlog- tabs. Sourced by bin/herd (cmd_reload + herd pane) and coordinator.sh so every pane-mutating path observes reality before it mutates
when_to_surface: When changing how the control room resolves/creates/adopts panes, debugging a duplicate viewer or a reload that built standalone tabs, or explaining why a mutating path observes the live layout before trusting the registry

name: TASK_PANE_VIEW
description: Builder-tab task-spec viewer: on (default) | off. When on, the builder lanes (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh) render the builder's live task spec ($WORKTREES_DIR/<slug>.task.md) in the tab's OTHERWISE-IDLE root pane via task-spec-view.sh (glow + the bundled tokyonight style, repaint-on-mtime, a quiet dim 'task spec removed' line when the file is reaped — never red), so a human sees WHAT the agent was told to build instead of a bare shell. Strictly ADDITIVE UX: the pane is unused today, so off (default on) restores the bare shell exactly. Launched ONLY when the root pane is not hosting the app preview or any live process, and NEVER under the headless driver (no panes → clean no-op). Applied on the next builder spawn.
when_to_surface: Set to off to keep builder tabs' root pane a bare shell; leave on (default) to surface each builder's task spec live in its otherwise-unused root pane

name: DOCTOR_STARTUP_HINT
description: Proactive soft-dependency surfacing on control-room startup (herd reload / coordinator launch): off (default) | on. Default off prints NOTHING extra, so every startup path is byte-identical unless opted in. When on, startup emits one DIM line per MISSING soft dep (glow -> raw backlog pane, shellcheck -> no lint, bats -> direct test run), each naming the single feature it degrades, then a dim pointer to `herd doctor` for the install command. Never red, never blocks (soft deps only degrade; the no-false-red rule). Applied on the next herd reload / coordinator launch
when_to_surface: Set to on to be reminded at control-room startup which optional tools are missing and what each degrades, instead of discovering it when the degradation bites; leave off (default) for a byte-identical startup

name: AGENT_UPDATE
description: Opt-in safe self-update of the AGENT RUNTIME (HERD-149): off (default) | on. Default off runs NOTHING — no installer probe, no update exec, no xattr — so the tree is byte-identical and operators keep updating claude (or, via the driver seam, codex/grok) by hand or a personal OS job, outside the engine. When on, `herd agent-update` (scripts/herd/agent-update.sh) detects the installer (brew/npm/native) of the runtime HERD_DRIVER points at, runs the update, and — the whole point — de-quarantines the resolved binary on macOS (strips com.apple.quarantine, the issue #137 footgun where a `brew upgrade --cask` leaves the new binary quarantined so every new exec hangs in _dyld_start). DRIVER-AWARE (each runtime-specific value comes from the active driver's DRIVER_AGENT_* bindings) and FAIL-SOFT (a missing runtime / failed installer warns, never hard-aborts). Any value other than on is treated as off
when_to_surface: Set to on to have the engine keep the agent runtime current (and auto-handle the macOS cask-quarantine footgun) instead of a hand-run upgrade; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior. Preview with `herd agent-update --dry-run`

name: ENGINE_MIN
description: The ENGINE VERSION HANDSHAKE floor (HERD-179): the minimum herdkit ENGINE LEVEL this project requires, committed in .herd/config. `herd upgrade` STAMPS it to the level of the engine that ran the upgrade and only ever RAISES it (monotonic), so an operator on an older checkout cannot silently un-pin the project. An engine below the floor is STALE and every WRITE path refuses it with one remedy — `run herd update`: lane spawn preflight (herd-preflight.sh), herd-claim, scribe-step apply (commit/add-item/update-state/amend), and `herd backend switch`. READ paths only warn (`herd status`, the advisory `herd doctor` row). HERD_ENGINE_SKIP_HANDSHAKE=1 is the deliberate escape hatch: it downgrades any refusal to a warning and JOURNALS the bypass (engine_handshake_bypass), so a forced write is always recoverable from `herd log`. Default 0 / absent ⇒ no floor ⇒ the handshake is inert and behavior is byte-identical to before it existed. The engine's own level constant (_HERD_ENGINE_LEVEL) lives in scripts/herd/engine-version.sh
when_to_surface: When a second operator (or a second machine) can run an OLDER engine checkout against this project's committed config — the handshake stops that stale engine from claiming an item, spawning a lane, draining a scribe request, or switching the backend. You never set it by hand; `herd upgrade` stamps it

name: ENGINE_AUTOUPDATE
description: What the engine DOES about a stale local checkout (HERD-179): off (default) | check | auto. off runs nothing beyond the always-advisory `herd doctor` engine row. check paints one quiet 'engine outdated' note on the watcher console (byte-identical console otherwise) and calls it out in the doctor; `herd update` stays a manual act. auto additionally has the watcher dispatch `herd update` in a QUIESCENT window every ~5 min — reusing that command's OWN refusal (it aborts under HERD_NONINTERACTIVE while builders are mid-flight, since their lanes reference engine scripts live, or over a dirty/diverged engine checkout) and rate-limited by a cooldown (HERD_ENGINE_COOLDOWN_SECS, default 900) so a persistent refusal never hammers the remote. The update is dispatched DETACHED because `herd update` ends in a reload that restarts the watcher. Any value other than check/auto is off
when_to_surface: Set to check when you want the console + doctor to tell you the engine has fallen behind this project's ENGINE_MIN; set to auto when you want the watcher to pull the engine forward for you between builds. Leave off (default) to keep `herd update` entirely manual

name: ENGINE_SEAT_RECONCILE
description: CROSS-SEAT DUAL-ENGINE SAFETY (HERD-308, engine-port P3.5): off (default) | on. The pool-level complement to the ENGINE_MIN handshake — it needs no committed floor. With it on the watcher STAMPS the engine level it writes at into a shared pool registry ($WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/engine-seats.tsv via herd_engine_seat_stamp) and RECONCILES it every tick: two DISTINCT engine levels writing one pool (the bash/Python dual-engine window, or two operators on different checkouts) never coexist silently — the STALE seat HALTS loudly (a red console row, a journaled engine_seat_mismatch) and its do_merge / post_gate_status writes are HELD, so there are ZERO cross-mismatch writes; the leading seat proceeds but says so. off is a HARD no-op (no stamp, no registry, byte-identical console + merge path); single-seat is always coherent so even ON it is inert for a solo operator. Mechanism in scripts/herd/engine-seat.sh
when_to_surface: Turn on when a project may be worked by two engine checkouts against one worktree pool at once — most importantly the P3–P5 engine-port window where a bash and a Python watcher run side by side. Leave off (default) for a single-engine project; it is inert either way for a solo operator

name: ENGINE_IMPL
description: The engine-core implementation the watcher runs (EPIC HERD-300, the Python port). After the P5 CUTOVER (HERD-306) there is exactly ONE engine core: python. The bash engine-core ACTION PASS (agent-watch.sh's _tick_act) was DELETED, so the supervisor hands EVERY tick to the Python live engine (pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py) via herd_engine_live_tick and, on a fault, runs a WATCHDOG (_engine_tick_watchdog: in-tick backoff retry, then past a fault streak a loud 'engine down · manual intervention' console banner + engine_down journal + one notification) — never a bash fallback and never a half-run. The historical values bash and shadow are RETIRED: herd_engine_impl (scripts/herd/engine-version.sh) WARNs loudly once and resolves them to python (a stale config value can never divert or disable the sole engine core), and `herd doctor --posture` flags a retired value. The parity SHADOW oracle (pysrc/herd/shadow_runtime.py) still exists, invoked out-of-band by scripts/herd/sim/parity-run.sh; only the live per-tick shadow dispatch is gone. Default python; leave unset.
when_to_surface: Leave unset — python is the sole engine core. If an old config still sets ENGINE_IMPL=bash or shadow, delete it: the value is a retired no-op that only produces a startup warning.

name: ENGINE_PAUSE
description: The OPERATOR EMERGENCY-OFF switch (HERD-347): on | off (default off). The first-class replacement for the pre-P5b `ENGINE_IMPL=bash` no-op pause that config validation now refuses — the only way to hold a misbehaving action pass WITHOUT killing the whole watcher (and its render/sweeps/alarms). With it on the watcher's supervisor (_engine_tick_watchdog in agent-watch.sh) SKIPS the Python live tick every cycle — zero gate/merge/refix dispatch — and does NOT count the skipped tick as a fault (the engine-down watchdog: fault streak, banner, notification are untouched, so a deliberate pause never trips the 'engine down' alarm). It paints a loud '⏸ engine paused by operator' console banner, pinned above even the engine-down row. Render, reconcile, sweeps and every alarm KEEP running — only the action engine is held. Read FRESH from the config file each tick (NOT from the sourced env value — which is why it carries no requires=watcher restart): any seat's `herd config set ENGINE_PAUSE on|off` takes effect on the shared watcher's very next tick with NO restart and no seat-local cache. Fail-soft (garbage → off, engine runs). off is a HARD no-op: byte-identical console + engine behavior to before this key existed. Resume with one `herd config set ENGINE_PAUSE off`.
when_to_surface: Turn ON to instantly pause the action engine (gate dispatch / auto-merge / refix / resolver respawn) during an incident — a misbehaving pass, a bad merge run — while keeping the console, reconcile and sweeps live and the watcher process up; effective on the next tick with no restart. Resume with `herd config set ENGINE_PAUSE off`. Leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior

name: STORE_BACKEND
description: The MUTABLE-STATE STORE backend the Python engine core reads (HERD-305, EPIC HERD-300, engine-port P4): auto (default) | flat | sqlite. P4 moves the ~45 flat state files that hold the engine's read-modify-write mutable state — approvals, the review ledger, health results, claims, refix rounds, once-guards, the seat registry — into ONE SQLite (WAL) database behind accessor functions (pysrc/herd/store.py) that mirror the flat-file semantics 1:1, every RMW TRANSACTIONAL and sha-keyed. The append-only journal (.herd/journal.jsonl) is NEVER in the db — forensic truth stays an append-only JSONL stream. auto => FLAT (the existing flat files agent-watch.sh owns) UNTIL the one-shot migration runner (`python3 -m herd.store --migrate`, operator-triggered, NOT run by any test or the watcher) has migrated the pool and written a .herd/store-backend marker; only then does auto engage sqlite. The runner crosses the P3.5 quiesce gate (herd_engine_migration_guard, engine-seat.sh) BEFORE any write — refusing loudly unless every other seat is quiesced or a dual-write window is declared, so a migration never races a live writer — and snapshots every state file's raw bytes so `--rollback` reconstructs them BYTE-IDENTICALLY (a lossless files->db->files round-trip). flat forces flat; sqlite forces sqlite (explicit opt-in / tests). With nothing migrated auto == flat, so behavior is BYTE-IDENTICAL to before this key. FAIL-SOFT: an unreadable marker / missing db degrades to flat (the store never engages a backend it cannot open). Consumed by pysrc/herd/store.py (resolve_backend), live_runtime.GateState + shadow_runtime
when_to_surface: Leave auto (default) in normal operation — the store is dormant and byte-identical to today until an operator deliberately runs the guarded migration; set flat to pin the flat substrate, or sqlite only post-migration to force the db backend

name: scripts/herd/task-spec-view.sh
description: The builder-tab task-spec viewer. Renders a builder's live task spec ($WORKTREES_DIR/<slug>.task.md) into the tab's otherwise-idle ROOT pane: glow + the bundled tokyonight style (else glow -s dark, else cat) painted directly to the pane TTY, repainting only on the file's mtime change, and showing one quiet dim 'task spec removed' line (no red, per the no-false-red rule) when the file is reaped with the worktree/tab — never crashing. Launched by herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh via the driver send-text surface, gated on TASK_PANE_VIEW (default on) and only when the root pane is unused; a no-op under the headless driver. Modeled on backlog-view.sh's file loop.
when_to_surface: When changing how a builder tab surfaces its task spec, or debugging why a builder tab's root pane shows/does not show the live task spec

name: scripts/herd/health-pane-view.sh
description: The HEALTH_PANE view command (HERD-568). Execed directly as the disposable health·<slug> pane's foreground process (a `clear` then, at the end, `exec tail` — never left sitting at a bare shell prompt with a stale fish greeting above it). Sidecar-aware: follows the live `<log>.progress` companion while the suite runs when one exists (else <log> itself — the bash worker's convention, already live throughout the run), swapping onto the sidecar the moment it appears; once the OBSERVED inflight marker (its 2nd arg) is gone it stops following the sidecar, prints a separator, and execs `tail -n +1 -F <log>` so the pane settles on the suite's final verdict instead of going idle. A VIEW ONLY: no model, no gate authority. Invoked by agent-watch.sh's _spawn_health_pane with `<log-path> <inflight-marker>`.
when_to_surface: When changing what the health pane actually shows, or debugging why it shows a stale greeting / nothing / the wrong stream during a live suite

name: HERD_THEME
description: Pluggable theming across all herd color surfaces: name of the active theme (default: tokyonight, the shipped built-in). A theme is a DIRECTORY holding palette.sh (console C_* truecolor + optional C_CLI_* 16-color CLI overrides) and glow.json (the glamour style). Resolution order per file: .herd/themes/<name>/ (user, project-local) -> templates/themes/<name>/ (engine built-ins) -> tokyonight fallback. An unknown/broken theme warns loudly once and falls back, never breaking a console. Threaded through agent-watch.sh (console palette), backlog-view.sh + task-spec-view.sh (glow.json), and bin/herd status/fleet/cost/why + herd-approve.sh (CLI palette). Fails soft: missing theme file -> built-in default; NO_COLOR or non-TTY renders plain. Default tokyonight is byte-identical to the pre-theme hardcoded palettes
when_to_surface: Set to switch every herd surface to a different built-in theme, or to a user theme dropped in .herd/themes/<name>/ (palette.sh + glow.json); leave unset/tokyonight for the shipped default rendering

name: scripts/herd/theme.sh
description: The HERD_THEME resolver library, sourced by every color surface. Resolves a theme dir palette.sh + glow.json via the search order (.herd/themes/<name>/ -> templates/themes/<name>/ -> tokyonight), fails soft to the built-in default (warns once on an unknown/broken theme), and blanks colors under NO_COLOR / a non-TTY stdout. herd_theme_load_console sets the truecolor C_* console palette; herd_theme_load_cli sets the 16-color c_* CLI palette (preferring C_CLI_*, falling back to C_*); herd_theme_glow_style echoes the resolved glow.json path
when_to_surface: When adding a new color-emitting surface (source theme.sh and call herd_theme_load_console / herd_theme_load_cli / herd_theme_glow_style), authoring a custom theme, or debugging why a surface did or did not pick up a theme

name: .herd/themes
description: User-defined, project-local theme directories: .herd/themes/<name>/ holding palette.sh + glow.json. Highest-precedence resolution for HERD_THEME=<name> (overrides an engine built-in of the same name). Read at render time; committing it is optional
when_to_surface: When a project wants its own color theme: drop palette.sh + glow.json into .herd/themes/<name>/ and set HERD_THEME=<name>

name: CLAIM_REQUIRED
description: Atomic work-item claiming gate (HERD-50): when on, the builder lanes (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh) run a SYNCHRONOUS claim via scripts/herd/herd-claim.sh BEFORE creating a worktree — but ONLY when a tracker id is present (HERD_CLAIM_ID, else the HERD_ITEM_REF the coordinator threads for tracked items). The claim reads the item CURRENT state+assignee through the active SCRIBE_BACKEND _backend_claim_item op, sets it In Progress + assigned to the operator identity (WATCHER_OWNER, else gh api user), and RE-READS to verify. An item already claimed by ANOTHER identity ABORTS the spawn loudly (no worktree, no agent, non-zero exit). OFF by default → today behavior exactly (no claim; the async scribe mark-in-progress is the only state write). No-id/unclaimed spawns pass through unchanged; a backend that is unreachable FAILS SOFT (warn + proceed) so a solo operator is never hard-blocked. Linear/GitHub lack compare-and-swap so claim-verify NARROWS the race to seconds; the file backend flip is atomic via git push serialization (loser push rejected, re-pull shows claimed, abort)
when_to_surface: Set to on when two or more operators work one repo concurrently and you need to stop them double-building the same backlog item; leave off (default) for a single operator or byte-identical legacy behavior. Requires a tracker id on the spawn (HERD_CLAIM_ID or HERD_ITEM_REF) to activate

name: CLAIM_RELEASE
description: Claim RELEASE for an abandoned builder (HERD-162 F12): off (default) | flag | release. The pre-spawn claim (CLAIM_REQUIRED) had no inverse — a builder that DIED before opening a PR left its tracker item In Progress + assigned forever, so a second operator's claim read it as ALREADY and aborted: the item was wedged against everyone but a dead process. With this on, the watcher's dead-builder reconcile hands the claim back. flag -> OBSERVE ONLY: journal claim_release_flagged naming the wedged ref and say so on the 💀 notification; NO tracker write. release -> also clear the claim marker through the active SCRIBE_BACKEND's _backend_release_item op (Linear/GitHub: the assignee; file: the '(claimed by …)' stamp plus the 🚧 -> 🔜 flip), leaving the item's workflow STATE untouched — an unassigned started item is exactly what the claim path treats as re-pickable, and reopening/re-queuing stays a coordinator act. HARD RAILS in both non-off modes: a claim is released ONLY for a builder that is dead, has a CLEAN worktree (no commits, no dirt), and is NOT being auto-respawned — a dead builder that left work is a human-recovery hold (releasing it invites a duplicate build on top of unrecovered work) and a respawning builder still owns its item; both refusals are journaled AND stated on the notification, never silent. Never steals another identity's claim (a foreign assignee/stamp is left alone). A backend with no release op (jira, changelog) FAILS SOFT to flag. off (default) -> byte-inert: no read, no tracker write, no journal event, and the 💀 notification string is byte-identical to before
when_to_surface: Turn on (flag first, release once you trust it) for an unattended or multi-operator run so a builder that dies pre-PR hands its tracker item back instead of wedging it against the other seat until a human unassigns it; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior. Pairs with CLAIM_REQUIRED — it releases exactly what that key claims. Watcher-affecting (takes effect on the next watcher restart)

name: TRACKED_SPAWNS
description: Tracker-routed spawn enforcement (HERD-64): make "every builder is traceable to a tracked work item" a PROJECT POLICY rather than an operator convention. off (default) | required. off → today's behavior EXACTLY: the spawn surfaces (herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh / spawn.sh) impose no gate. required → a spawn carrying NO tracker ref (HERD_CLAIM_ID, else the HERD_ITEM_REF the coordinator threads for tracked items) is REFUSED with a loud one-line reason, creating nothing; HERD_FORCE_SPAWN=1 (or a lane's --force) is the explicit escape hatch that lets it through and JOURNALS the bypass (tracked_spawn_bypassed). Enforced via herd_tracked_spawn_or_abort (herd-config.sh); the durable spawn queue threads the ref through a sidecar so a queued tracked intent is never re-refused at drain time. Any value but required is treated as off. Composes with CLAIM_REQUIRED (HERD-50): the ref set is identical, so with both on every spawn is atomically CLAIMED and VISIBLE in the tracker — TRACKED_SPAWNS enforces visibility, CLAIM_REQUIRED exclusivity
when_to_surface: Set to required on a shared repo (or any project that wants an auditable tracker trail) so no builder is spawned off-book — every worktree maps to a tracked item; leave off (default) for a single operator or byte-identical legacy behavior. Pairs with CLAIM_REQUIRED for multi-operator repos

name: herd-claim.sh
description: Atomic pre-spawn work-item claim (HERD-50): sourced by herd-quick.sh / herd-feature.sh and called ONCE before worktree creation. herd_claim_or_abort resolves the tracker id (HERD_CLAIM_ID else HERD_ITEM_REF) and operator identity (WATCHER_OWNER else gh api user), and — only when CLAIM_REQUIRED is on and an id is present — claims the item synchronously through the active SCRIBE_BACKEND _backend_claim_item op (sourced in a subshell so backend helpers never leak). Returns non-zero to ABORT the spawn when the item is already claimed by another identity; returns 0 (proceed) for our-own-claim, self-claim, no-id/disabled, and fail-soft backend-unreachable paths
when_to_surface: Internal to the builder lanes; not launched directly. Governs whether a spawn claims its tracked item before building, gated by CLAIM_REQUIRED

name: MCP_PROVISION
description: Builder MCP tool-provisioning surface (the tools SIBLING of CONTEXT_PROVISION): a SPACE-SEPARATED list of MCP server names wired into every spawned builder worktree's project-level .claude/settings.json (mcpServers block) by herd_write_mcp_servers (herd-config.sh), called from new-feature.sh, so a builder can reach those tools with no per-session setup. Empty/unset (default) → NOTHING written, settings.json byte-identical to today. The write is ADDITIVE + NON-CLOBBER (per-entry: an existing/user-authored server of the same name is never overwritten), idempotent, and atomic — same guarantees as the rate-limit hook it merges alongside. Each name resolves to a {command,args,env} entry from a BUILT-IN default, overridable per server by MCP_<NAME>_COMMAND / MCP_<NAME>_ARGS / MCP_<NAME>_ENV (NAME upper-cased, -/. → _), set by editing .herd/config directly (dynamic per-server keys are not registered here). A name with no built-in and no _COMMAND override is ignored (forward-compatible). PRIVACY: credentials are NEVER written — MCP_<NAME>_ENV lists env-var NAMES passed through as "${VAR}" references Claude Code expands at launch from the runtime env (populated from .herd/secrets), so no secret value lands in any committed/generated file; DENY_PATHS stays honored. Built-ins: context7 (up-to-date library docs, high-value for CONSUMER projects; low-value in bash herdkit itself — the mechanism is the deliverable) and graphify-mcp (local example server)
when_to_surface: Set to e.g. 'context7' to wire the up-to-date-library-docs MCP server into each builder worktree so builders can query live library docs (most valuable on real code CONSUMER projects herdkit runs on); leave empty (default) for today's byte-identical settings.json with no MCP wiring. Space-separate multiple servers; override a server's command/args/env or add a custom server via MCP_<NAME>_COMMAND/_ARGS/_ENV in .herd/config

name: GRAPHIFY_BIN
description: Machine-local path to the graphify call-graph binary (PyPI 'graphifyy'; usually ~/.local/bin/graphify) that the COORDINATOR resolves for its pre-spawn/periodic impact-conflict analysis — the coordinator-side THIRD LEG alongside CONTEXT_PROVISION=codemap (builder grounding) and MCP_PROVISION graphify-mcp (builder tools). Resolution: this key, else 'graphify' on PATH; when NEITHER resolves the analysis is SKIPPED SILENTLY (no warning, no red row — the tool is an optional accelerator, never required). MACHINE-scoped (HERD-47): the path is per-machine, so 'herd config set GRAPHIFY_BIN <path>' routes to the gitignored .herd/config.local, never the committed baseline. The coordinator runs 'graphify update --no-cluster' to rebuild graphify-out/graph.json LLM-free (zero Claude quota), then crosses each in-flight worktree's changed files against the other worktrees AND the candidate item's likely file surface to sequence/warn on overlap before spawning. HONEST SCOPE: FILE-level overlap + within-file structure ONLY — graphify's bash cross-file CALL resolution is weak (measured 2026-07-06: 0 cross-file call links among the big engine scripts; the ~136 repo-wide cross-file links are mostly imports/contains), so this is NOT a cross-script call graph
when_to_surface: Set to the absolute path of the graphify binary on THIS machine (e.g. ~/.local/bin/graphify) to enable the coordinator's pre-spawn overlap read; leave unset to fall back to 'graphify' on PATH, and if that is absent too the analysis is skipped silently (optional — the coordinator still spawns normally)

name: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
description: Claude Code custom model endpoint (HERD-171): the standard ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL env Claude Code already honors, exposed as a MACHINE-scoped herdkit config key so an operator can point the claude runtime at an enterprise/BAA-covered gateway or a local model server without forking the driver. Empty/unset (default) → Claude Code's default Anthropic endpoint; behavior is byte-identical. When set, herd-config.sh exports it and scripts/herd/driver.sh injects it as --env on every herdr agent start (and headless children inherit the export), so interactive spawns, one-shot drainers, and detached agents all hit the same endpoint. MACHINE-scoped (HERD-47): `herd config set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL <url>` routes to the gitignored .herd/config.local — NEVER the committed baseline (a tenant/gateway URL is secrets-adjacent). Companion credentials (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) live in .herd/secrets or the control-room process env, never in .herd/config. Composes with the model matrix (HERD-151): MODEL_* still pick the model id; this key only relocates the endpoint the claude runtime talks to. See docs/sensitive-data.md.
when_to_surface: Set on a machine that must route Claude Code traffic through an enterprise/BAA endpoint or a local model gateway (e.g. https://my-corp.example/v1 or http://127.0.0.1:11434); leave unset for Anthropic's default public endpoint

name: GH_TOKEN
description: Optional per-project GitHub token (HERD-671 leg 3) that partitions this project's `gh` calls (REST and GraphQL alike) onto their own GitHub rate-limit bucket. GitHub limits are PER USER, not per token: several projects/watchers on one machine sharing the operator's plain `gh auth login` identity all draw from the SAME 5000/hr GraphQL bucket, so a heavy evening on one project can starve every other watcher's gate/merge reads (GROUNDED 2026-08-13: four watchers here exhausted it together). Setting GH_TOKEN only PARTITIONS anything when it names a DIFFERENTLY-OWNED identity — a machine account or a GitHub App installation token; a second personal PAT for the SAME human account still shares that human's one bucket and partitions nothing. Lives ONLY in .herd/secrets (gitignored) — never in .herd/config or .herd/config.local, and `herd config set GH_TOKEN` is refused (secret-shaped key name, _config_secret_key). scripts/herd/herd-config.sh reads the single GH_TOKEN= line via `grep` (never sources the file, so no other secret and no arbitrary shell code in .herd/secrets ever reaches this process) and exports it into the watcher's own process — every lane/builder worktree inherits the export chain from there, so this is the ONE place the passthrough is wired, not a per-lane copy. `gh` (and `gh api graphql`) already prefers GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN over stored `gh auth login` credentials the moment it is present in the environment, so exporting it here IS the whole integration — no other seam changes to use it. An already-exported GH_TOKEN (the operator's own shell, a CI runner) wins over the file. FAIL-SOFT + byte-identical when absent: no .herd/secrets, an unreadable file, or no GH_TOKEN line in it exports nothing, and `gh` falls back to its already-authenticated identity exactly as before this key existed. See docs/sensitive-data.md (Part 3) for the machine-account requirement.
when_to_surface: Set GH_TOKEN in .herd/secrets to a machine-account or GitHub App token when this project's watcher is exhausting its shared GraphQL/REST rate-limit bucket alongside other projects on the same machine; a second personal PAT does not help, it must be a differently-owned identity.
