Leave unset (default) for a solo machine or when the shared budget is not a problem.

name: .herd/config.local
description: Per-user / per-machine overlay for .herd/config (gitignored, HERD-47): sourced AFTER .herd/config by herd-config.sh so its keys OVERRIDE the committed baseline, mirroring the settings.json/settings.local.json convention. Absent => effective config is byte-identical to a single-file setup (backward-compatible). Write to it with `herd config set --local KEY VALUE`; every key marked scope=machine in this manifest routes there by DEFAULT even without --local — currently: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, COORDINATOR_AUTONOMY, COORDINATOR_WATCHDOG, DEAD_BUILDER_AUTORESPAWN, DRAFT_AUTO_PROMOTE, ENGINE_PAUSE, GRAPHIFY_BIN, HERD_DRIVER, INFRA_BREAKER_COOLDOWN, INFRA_BREAKER_MAX, MODEL_ADVISE, MODEL_COORDINATOR, MODEL_ESCALATE, MODEL_FEATURE, MODEL_QUICK, MODEL_RESEARCH, MODEL_RESOLVER, MODEL_REVIEW, MODEL_SCRIBE, REVIEW_MODEL_ESCALATED, TEAM_ALIASES, TOKEN_MODE, WATCHER_OWNER, WATCHER_VIEW, WATCHER_VIEW_ASSIGNEE, WATCHER_VIEW_AUTHOR, WATCHER_VIEW_DEPS_LABEL, WATCHER_VIEW_LABEL, WATCHER_VIEW_STATUS, WATCH_CLAUDE_PROBE_TIMEOUT, WATCH_HOTKEYS, WEDGE_AUTOWAKE, WORKSPACE_NAME. `herd config list` shows each value source (baseline | local). ZERO-SECRET: credentials stay in .herd/secrets
when_to_surface: Keep per-user/per-machine state (driver, model-tier & token-budget choices, operator-posture opt-ins) out of the shared committed baseline so a collaborator edit never diverges main or dirties the ff-only `herd update` pull

name: .claude/commands/coordinator.md
description: The RENDERED coordinator skill (HERD-214): render_skill writes it from templates/coordinator.md.tmpl + the effective .herd/config (+ .herd/config.local) on herd init / update / upgrade / reload / render / a render-affecting `config set`, and its basename follows COORDINATOR_CMD. IGNORED, never tracked — a PER-MACHINE derived artifact, exactly like .herd/config.local: teams share the TEMPLATE, each checkout renders its own copy. HERD-519: the ignore ENTRY is CHECKOUT-LOCAL (.git/info/exclude), never the committed .gitignore — writing it to a tracked file made every fresh clone go dirty on its first render; a project whose .gitignore already carries the line keeps it untouched (no churn, no removal). A tracked render dirtied every checkout any of those commands ran in, which made the sweep FLAG worktrees it should have reaped, the watcher's startup reap skip stranded trees as dirty, the stale-base gate HOLD PRs on a bogus overlap, and the ff-only `herd update` pull refuse. `herd upgrade` untracks a legacy tracked copy once (staged deletion + the checkout-local exclude entry) and every render path recreates the file when absent. scripts/herd/derived-files.sh is the ONE list of these regenerable derived files; the sweep's dirt classifier, the startup reap's dirty check, and the stale-base overlap all excuse them from it
when_to_surface: When a render appears in `git status` or a PR diff (it should never be committed — delete the tracked copy, `herd render` regenerates it), when a worktree will not reap or a PR is held on a stale base naming .claude/commands/, and when adding a new engine-generated file that any checkout can regenerate — put it in scripts/herd/derived-files.sh rather than teaching each reaper about it

name: .claude/commands/autopilot.md
description: The RENDERED /autopilot STANDING WATCH-AND-DRAIN skill (HERD-515): render_skill writes it from templates/autopilot.md.tmpl through the SAME token machinery, on the SAME paths (herd init / update / upgrade / reload / render / a render-affecting `config set`) as the coordinator render, under a FIXED basename — no config key selects it. The skill is DRAIN MODE with its 'backlog empty' STOP replaced by an IDLE WAIT: an idempotent yolo-posture check (compare `herd posture show yolo` against the effective config and apply ONLY if a lever differs — a blind re-apply restarts the watcher for nothing), then a standing loop that each cycle polls `herd backlog`, `gh issue list`, `herd notes` and in-flight gate state, runs the coordinator skill's Drain mode loop while open work exists (CITED, never forked — one doctrine, two entry points, multi-seat rule 2), and self-paces a 20-30 minute wakeup when idle. Hard stops stay BUDGET_DAILY, genuine escalation, and an explicit operator stop; an unreachable gh or tracker backend logs its one-line reason and idle-waits rather than crashing the loop. GITIGNORED, never tracked — a PER-MACHINE derived artifact carried in scripts/herd/derived-files.sh exactly like the coordinator render
when_to_surface: When the operator wants to turn the herd on and walk away — `/autopilot` in the coordinator seat holds the yolo posture and keeps draining work as it arrives instead of stopping at an empty backlog; when a night run should survive an idle stretch without a human re-invoking `/coordinator yolo`. Read templates/autopilot.md.tmpl (the shared source) rather than any machine's render, and when the DRAIN DOCTRINE itself changes edit the coordinator template's Drain mode section — this skill cites it, so a fork here would silently drift

name: .herd/steps.tsv
description: Declarative PIPELINE STEP LIST (HERD-132), committed like .herd/links: one TAB-separated row per custom stage — name | at (post-build|post-healthcheck|pre-merge|post-merge) | run (shell command or skill:<name>) | on_fail (block|warn) | hold (none|notify|approve). Blank / '#'-prefixed lines ignored. Validated by 'steps.sh validate'; consumed by scripts/herd/steps.sh. Absent/empty ⇒ byte-identical pipeline (feature ships dormant)

name: .herd/triggers.tsv
description: Declarative SCHEDULED/TRIGGERED RUN LIST (HERD-169), committed like .herd/steps.tsv: one TAB-separated row per trigger — name | schedule (@hourly|@daily|@weekly|every:<N>[smhd]|manual) | lane (quick|feature|mechanical, HERD-673) | task (quick/feature: workflow text; mechanical: the literal shell command to run; {item}/{name} tokens either way) | input (shell command whose stdout lines are the input set) | OPTIONAL 6th column agent (quick/feature only: a .herd/agents/<name>.md roster definition to build the spawn with, threaded via HERD_AGENT — blank/absent ⇒ no override). Blank / '#'-prefixed lines ignored. Validated by 'triggers.sh validate'; consumed by scripts/herd/triggers.sh, which diffs the input set against .herd/trigger-state/<name>.snapshot and enqueues one spawn (quick/feature) or runs one command directly (mechanical) per new line. Absent/empty ⇒ byte-identical engine (feature ships dormant)

name: templates/postures.tsv
description: The CANONICAL CONFIG POSTURES (HERD-153): the committed, authoritative set of named operating postures — solo-auto (MERGE_POLICY=auto) | team-approve (MERGE_POLICY=approve + HUMAN_VERIFY_POLICY=hold) | gated-push (PUSH_GATE=human + PR_FLOW=draft) | custom-steps (a .herd/steps.tsv approve-stage) | observe-only (MERGE_POLICY=observe) | docs-lab (HERD-409/#520: DOCS_ONLY_GLOB + lighter MODEL_FEATURE/MODEL_REVIEW, pairs with the docs/research-lab PROJECT ARCHETYPE). Each posture is a small named bundle of .herd/config KEY=VALUE settings (name | keys | intent, TAB-separated). SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH consumed by the posture-matrix sim (scripts/herd/sim/sandbox-posture-matrix.sh, which proves the gate loop under each posture) and by HERD-141 init v2 posture profiles (shipped: `herd init` offers + renders these bundles into .herd/config) at herd init time. Add a posture here, not in the sim or installer, and every consumer picks it up
when_to_surface: When choosing or documenting a project's governance stance at init, or when adding a new named posture bundle — edit templates/postures.tsv (authoritative), then the posture-matrix sim and HERD-141 both consume it

name: herd conformance <report|run>
description: The capability CONFORMANCE MATRIX (HERD-144): joins the capabilities manifest (templates/capabilities.tsv) against the committed proof map (templates/conformance.tsv, a SIBLING keyed by capability name so the manifest stays byte-identical) to make per-feature test coverage accountable. `report` [--json] is DETERMINISTIC + no-LLM: it lists every capability with NO proof mapping (a gap) and every mapping whose proof_ref no longer exists (rot), exiting non-zero ONLY on rot (a dangling ref — gaps alone never fail). `run` [--kind unit] executes the mapped proofs and writes conformance.json (capability -> verdict -> sha -> timestamp), the whole-surface analog of the sim scorecard. GATE/AUTOFIX RATCHET (HERD-424, audit P3.2 — no flag): PLAIN `report`/`run` ALSO require every capability explicitly classified gate|autofix in a THIRD sibling, templates/capability-class.tsv (never guessed from description prose), to carry a real, existing proof_kind=sim mapping — a none-yet note or a unit/render-only mapping is a loud, default-visible failure (JSON `ratchet{class_present,count,violations[]}` + a human GATE/AUTOFIX RATCHET section), driving a non-zero exit on top of the existing rot check. FAIL-SOFT: an absent proof map or class file is a soft note (nothing to enforce), never a red row; REPORT-ONLY — nothing here is a merge gate.
when_to_surface: When auditing which capabilities have or lack test coverage, after adding a capability or a test so the proof map stays honest, or to catch a proof_ref a rename/deletion left dangling; run `herd conformance report` for the gap/rot list (it already reds on any classified gate/autofix capability missing sim proof) and `herd conformance run` to execute mapped proofs into conformance.json

name: MODEL_* ref <driver>:<model>
description: Runtime-qualified MODEL_* value (HERD-151): every MODEL_* key accepts an optionally driver-qualified ref '<driver>:<model>' pinning a role's agent to a shipped runtime driver (templates/drivers/<name>.driver) AND model, not just Claude. A BARE value (no '<driver>:' prefix) resolves to the default driver with the whole value as the model, so every existing bare-claude config is BYTE-IDENTICAL. Resolved at spawn time by scripts/herd/driver.sh (herd_model_resolve/herd_model_for_spawn) — the seam next to PR #264's DRIVER_AGENT_* exec bindings; an UNKNOWN driver prefix is a LOUD hard error at spawn, never a silent claude fallback. The bare model id is what the runtime spawns on --model; the resolved driver feeds the queued HERD-150 P2-P5 runtime routing
when_to_surface: When pointing a role (feature/quick/review/scribe/research/resolver/coordinator/advise) at a non-default runtime, or reading why a MODEL_* value with a colon fails loudly at spawn — write a bare model for today's default-driver behavior, or <driver>:<model> naming a shipped driver

name: templates/models.tsv
description: Model SUGGESTIONS CATALOG (HERD-151): an advisory, perishable TSV of model refs with a coarse tier (judgment|balanced|cheap|docs), a role-fit hint and an as-of date. 'herd config set MODEL_*' consults it to SUGGEST a fit and to soft-note an uncatalogued model or an unshipped driver prefix — it NEVER refuses an operator's model (catalog / CLAUDE.md / manual set are coequal, none required). Not a gate: a stale or missing row never blocks a spawn or a merge. Browse with 'herd config models'; validate rows with 'herd config models lint' (tier + date per row). Keyed by the bare model id; price a catalogued foreign model in cost.sh too, else it shows as 'unpriced' in herd cost
when_to_surface: When choosing a MODEL_* value, or curating the recommended model set for a project; extend it (bump each row's as_of) as runtimes ship new models

name: herd config models
description: Print the model suggestions catalog (templates/models.tsv) — each ref with its tier, role-fit hint and as-of date. 'herd config models lint' validates every row (4 columns, tier in judgment|balanced|cheap|docs, as_of shaped YYYY-MM-DD) and exits non-zero on any malformed row. Read-only; advisory (never a gate)
when_to_surface: Browsing recommended models before 'herd config set MODEL_*', or checking the catalog is well-formed after editing templates/models.tsv

name: create-retry.sh
description: The DURABLE RETRY QUEUE for failed tracker-item creates (HERD-267). Sourced (never launched) by scribe-step.sh and sweep.sh. create_retry_enqueue writes the ORIGINAL request text to $WORKTREES_DIR/.create-retry/<hash>.text BEFORE the drainer drops its claim, so a create the tracker refuses can no longer be silently consumed (the 2026-07-10 incident: Linear's free-tier issue cap ate six coordinator filings over 2h with an empty queue and no trace). create_retry_class separates a PERMANENT wall (cap | auth) from a RETRYABLE hiccup (transient | unknown); permanent entries surface loudly with their own label and are never re-injected, so a doomed request never spins. create_retry_reinject copies due entries back into the backlog queue with exponential backoff, and create_retry_resolve removes an entry on a CONFIRMED create. Entries are keyed by a content hash, so repeated failures of one request COALESCE into one row carrying its attempt count. Fail-soft throughout; inert while CREATE_SELFHEAL=off or the queue is empty
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when tracker-create failure handling, its error classification, or the retry backoff changes. Operators can run `bash scripts/herd/create-retry.sh rows` to see what is stuck

name: CREATE_SELFHEAL
description: Tracker-create failure SELF-HEAL (HERD-267): on (default) | off. on -> a backend create the tracker REFUSES is diverted into a durable retry queue instead of being dropped: the request text is written to disk before the claim is released, the reason is classified (cap | auth | transient | unknown), journaled as `scribe_add_failed`, and shouted with a label distinct per class (no-false-red doctrine works in both directions — a wall must not read as a flake). The scribe drainer re-injects due entries with exponential backoff on its next poll, capped by CREATE_RETRY_MAX; a PERMANENT reason (issue cap, bad API key) is never retried automatically. `herd sweep` gains an ADVISORY leg that finds merged PRs whose `Refs:` line names no tracker item (the create never landed) and enqueues a search-first retroactive-linkage request into the backlog queue — it never writes the tracker itself. off -> byte-identical to the pre-HERD-267 behavior: a refused create reports NOCHANGE and the request is lost. Consumed by scribe-step.sh and sweep.sh via create-retry.sh
when_to_surface: Leave on (default) on any project whose tracker can refuse a create — an API backend with a plan/quota limit, a key that can expire, or a flaky endpoint. Set off only to reproduce the old drop-on-failure behavior; nothing else in the engine changes

name: CREATE_RETRY_MAX
description: How many times a durably-queued tracker create is re-attempted before it is marked PERMANENT (HERD-267): a positive integer, default 5. Bounds only the TRANSIENT and UNKNOWN classes — a cap or auth failure is permanent on its FIRST attempt, because retrying a wall cannot succeed and the spin is precisely what buried the reason during the incident. PERMANENT means stop retrying and shout, never discard: the request text stays on disk, the coalesced console row keeps rendering it, and a `herd scribe` re-drains it once a human fixes the cause. A non-numeric value reads as 5. Consumed by create-retry.sh
when_to_surface: Raise it when the tracker API is known-flaky and a long backoff tail is preferable to an early permanent row; lower it to surface a stuck create sooner. Backoff is exponential (60s doubling, capped at 1h), so each extra attempt roughly doubles the wait before the permanent row appears

name: work-units/git-pr.sh
description: THE GIT-PR WORK-UNIT ADAPTER BODY, Phase 3 (HERD-395/HERD-398; design: docs/spikes/work-unit-abstraction.md): the PR-specific implementations MOVED out of agent-watch.sh and behind the work-unit facade — do_merge (merge actuation/verify, gh pr merge --match-head-commit + the $STATE row), reconcile_backlog + _reconcile_pr_ref (reconcile: gh pr view Refs: fetch), _classify_review_tier (review dispatch argv: gh pr diff --name-only), already_merged (state-file key idempotency read), _merge_method_flag/_delete_branch_flag (merge actuation flags), _watcher_tick_fields + _prs_fetch_tick (discovery: the ticks gh pr list --json call + candidate schema field set). Selected by WORK_UNIT_KIND=git-pr (default; the only kind that ships). Sourced by agent-watch.sh under the SAME function names the code always used, so every call site is unchanged — a pure relocation, byte-identical git-pr pipeline. Some named seams (teardown/_reap_slug, _reconcile_via_ref, the discover_feature_worktrees candidate join, stale-dup-gate.sh) deliberately did NOT move — already kind-agnostic or too entangled to extract without semantic risk; see the file header for the full accounting.
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched by agent-watch.sh; REFERENCE-MODEL-ONLY (spike §9.1) — do_merge has zero production call sites (superseded live by pysrc/herd/live_runtime.py's LiveActuator.merge); doc-apply (HERD-399) shipped as a python-only adapter instead of a sibling bash file here, per spike §9.4's re-plan

name: WORK_UNIT_KIND
description: The work-unit delivery-vehicle adapter selector (HERD-398/HERD-399, docs/spikes/work-unit-abstraction.md). BASH side (agent-watch.sh boot check + scripts/herd/work-unit.sh's wunit_resolve_adapter) still ships exactly ONE kind, git-pr (default) — todays exact gh pr create/list/view/diff/merge pipeline, byte-identical to before; any other value there fails STRICT to git-pr with a loud warning. PYTHON side (herd.work_unit.resolve_adapter, the LIVE engine) now ships a real SECOND kind too: doc-apply (HERD-399, §9.4) — a manifest-driven (<WORKTREES_DIR>/<slug>.unit.json) documentation change-set landed straight onto the default branch with NO gh pr create/merge anywhere in its chain, gated by the same fail-closed path-allowlist + health/review composition shape as git-pr. Neither engine's default changes: WORK_UNIT_KIND unset (or any value besides the kind(s) each engine ships) still resolves git-pr / refuses loudly — doc-apply is reached only via an EXPLICIT WORK_UNIT_KIND=doc-apply AND a <slug>.unit.json manifest on disk (STRICTLY OPT-IN).
when_to_surface: Set to git-pr (default, both engines) or, on the python engine only, doc-apply for a manifest-driven docs-only delivery; any other value is a loud not-yet-supported refusal, never a silent behavior change

name: herd.work_unit.DocApplyAdapter
description: THE DOC-APPLY WORK-UNIT ADAPTER BODY (HERD-399, pysrc/herd/work_unit.py; design: docs/spikes/work-unit-abstraction.md §9.4's re-planned Phase 4 — python-first, not a bash rail, because git-pr's own bash adapter is already reference-model-only post-port). Implements open (writes the <slug>.unit.json manifest), list_open (filesystem glob, fail-soft on a malformed manifest), inspect, gate (fail-closed path allowlist THEN the same LiveGates.health/.review composition GitPrAdapter.gate uses, via a synthetic slug-keyed candidate), and apply (LiveDocApply: a scoped `git checkout <revision> -- <paths>` onto $MAIN, commit, ff-only push with one rebase retry and a hard rollback on a rejected push — never gh pr create, never gh pr merge). reconcile/teardown are deliberately NOT IMPLEMENTED — those two legs stay bash's job for every kind (spike §9.1), and the generic primitives a future wiring phase would call (_reconcile_via_ref, _reap_slug) are already kind-agnostic and reusable as-is with no code change on either side. Selected by WORK_UNIT_KIND=doc-apply (python engine only); STRICTLY OPT-IN — with no manifest on disk, list_open returns [] and nothing about the git-pr path changes.
when_to_surface: The seam a real doc-apply delivery plugs into once a caller writes a <slug>.unit.json manifest and resolves WORK_UNIT_KIND=doc-apply; not wired into any live_runtime.py call site by this PR (a skeleton, like GitPrAdapter before it)

name: <slug>.unit.json
description: The doc-apply work-unit MANIFEST (HERD-399, spike §3.2 step 1), written by herd.work_unit.DocApplyAdapter.open at <WORKTREES_DIR>/<slug>.unit.json: {kind:"doc-apply", slug, revision, item_ref, paths:[...], title, body, worktree, opened_at, state}. paths entries are LITERAL FILE PATHS, PERIOD (the accepted-input invariant, stated once on herd.work_unit._safe_manifest_path): each must be a normalized relative literal path — no ".." or absolute form, NO pathspec wildcard (* ? [) or leading-colon pathspec magic (HERD-399 round 4: "docs/*" cleared the allowlist, blinded the non-recursive ls-tree tree-guard, then matched RECURSIVELY at checkout so a file deleted at <revision> silently survived a recorded-clean landing), matching DOC_APPLY_PATH_GLOB (if the operator set one) or the hardcoded ^docs/ default, and resolving to exactly one blob at <revision> (a directory-shaped path is refused as directory-path-not-supported; anything that cannot be PROVEN a blob — missing at <revision>, transient ls-tree failure — is refused as path-not-a-blob-at-revision, the HERD-399 round-5 strict check); any violation makes gate/apply both refuse. NOTE doc-apply cannot express a DELETION at all today: a scoped checkout only adds/updates, so a single-file path deleted at <revision> is refused up front rather than silently under-applying — a change-set that removes a doc needs a git-pr unit. state flips open -> applied (at-most-once; list_open excludes applied/reaped) — ONLY once the change is verified to have reached the remote, never merely committed to the shared MAIN checkout locally. A malformed or unreadable manifest is a journaled skip (doc_apply_manifest_invalid), never a crash; a manifest whose worktree HEAD has moved past its declared revision is journaled stale (doc_apply_manifest_stale) and skipped until re-opened. No manifest on disk = no doc-apply behavior at all (the STRICTLY OPT-IN invariant).
when_to_surface: When a caller wants to publish a doc-apply delivery candidate for the watcher's python engine to discover, or when debugging why a doc-apply unit is/isn't showing up in list_open

name: DOC_APPLY_PATH_GLOB
description: The doc-apply FAIL-CLOSED path allowlist override (HERD-399 round 3, herd.work_unit._doc_apply_path_pattern): a regex, matched PREFIX-anchored (re.match) against each manifest path AFTER normalization. Blank (default) → the hardcoded ^docs/ prefix applies; every doc-apply unit's paths must clear it or gate/apply refuse. Deliberately a DEDICATED key, NOT a reuse of DOCS_ONLY_GLOB (the review-tier classifier) — two rounds of review found reusing that key unsafe in BOTH directions: an unanchored operator pattern widened the allowlist to match a substring anywhere in a path, and the anchored fix then made a real DOCS_ONLY_GLOB value (e.g. this repo's own "[.](md|txt)", a suffix-shaped pattern for its ACTUAL job) unable to match ANY docs/ path at all, refusing every doc-apply unit. An unparseable pattern is DROPPED in favor of the hardcoded default rather than raising — a bad regex must never silently widen a safety gate.
when_to_surface: Set only to scope doc-apply's allowlist beyond the default docs/ prefix (e.g. to also allow a project's notes/ tree); leave unset for the safe default

name: resolver-claim.sh
description: THE cross-seat resolver-dispatch CLAIM (HERD-423, docs/spikes/cross-seat-coordination.md §5 Phase 1): a repo-visible v1 claim closing the proven cross-seat gap (audit G5/N8) where two seats with separate local $TREES and one shared GitHub remote could each independently spawn_resolver the SAME conflicting (PR, exact head sha), racing pushes. Substrate is a single HTML-hidden marker PR comment (never a Statuses/Check-Run write, which would risk stranding mergeability per HERD-247), upserted in place: <!-- herd:resolve-claim v1 pr/sha/seat/slug/epoch/state(claimed|done|escalated) -->. Wired as the ONE choke point inside spawn_resolver (agent-watch.sh), layered ABOVE the existing same-seat _resolver_in_flight guard, never replacing it: _resolve_claim_should_hold reads the current claim before any local record/spawn and HOLDS behind a live foreign claim (state=claimed inside RESOLVE_CLAIM_TTL, or a foreign done/escalated terminal for the exact sha) without burning local respawn budget; _resolve_claim_publish_claimed publishes our own claim before record_resolve_attempt; _resolve_claim_publish_terminal best-effort-updates the shared claim to done/escalated at the _classify_conflict result/escalation seam. A claim for a DIFFERENT sha reads as stale (ignored); a TTL-expired foreign claimed row is a bounded steal (journaled resolve_claim_steal). Parsing NEVER evals the untrusted comment body (a malformed/forged marker is rejected field-by-field and read as "no claim", never a crash or a false hold). Any gh read/write failure fails soft to "no claim" / best-effort-skip — never fabricates a foreign claim, never holds the gate on an outage. Ship-dormant: every function is a no-op (zero gh calls) unless BOTH RESOLVE_CLAIM is a recognized on-value AND WATCHER_SCOPE=all (_effective_resolve_claim)
when_to_surface: The seam to change when the cross-seat claim's marker schema, TTL/steal policy, or hold/proceed decision changes; sourced by agent-watch.sh

name: RESOLVE_CLAIM
description: Ship-dormant lever (default off) arming the cross-seat resolver-dispatch claim (HERD-423, resolver-claim.sh). Recognized on-values (on|true|yes|1) arm the claim ONLY when ALSO WATCHER_SCOPE=all (team mode) — WATCHER_SCOPE=mine (default) or RESOLVE_CLAIM off/unset/unrecognized all read "off": no gh comment reads/writes, no journal lines, byte-identical to pre-HERD-423. When both conditions hold, spawn_resolver consults/publishes the shared PR-comment claim before any local dispatch, so at most one seat resolves a given (PR, exact head sha)
when_to_surface: Set to on (with WATCHER_SCOPE=all) on a SHARED repo with multiple watcher seats to prevent two seats from independently dispatching a conflict resolver onto the same commit; leave off/unset for a solo install (behavior unchanged)

name: RESOLVE_CLAIM_TTL
description: Seconds a foreign "claimed" cross-seat resolver-claim row (RESOLVE_CLAIM) stays binding before it is a bounded steal target (resolver-claim.sh:_resolve_claim_ttl). Any non-numeric/unset value falls back to the safe default 2700 (45 min — comfortably above resolver startup grace + a typical resolve round), so a typo can never widen or shrink the hold unpredictably. Only consulted when RESOLVE_CLAIM is armed (see RESOLVE_CLAIM); otherwise unread
when_to_surface: Raise it if resolvers on this project routinely run longer than 45 minutes before pushing/escalating, so a still-working foreign resolver is never stolen from under itself; leave unset for the default

name: team-presence-live.sh
description: THE live builder-state publish/consume channel for TEAM_PRESENCE=live (HERD-661, GitHub issue #639 phase 2). PUBLISH: on the SAME ~60s throttled tick as the phase-1 join (_team_presence_live_publish_tick, agent-watch.sh), each seat iterates its OWN already-discovered FEATS worktree table and upserts ONE versioned, epoch-stamped, HTML-hidden marker comment (never a Statuses/Check-Run write) per PR it authored and is actively building: <!-- herd:team-presence-live v1 pr/slug/seat/status/epoch -->, REUSING resolver-claim.sh's exact upsert-in-place substrate rather than a new one. A worktree with no resolved PR publishes nothing, and a PR authored by someone else (ADOPT_REMOTE_PRS) is never published to. CONSUME: _team_presence_live_status_for <pr> is the pure read side — loads the marker (if any) and prints "<status>\t<epoch>"; agent-watch.sh's _team_presence_live_augment calls it for every phase-1-attributed PR (bounded set, same cadence) to append the freshness fields the ungated-PR row renders as "active Nm ago" (fresh, inside _TEAM_PRESENCE_LIVE_STALE_SECS=300s) or "last active Nh ago (stale?)" (past it). Parsing NEVER evals the untrusted comment body (a malformed/forged marker is rejected field-by-field and reads as "no live data"). Any gh read/write failure fails soft to no-live-data — never a fabricated status, never a crash, never a held row; a caller always falls back to TEAM_PRESENCE=on's plain attribution. Every function is independently sourceable/testable (falls back to plain `gh` / WATCHER_OWNER when agent-watch.sh's own helpers are not in scope), mirroring resolver-claim.sh's own fallback discipline. Ship-dormant: every function is a no-op unless a caller actively invokes it, which only happens under TEAM_PRESENCE=live
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the live marker's schema, staleness window, or publish/consume eligibility rules change. Surface it when explaining where a '· active Nm ago' / '(stale?)' clause on an ungated-PR row comes from, or when TEAM_PRESENCE=live shows no freshness clause despite a teammate visibly building (channel unreachable — check gh auth / rate limit on their PR's comment history)

name: CHECKOUT_GUARD
description: Auto-restore the shared checkout ($MAIN) when it is found detached-but-otherwise-clean (HERD-452) — on | off (default off for consumers, ship-dormant; on in herdkit's own dogfood .herd/config). GROUNDED 2026-07-31: $MAIN was found detached at a PR branch's head (#563), and the main-health suite — which ran the heavy suite DIRECTLY inside the live $MAIN working tree, unlike the sandboxed baseline-vs-candidate leg (HERD-361) — reproduced a red off that FEATURE branch's own code and labeled it 'MAIN RED', training the operator to ignore a standing alarm that named nothing true about the default branch. Two parts of the HERD-452 fix are UNCONDITIONAL (never gated on this key, because a lying alarm or a suite that can mutate the operator's live tree is never acceptable): (1) _main_health_worker now ALWAYS runs the heavy suite in a DISPOSABLE detached worktree pinned to the dispatched sha, never live inside $MAIN; (2) _main_health_dispatch asserts $MAIN is ATTACHED to the default branch with no foreign contamination (_checkout_offenders, HERD-361) BEFORE every dispatch — unsound → the attempt is WITHHELD (no worker, no marker, no verdict, ever) and journaled once as main_health result=contaminated. THIS KEY gates only the third part, the AUTO-HEAL: on → when reconcile_checkout_cleanliness (HERD-361) finds $MAIN detached AND otherwise CLEAN (no offenders — nothing tracked would be discarded), it runs a plain `git checkout <default-branch>` (never --force, never reset --hard — a clean tree needs neither), journals checkout_guard result=restored, and clears the standing CHECKOUT UNCLEAN row the same tick. A DIRTY checkout (offenders present, detached or not) is NEVER auto-touched no matter this lever — that evidence stays for a human. off (default) → byte-identical: no checkout, no journal line, the existing HERD-361 advisory row is the only signal.
when_to_surface: Enable in a repo that wants a detached shared checkout to self-heal instead of standing until a human notices (herdkit enables it for itself after the 2026-07-31 #563 incident). Leave off (default) elsewhere: zero behavior change, and the HERD-361 CHECKOUT UNCLEAN row still surfaces the same condition for a human to resolve by hand. Pair with MAIN_HEALTH_TICK — the withhold-a-lying-verdict half of HERD-452 protects main-health regardless of this key.

name: GATE_SCALE
description: Auto-scale REVIEW_CONCURRENCY / HEALTH_CONCURRENCY with the LIVE fleet size so an operator never hand-tunes concurrency as builders come and go (HERD-542): off (default, ship-dormant) | on (yolo posture adopts on). off -> _review_conc / _health_conc (agent-watch.sh) resolve exactly the configured values, byte-identical to before this key existed; herd_engine_live_tick (engine-version.sh) passes the Python engine core those SAME unscaled values it always has. on -> each watcher tick derives an EFFECTIVE cap per gate: clamp(configured_floor, ceil(live_builder_count / 2), cores_ceiling), where configured_floor is the value this key would resolve to with GATE_SCALE off (an explicit operator value is a FLOOR scaling never lowers), live_builder_count reuses the EXACT source herd-spawn-gate.sh's own spawn advisory reads (git worktrees under WORKTREES_DIR), and cores_ceiling is the box's logical core count (nproc / sysctl -n hw.ncpu; unreadable -> a built-in fallback). This is not console-only: herd_engine_live_tick passes the derived values as an explicit env override for that one Python tick, so GATE_SCALE actually moves the LIVE gate. Journals `gate_scale review=N health=M builders=K` once per change; the console renders the derived values with a 'scaled' qualifier. Unknown value -> off (fail safe)
when_to_surface: Turn on for a fleet whose builder count varies over a session (a coordinator spawning/retiring builders through the day) so review/health throughput tracks it without a manual REVIEW_CONCURRENCY/HEALTH_CONCURRENCY edit each time; leave off (default) for a fixed-size fleet or when an operator wants full manual control of both caps

name: tab-discipline.sh
description: THE RECONCILED TAB-DISCIPLINE SWEEP (HERD-569): herd_tab_discipline_sweep reconciles the OBSERVED workspace tab bar against the tabs the invariant allows and retires the rest. Operator directive 2026-08-05, verbatim: "there shouldn't be ANY other tabs spawned other than builders, or the scribe" — the tab bar is the operator's situational-awareness surface, so a tab that is neither a builder, the scribe, nor the control room is a defect. ALLOWED: (a) a $TREES/.herd-tabs row of kind `builder`; (b) a tab whose label is a live worktree directory in $WORKTREES_DIR (belt to (a)'s braces — the registry write is best-effort, and a builder whose row never landed must not be vaporised for the engine's own bookkeeping slip); (c) the scribe drainer's tab ($HERD_AGENT_SCRIBE); (d) the control room ($HERD_TAB_COORDINATOR) and this watcher's own $HERD_WATCHER_TAB_ID; (e) a `label` row in templates/tab-discipline-exempt.tsv. Everything else is retired through `herdr tab close` + a `tab_discipline_retired` journal event carrying the label and WHY (unregistered | kind:<k>), with any registry row it left behind pruned. Reconcile, not hook (docs/multi-seat-doctrine.md rule 1): it judges OBSERVED tabs, so it holds regardless of which seat, which build, or which hand-run script created the stray — the half a lint cannot cover. Because the action is CLOSING TABS, every missing input is a REFUSAL rather than a guess: an unresolvable workspace id (never sweep unscoped — the cross-project-kill lesson), an absent .herd-tabs (no way to tell a builder from a stray), an unreachable mux, dry-run, headless and a builder-worktree context (HERD-310 guard) all sweep NOTHING, byte-quiet; more than $HERD_TAB_DISCIPLINE_MAX (default 5) strays in one pass retires the cap's worth and journals tab_discipline_capped, so a bad read of the world is a slow visible drain rather than a one-tick wipe. Pure classifier form herd_tab_discipline_classify (tab-list JSON on stdin + env) used by the hermetic tests and provable against REAL tabs by the P2b real-panes scenario. Sourced by agent-watch.sh; runs on the orphan-sweep cadence (~60 s). Ship-dormant: TAB_DISCIPLINE=off (the default) is a HARD no-op — no herdr call, no journal line, no file read
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the ALLOWED TAB set changes (a new singleton role, a new registry kind, the exemption table's shape) or when a stray class needs a different disposition. Surface it when an operator asks why a tab vanished — or why one did NOT

name: tab-create-lint.sh
description: THE shared TAB-DISCIPLINE CREATION guard (HERD-569): herd_tab_create_lint [<root>] reds a `herdr … tab create` invocation (or a call to the driver's create-tab seam) in PRODUCTION engine code outside the modules the invariant allows — the builder lane (driver.sh, herd-feature.sh, herd-quick.sh), the scribe (scribe.sh) and the control room (coordinator.sh, bin/herd). Everything else splits a PANE inside the tab it belongs to. The build-time half of the invariant whose runtime half is scripts/herd/tab-discipline.sh: a lint cannot see a tab another seat's older build opened, and a sweep cannot tell a stray from a deliberate one, so both surfaces exist and read the SAME committed exemption table. Lines are normalized (quotes/commas to spaces) so one grammar covers the shell form and a python argv form alike; requiring the subcommand to follow `herdr` past any flags keeps English prose (herd-preflight.sh's help text names the command) out. scripts/herd/sim/, scripts/herd/experiment/ and tests/ stand up real tabs in DISPOSABLE workspaces and are classified FIXTURE — scanned, counted in the advisory, never flagged — so the distinction is asserted rather than an artifact of a non-recursive glob. A deliberate exception is a `callsite<TAB><path><TAB><reason>` row in templates/tab-discipline-exempt.tsv: the reason is MANDATORY (a bare row reds EXEMPT-MALFORMED rather than laundering a finding) and a row that no longer excuses anything reds STALE-EXEMPT (an exemption list that outlives what it excused is how a ratchet stops ratcheting). That file also carries the BASELINE — the lanes already creating tabs the day the guard landed, each naming the conversion that retires its row — so the guard ships GREEN and works as a no-new-tab-create ratchet from day one. Pure-function form herd_tab_create_check <file>... used by hermetic tests. Sourced (never executed) by BOTH scripts/herd/healthcheck.sh's light profile (the builder's pre-PR gate) and .herd/healthcheck.project.sh (the heavy/merge gate), so the two gates can never disagree. Fail-soft: the scan runs ONLY in a herdkit ENGINE tree — every consuming project is a SKIP with a reason in $HERD_TAB_CREATE_SKIP_REASON before a file is read. Exit 0 clean / 1 out-of-module / 2 skipped
when_to_surface: Internal library, sourced not launched; the seam to change when the tab-creation rule changes (the allowed-module set, the detection grammar, the fixture classification, or the exemption table). Surface it when a TAB-DISCIPLINE red needs explaining, or when asked what stops a new lane from spawning its own tab

name: TAB_DISCIPLINE
description: The TAB DISCIPLINE invariant as a RECONCILED SWEEP (HERD-569): on | report | off (default off, ship-dormant). Operator directive 2026-08-05, verbatim: "there shouldn't be ANY other tabs spawned other than builders, or the scribe". on -> on the orphan-sweep cadence (~60 s) the watcher enumerates THIS workspace's tabs and retires every one outside the allowed set (a registered `builder` row in $TREES/.herd-tabs, a tab whose label is a live worktree in $WORKTREES_DIR, the scribe's tab, the control room's tab or this watcher's own HERD_WATCHER_TAB_ID, or a `label` row in templates/tab-discipline-exempt.tsv), journaling tab_discipline_retired with the label and why and pruning any registry row left behind. report -> detect and journal tab_discipline_stray, closing NOTHING — the safe way to watch what a real control room would lose before arming it. off (default) -> a HARD no-op: no herdr call, no journal line, no file read. Every missing input is a REFUSAL rather than a guess (unresolvable workspace id, absent .herd-tabs, unreachable mux, dry-run, headless, builder-worktree context), and a runaway pass is capped at HERD_TAB_DISCIPLINE_MAX (5) with a journaled tab_discipline_capped. An unrecognized value reads off, so a typo can never arm a tab-closing path. The build-time sibling is scripts/herd/tab-create-lint.sh, which reds a NEW tab-create call site outside the builder-lane/scribe/control-room modules. Consumed by agent-watch.sh via tab-discipline.sh
when_to_surface: Set report first on a live control room to see which tabs the sweep would retire (journal only, nothing closed); set on once the list is what you expect and the tab bar should self-clean; leave off (default) for a byte-identical control room. Surface it when an operator complains the tab bar is full of tabs nobody asked for

name: OUTCOME_LEDGER
description: The OUTCOME LEDGER MVP (HERD-739, week-1 child of the Governance & Proof EPIC): off (default, ship-dormant) | on. on -> `herd ledger-report`, `herd intervene` and `herd sweep`'s leg 6 derive a per-tracker-ref VALUE record MECHANICALLY from the existing engine journal — no parallel bookkeeping path a builder must remember. Rows are built by joining `reconcile` (pr->ref, emitted on every merge), `merge`/`merge_observed` (when/what landed), `cost` (spend, builder/review split), `verdict_recorded` (review verdicts + BLOCK reasons) and any `*_bounce`-shaped refix event, plus two event families this feature is the SOLE producer of: `intervention` (a human touched the pipeline, taxonomy safety|product|infra-recovery|convenience) and `outcome_ledger_eval` (the delayed +24h/+7d re-evaluation the sweep leg fills — mechanically: reverted -> harmful, same-risk-class churn within the window -> neutral, else valuable). Disposition is honestly scoped to {accepted, reverted, unknown} — duplicate/abandoned would need a live tracker query this reader never makes, by design (offline + hermetic-test safe, zero network calls). off (default) -> every entry point refuses with one dormant line and writes NOTHING (no journal event, no file), mirroring AGENT_UPDATE's off posture; `herd sweep`'s own output is byte-identical (leg 6 is gated on this key BEFORE it execs the script, not only by the script's own refusal). Never sourced by agent-watch.sh and defines no per-tick behavior — the only automatic trigger is `herd sweep`'s leg 6, an on-demand CLI command. Consumed by scripts/herd/outcome-ledger.sh (its own bin/herd) and bin/herd's cmd_sweep leg 6.
when_to_surface: Set to on to start deriving per-item value records and enable `herd intervene`; leave off (default) for byte-identical behavior across ledger-report/intervene/sweep

name: herd ledger-report [--json | --alerts | --daily [--file PATH]]
description: The OUTCOME LEDGER reader (HERD-739): prints one line per tracker ref with disposition, spend (builder/review split, reusing cost.sh's journaled `cost` events), review verdict summary, refix-round count, risk class (core-surface/rails/docs/app, from a git diff of the first merge sha classified against CORE_SURFACE_GLOB) and the +24h/+7d evaluation status, followed by a loud alerts section (missing evaluations past due, reversions, value still unknown past +7d). --json prints the full derived model instead of the human summary. --alerts prints only the alerts section and exits 1 iff at least one fired (script-friendly). --daily [--file PATH] renders the same model as a markdown table and writes it into the worktree pool (default $WORKTREES_DIR/.herd/ledger-reports/<UTC date>.md, idempotent — a byte-identical rewrite is skipped). Pure dispatch to scripts/herd/outcome-ledger.sh. Ship-dormant behind OUTCOME_LEDGER=off (default): prints one dormant line and exits 0, no reads/writes beyond that
when_to_surface: After a merge, to see whether the item paid off — spend vs verdict vs later churn/reversion — or in a daily/weekly review; wire --alerts into a cron/watcher note to catch a missing +24h/+7d evaluation before it goes stale

name: herd intervene <ref> <safety|product|infra-recovery|convenience> "<note>"
description: Record one first-class OUTCOME LEDGER intervention (HERD-739): the coordinator/operator's entry point for "a human touched the pipeline for this tracker ref", classified by the fixed taxonomy — safety (a human stepped in to prevent harm), product (a judgment call the system could not make on its own — read as "the system failed to surface a decision"), infra-recovery (unwedging broken infra, not a build defect), convenience (a human did something the system could have done itself — counts AGAINST autonomy in the streak scorer). Journals one `intervention` event (ref/taxonomy/note/operator); refuses (exit 2) on an unknown taxonomy rather than journaling a value a reader would have to special-case forever. Pure dispatch to scripts/herd/outcome-ledger.sh. Ship-dormant behind OUTCOME_LEDGER=off (default): prints one dormant line and exits 0, no journal write
when_to_surface: Whenever an operator/coordinator manually intervenes in an otherwise-autonomous pipeline, so the streak scorer and `herd ledger-report` see WHY a human stepped in instead of the intervention going unrecorded
